text:
CONFIDENTIAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Flores Garcia
Date of Birth: April 12, 2021
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 4;6
Evaluation Dates: October 2, 2025 and October 6, 2025
Report Date: October 9, 2025
Medicaid ID: 987654321B
CDSA Case ID: CDSA-04471
Primary Language(s): Spanish and English (bilingual, Spanish-dominant at home)

Evaluator: Jennifer Suarez-Diaz, M.S., CCC-SLP, Bilingual Spanish-English Speech-Language Pathologist
Employer: Triad Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Clinic Address: 4420 Friendly Avenue, Suite 210, Greensboro, NC 27410
Clinic Phone: (336) 555-0148
Clinic Email: jsuarezdiaz@triadbilingualslp.com

Referral Source: Piedmont CDSA (Children's Developmental Services Agency), service coordinator Tom Whitfield ("Mr. Tom")
Interpreter Present: No (evaluator is bilingual and conducted the session directly in Spanish and English)

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Mateo is a 4-year-old boy referred for a comprehensive bilingual speech-language evaluation by his service coordinator at Piedmont CDSA, Mr. Tom, following a developmental screening completed as part of his annual IFSP review on September 18, 2025. Mateo's mother, Lucia Hernandez Flores, reported ongoing concerns about his limited expressive vocabulary in both Spanish and English, difficulty being understood by unfamiliar listeners, and frustration behaviors at home and at daycare. Mateo's daycare teacher, la maestra Carmen, also raised concerns through the daycare's monthly progress note, prompting this referral for further evaluation to determine eligibility for continued Part C early intervention services and to guide transition planning toward preschool special education services.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION

Background information was obtained through parent interview with Mateo's mother, Lucia Hernandez Flores, and father, Javier Flores Ramirez, who were both present for the intake portion of the evaluation on October 2, 2025. Records were also reviewed from Piedmont CDSA, including the most recent IFSP dated March 14, 2025, and from Mateo's pediatrician.

Birth and Medical History

Lucia reported that her pregnancy with Mateo was complicated by gestational hypertension, and that Mateo was born at 34 weeks gestation via emergency cesarean section at Wake Piedmont Regional Medical Center on April 12, 2021, weighing 4 pounds, 6 ounces. Mateo spent 21 days in the Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at Wake Piedmont Regional Medical Center, where he was treated for respiratory distress syndrome and mild jaundice. His attending neonatologist in the NICU was Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran, and his discharge was coordinated by Dr. Priya Chandrasekaran in consultation with Dr. Marcus Webb, pediatric pulmonology. Mateo passed his newborn hearing screening prior to NICU discharge and has had normal hearing screenings at each well-child visit since, most recently on August 11, 2025, per his pediatrician, Dr. Anita Reyes, at Greensboro Pediatric Associates.

Lucia reported no additional hospitalizations since the NICU stay, though Mateo had recurrent ear infections between 18 months and 3 years of age, treated with multiple rounds of antibiotics. He had bilateral pressure-equalization tubes placed at age 2;8 by Dr. Samuel Okafor, an ENT at Wake Piedmont Regional Medical Center's outpatient surgical center, and has had no further ear infections since that procedure. Javier reported a family history of late talking on his side of the family, noting that he himself did not begin combining words until close to age 3.

Developmental milestones were reported as generally delayed: Mateo sat independently at 9 months, walked at 17 months, and said his first words (in Spanish) around 22 months. Lucia stated that his vocabulary growth has remained slow and that he currently combines only a few two-word phrases in Spanish, with fewer still in English.

Family and Language History

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucia Hernandez Flores; his father, Javier Flores Ramirez; his older sister, Valentina Flores, age 6; and his younger brother, Diego Flores, age 1, at 118 Rosewood Court, Greensboro, NC 27406. Mateo's maternal grandmother, referred to in the home as doña Lupe, lives nearby and provides childcare three days a week while Lucia works. Lucia is employed part-time as a housekeeper at Carolina Inn & Suites, and Javier works full-time in landscaping for GreenScape Lawn & Tree Service. Mateo's maternal aunt, Rosa Hernandez, also assists with childcare on weekends and occasionally picks the children up from daycare.

The family's primary home language is Spanish. Lucia and Javier both report speaking almost exclusively Spanish with Mateo and his siblings at home, while doña Lupe speaks only Spanish. Valentina, who attends kindergarten at Fairview Elementary School, has become increasingly dominant in English and frequently code-switches with Mateo during play. The family reports watching Spanish-language children's programming at home and attending services at a Spanish-speaking church, where Mateo interacts with other children including his cousin Emilio and a family friend's son, Santiago.

The family has been connected with several community agencies since Mateo's NICU discharge. Lucia reported ongoing involvement with Guilford County WIC for nutritional support for Diego, and the family received home-visiting services through Guilford County Early Head Start when Mateo was an infant. The family was also briefly involved with Guilford County Department of Social Services (DSS) around Mateo's second birthday, following a referral related to housing instability; Lucia reported that case was closed without further action after the family secured stable housing with assistance from Guilford County Smart Start Partnership for Children. Mateo has received Part C early intervention services, including speech-language therapy and occupational therapy, coordinated through Piedmont CDSA since age 2;3, with Mr. Tom serving as his service coordinator for the past year.

Mateo currently attends Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare four days a week, where his primary teacher is la maestra Carmen and his assistant teacher is Miss Ana. la maestra Carmen reported that Mateo plays well with peers, including his frequent playmates Josue and Camila, but often resorts to pointing, gesturing, or pulling adults by the hand rather than using words when he wants something. The family's dog, Max, is frequently mentioned by Mateo during play and was referenced spontaneously during the evaluation session.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Mateo presented as a friendly, curious child who separated easily from his mother for the testing portion of the session. He demonstrated some initial shyness with this evaluator, Jennifer Suarez-Diaz, but warmed up quickly once rapport was established in Spanish. He engaged well with toys and picture-based tasks, though he showed brief frustration when unable to retrieve a word, occasionally vocalizing "no se" and looking to his mother for help. Attention and engagement were adequate for the full evaluation session, which lasted approximately 90 minutes across two visits. Oral-motor structures were judged to be within normal limits for speech production, with no evidence of dysarthria or apraxic features observed.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND RESULTS

The following standardized and informal measures were administered in both Spanish and English, as appropriate, to capture Mateo's full linguistic repertoire:

- Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA)
- Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition: Spanish (PLS-5 Spanish)
- Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3), administered in English with Spanish phonological analysis
- Spontaneous language sample (Spanish and English) analyzed using SALT conventions
- Parent/caregiver interview and clinical observation

Standardized Score Summary

Measure | Domain | Standard Score | Percentile Rank
BESA | Morphosyntax (Spanish) | 72 | 3rd
BESA | Morphosyntax (English) | 68 | 2nd
BESA | Semantics (Spanish) | 75 | 5th
BESA | Semantics (English) | 70 | 2nd
PLS-5 Spanish | Auditory Comprehension | 71 | 3rd
PLS-5 Spanish | Expressive Communication | 65 | 1st
GFTA-3 | Sounds-in-Words | 78 | 7th

Language Sample Analysis

A 50-utterance spontaneous language sample was collected in Spanish, yielding a mean length of utterance (MLU) of 2.1 morphemes, which falls well below age expectations. A parallel 30-utterance sample in English yielded an MLU of 1.6 morphemes. Across both samples, Mateo relied heavily on single-word utterances and two-word combinations (for example, "mas agua," "no quiero," "perro grande"), with limited use of grammatical morphemes such as plural markers and verb tense inflections in either language. SALT coding identified frequent use of the [EW] code for word-finding difficulty and reduced use of bound morphemes relative to same-age bilingual peers.

Articulation and Phonology

On the GFTA-3, Mateo demonstrated the following sound errors in English: final consonant deletion (for example, "bu" for "bus"), stopping of fricatives (for example, "tu" for "shoe," producing /t/ for /sh/), and gliding of liquids (for example, "wabbit" for "rabbit," [w] for /r/). In Spanish, similar patterns of final consonant deletion and gliding were observed, with the trilled /r/ consistently produced as [l], consistent with a phonological process pattern rather than an articulation disorder isolated to one language. Intelligibility was judged to be approximately 6/10 in known context and 3/10 to unfamiliar listeners, which is reduced for his age in both languages.

Receptive and Expressive Language

Mateo's receptive language skills, while also below age expectations, were relatively stronger than his expressive language skills across both languages, consistent with a receptive-expressive gap commonly seen in true language impairment rather than second-language acquisition alone. He followed one-step directions reliably (8/10 trials) but struggled with two-step directions involving spatial concepts (3/10 trials). Vocabulary knowledge, assessed informally through labeling and category tasks, was estimated to be below the 10th percentile in both languages when scores were considered individually, though his total conceptual vocabulary across both languages was somewhat stronger, suggesting that language exposure patterns alone do not fully account for his difficulties.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized testing, language sampling, parent and teacher report, and clinical observation, Mateo presents with a developmental language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, characterized by significantly reduced expressive vocabulary, limited morphosyntactic development, and a co-occurring phonological disorder affecting speech sound production in both languages. His pattern of errors and the gap between receptive and expressive skills, present across both languages rather than isolated to the language of lesser exposure, support a diagnosis of language disorder rather than a language difference attributable solely to bilingual development. His case is consistent with ICD-10 code F80.1 (expressive language disorder) and F80.0 (phonological disorder), and his presentation meets criteria under CPT code 92523 (evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression).

Mateo's reduced intelligibility and limited expressive language are likely contributing to the frustration behaviors reported by his mother, Lucia, and by la maestra Carmen at daycare. Continued delay in both languages, rather than a lag confined to his less-dominant language, supports continued eligibility for speech-language intervention services as he transitions from Part C to Part B services.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo is recommended for continued speech-language therapy services, ideally delivered bilingually or with a bilingual provider, at a frequency of two 30-minute sessions per week, targeting expressive vocabulary growth, morphosyntactic development (plural markers, verb tense), and phonological processes (final consonant deletion, stopping, gliding) in both Spanish and English.

2. It is recommended that Mateo's service coordinator, Mr. Tom at Piedmont CDSA, initiate transition planning toward Part B preschool special education services well in advance of Mateo's third birthday eligibility cutoff for Part C, given his continued need for services, and coordinate with Mateo's local school district to schedule an eligibility evaluation.

3. Continued coordination with Little Sprouts Bilingual Daycare staff, including la maestra Carmen and Miss Ana, is recommended to support consistent language-facilitation strategies across home, daycare, and therapy settings. A brief classroom consultation visit by this evaluator is recommended within the next two months.

4. Parent coaching is recommended to support Lucia and Javier in using expansion and modeling strategies at home in Spanish, their language of greatest comfort and fluency, to support vocabulary growth without discouraging continued exposure to English through Valentina and at daycare.

5. Given the family's history of involvement with Guilford County WIC, Guilford County Early Head Start, and Guilford County Smart Start Partnership for Children, continued communication among these agencies and Piedmont CDSA is recommended to ensure consistent support for the family as services transition.

6. A follow-up hearing screening is recommended at Mateo's next well-child visit with Dr. Anita Reyes to rule out any recurrence of middle-ear involvement, given his history of chronic ear infections and tube placement.

7. Re-evaluation of Mateo's speech and language skills is recommended in approximately 6 months, or sooner if significant concerns arise, to monitor progress and adjust the intervention plan as needed.

Thank you for the opportunity to evaluate Mateo. Please contact this evaluator with any questions regarding this report or recommendations.

Respectfully submitted,

Jennifer Suarez-Diaz, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Spanish-English Speech-Language Pathologist
Triad Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
4420 Friendly Avenue, Suite 210, Greensboro, NC 27410
Phone: (336) 555-0148
Email: jsuarezdiaz@triadbilingualslp.com

text:
Nombre del paciente: Jesús Emmanuel Domínguez Flores ("Chuy", "Chuyito")   Fecha de nacimiento: 14 de mayo de 2021   Edad actual: 4;9

Fecha de la evaluación: 3 de marzo de 2026   Número de expediente: LD-48219   Número de Medicaid: 987654321A

Evaluadora: Patricia Gómez-Hidalgo, MS, CCC-SLP   Clínica: Carolina Pediatric Therapy, PLLC   Teléfono: (919) 555-0148   Correo: pgomez@carolinapediatrictherapy.com

Dirección del paciente: 742 Oakwood Drive, Raleigh, NC 27610   Condado: Wake   Teléfono de contacto: (919) 555-2271

Padre: Roberto Domínguez Salinas   Madre: Fernanda Flores Castillo   Idioma del hogar: español e inglés

Escuela actual: Escuela Primaria Riverside Oaks   Maestra: Sra. Amanda Collins   Asistente de aula: Sra. Brenda Watts

Pediatra: Dr. Michael Chen   Coordinadora de servicios (CDSA): Ashley Brooks   Agencia: CDSA del Piedmont

Códigos de facturación de esta visita: CPT 92523, CPT 92507   Diagnóstico: F80.2

MOTIVO DE LA REMISIÓN

Jesús Emmanuel Domínguez Flores, conocido en casa y en la escuela como "Chuy" o cariñosamente "Chuyito", fue remitido para una evaluación integral del lenguaje y del habla a petición de su maestra, la Sra. Amanda Collins, y de su madre, Fernanda Flores Castillo. La familia reporta que Chuy es difícil de entender tanto en español como en inglés, que omite sonidos al final de las palabras y que a veces se frustra cuando sus compañeros de clase no le entienden. El pediatra, Dr. Michael Chen, también notó durante la visita de los 4 años, el 12 de febrero de 2026, que el habla de Chuy parecía estar por debajo de lo esperado para su edad y recomendó la evaluación con la Dra. Susan Patel, audióloga, antes de proceder.

HISTORIA PRENATAL Y DEL PARTO

Según refiere Fernanda Flores Castillo, el embarazo de Chuy fue de término completo, sin complicaciones mayores, aunque la madre tuvo náuseas intensas durante el primer trimestre. Chuy nació el 14 de mayo de 2021 en el WakeMed Children's Hospital, mediante parto vaginal, con un peso de 7 libras y 4 onzas. No requirió tiempo en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales. Los puntajes de Apgar fueron normales. La madre indica que no hubo ictericia prolongada ni otras complicaciones en el periodo neonatal inmediato.

HISTORIA MÉDICA

Chuy tuvo varias infecciones de oído entre los 8 meses y los 2 años de edad, con un total de seis episodios documentados de otitis media. Se le colocaron tubos de ventilación (miringotomía) el 9/18/2023 en el UNC Children's Hospital por el otorrinolaringólogo. Desde entonces, las infecciones han disminuido considerablemente, aunque tuvo un episodio leve en noviembre de 2025. La audición se evaluó más recientemente el 20 de febrero de 2026 por la Dra. Susan Patel, con resultados dentro de límites normales bilateralmente. No hay historial de convulsiones, hospitalizaciones significativas ni cirugías mayores. Chuy toma un multivitamínico diario y no tiene alergias conocidas a medicamentos. Su hermano menor, José Domínguez Flores, a quien la familia llama "Pepito", nació con un paladar hendido reparado quirúrgicamente, lo cual la madre menciona como antecedente familiar relevante para el desarrollo del habla.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LOS IDIOMAS

Chuy vive con sus padres, Roberto Domínguez Salinas y Fernanda Flores Castillo, su hermana mayor Guadalupe Domínguez Flores (apodada "Lupita", de 7 años) y su hermano menor José Domínguez Flores ("Pepito", de 2 años) en Raleigh. En el hogar se habla principalmente español; Fernanda Flores Castillo le habla a los niños casi exclusivamente en español, mientras que Roberto Domínguez Salinas alterna entre español e inglés dependiendo del contexto. Chuy comenzó a escuchar inglés de manera más consistente al entrar a Little Sprouts Daycare Center a los 18 meses de edad, y lo sigue escuchando ahora en la Escuela Primaria Riverside Oaks.

La abuela materna, Rosa María Castillo Vega, cuida a los niños con frecuencia después de la escuela y les habla únicamente en español. La familia también cuenta con el apoyo de una niñera, Carmen Yolanda Pérez Nava, quien recoge a Chuy y a Lupita de la escuela los martes y jueves y los cuida hasta que Fernanda Flores Castillo regresa del trabajo. Según Carmen Yolanda Pérez Nava, Chuy se comunica mejor cuando está relajado y jugando con el perro de la familia, un labrador llamado Rocky, que cuando intenta hablar con adultos desconocidos.

Los primos de Chuy, Ana Sofía Reyes Luna y Diego Alejandro Reyes Luna, visitan casi todos los fines de semana, y la madre reporta que Chuy juega bien con ellos, aunque a veces Ana Sofía Reyes Luna, que es mayor, termina "traduciendo" lo que dice Chuy para que los adultos entiendan.

Antes de la evaluación actual, Chuy recibió servicios de intervención temprana a través del CDSA del Piedmont desde los 2;6 hasta los 3 años, bajo un Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) firmado el 15 de noviembre de 2023 y revisado por última vez el 3/1/2024. La terapeuta del habla en ese entonces fue Laura Jiménez, quien documentó un retraso leve en el vocabulario expresivo en español. Chuy fue dado de alta de esos servicios al cumplir 3 años y transferido al sistema escolar.

HISTORIA EDUCATIVA

Chuy asiste actualmente al salón de pre-kínder de la Sra. Amanda Collins en la Escuela Primaria Riverside Oaks, de lunes a viernes de 8:00 a.m. a 2:30 p.m. La maestra asistente, Sra. Brenda Watts, también trabaja con él en pequeños grupos de lenguaje dos veces por semana. Según el reporte de progreso del el martes 4 de junio de 2025, Chuy participa con entusiasmo en las actividades grupales pero evita hablar frente a toda la clase. Sus compañeros de clase, Mateo Vásquez Lira (a quien llaman "Teo") y Juan Carlos Rivas Molina ("Juanito"), suelen jugar con él en el área de bloques y en el recreo. Otra compañera, Isabella Moreno, se sienta junto a él durante el círculo de lectura. La Sra. Amanda Collins reporta que Chuy a veces se queda calla do cuando Teo y Juanito le hacen preguntas directas, y que prefiere señalar o usar gestos en lugar de responder verbalmente frente al grupo.

OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES Y DE LA SESIÓN

La evaluación se llevó a cabo el 3 de marzo de 2026 de 10:00 a.m. a 12:15 p.m. en las oficinas de Carolina Pediatric Therapy, PLLC, ubicadas en 118 Lakeview Parkway, Suite 220, Raleigh. Fernanda Flores Castillo estuvo presente durante toda la sesión y ayudó a interpretar algunas respuestas de Chuy cuando él hablaba muy bajo. Chuy se mostró inicialmente tímido, pero se relajó después de los primeros 15 minutos de juego libre con bloques y figuras de animales. Mantuvo buen contacto visual, siguió instrucciones de dos pasos sin dificultad y demostró buena atención conjunta durante las actividades estructuradas. No se observaron conductas repetitivas ni dificultades sensoriales significativas.

Durante la conversación espontánea, Chuy produjo enunciados de 4 a 6 palabras tanto en español como en inglés, aunque mezclaba ambos idiomas con frecuencia (code-switching), lo cual es esperado y apropiado en niños bilingües de su edad y no se consideró un indicador de trastorno del lenguaje por sí solo.

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS ESTANDARIZADAS

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas en español e inglés, según corresponda, con apoyo de materiales bilingües:

Prueba                                          Dominio                           Puntaje estándar   Percentil
Preschool Language Scale-5 Español              Lenguaje receptivo                72                 3
Preschool Language Scale-5 Español              Lenguaje expresivo                68                 2
Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA)     Morfosintaxis (español)           7 (escala 1-10)    16
Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA)     Morfosintaxis (inglés)            6 (escala 1-10)    9
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3          Articulación (inglés)             71                 3
Prueba de fonología en español (lista informal) Articulación (español)            No estandarizado   N/A

En la prueba de articulación en español, Chuy obtuvo 8/10 en la producción de palabras con /s/ inicial, pero solo 4/10 en palabras con consonantes finales, omitiendo consistentemente los sonidos /s/, /n/ y /r/ al final de la palabra (por ejemplo, produjo "pa" para "pan" y "do" para "dos"). En inglés, logró el 80% de precisión en palabras monosilábicas con estructura CV pero solo el 30% de precisión en palabras con grupos consonánticos iniciales como /pl/ y /st/, simplificando "stop" a "top" y "play" a "pay".

Durante la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo, transcrita y analizada con el sistema SALT, se codificaron 42 enunciados; 11 de ellos mostraron errores gramaticales marcados con el código [EW] (omisión de palabra esperada), principalmente omisión del artículo definido en inglés y del pronombre clítico en español (por ejemplo, "quiero" en lugar de "lo quiero").

En cuanto a la inteligibilidad, los padres calificaron el habla de Chuy como comprensible aproximadamente el 60% del tiempo para oyentes desconocidos, y un examinador no familiarizado con el niño reportó una inteligibilidad similar durante la sesión. Con claves moderadas (mod cues) de imitación y modelado, Chuy pudo producir correctamente el fonema /r/ en posición inicial en el 70% de los intentos, lo cual sugiere buen potencial de estimulabilidad.

El rango de movimiento oral-motor fue adecuado; no se observaron signos de apraxia del habla infantil ni de disartria. La estructura oral (labios, lengua, paladar, dentición) se encontró dentro de límites normales para la edad.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

Con base en los resultados obtenidos, Chuy presenta un trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo (F80.2) junto con un trastorno de los sonidos del habla, evidente tanto en español como en inglés, lo cual confirma que las dificultades no se deben únicamente a la exposición bilingüe sino a un patrón consistente de retraso en ambos idiomas. Las omisiones de consonantes finales y la simplificación de grupos consonánticos son consistentes con un retraso fonológico, más que con un trastorno motor del habla. Los errores gramaticales observados, incluyendo las omisiones marcadas como [EW], son mayores de lo esperado para un niño bilingüe secuencial de 4;9 de edad expuesto al español desde el nacimiento y al inglés desde los 18 meses.

Es importante notar que Chuy muestra fortalezas relativas en la comprensión de vocabulario concreto, en el seguimiento de instrucciones de dos pasos y en la atención conjunta, lo cual son factores protectores favorables para el pronóstico. El antecedente de otitis media recurrente con tubos de ventilación también pudo haber contribuido al retraso fonológico durante un periodo crítico del desarrollo del lenguaje, aunque la audición actual es normal según la Dra. Susan Patel.

RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda terapia de lenguaje y habla individual, bilingüe (español e inglés), dos veces por semana, sesiones de 30 minutos, bajo los códigos CPT 92507 para tratamiento continuo, utilizando el código CPT 92523 para la evaluación combinada de habla y lenguaje ya facturada en esta visita.

2. Continuar la colaboración con la Sra. Amanda Collins y la Sra. Brenda Watts para reforzar objetivos de lenguaje dentro del aula, particularmente durante las actividades de grupo pequeño ya establecidas.

3. Referir a evaluación con terapia ocupacional con Jennifer Lee, OTR/L, para descartar dificultades asociadas de coordinación motora fina que pudieran afectar el rendimiento preacadémico, según lo observado de manera informal durante la sesión.

4. Solicitar una nueva revisión de IFSP o plan educativo individualizado (IEP) a través de la Escuela Primaria Riverside Oaks, con reunión propuesta para el 28 de abril de 2026, a las 1:00 p.m.

5. Se sugiere que la familia continúe exponiendo a Chuy a ambos idiomas de manera consistente, sin eliminar el español del hogar, ya que mantener el idioma del hogar favorece el desarrollo bilingüe saludable y el vínculo con la abuela Rosa María Castillo Vega y los primos Ana Sofía Reyes Luna y Diego Alejandro Reyes Luna.

6. Reevaluación formal en 6 meses, aproximadamente para septiembre de 2026, para medir el progreso en inteligibilidad y en morfosintaxis en ambos idiomas.

7. Continuar seguimiento audiológico anual con la Dra. Susan Patel dado el historial de otitis media recurrente.

8. Coordinar con Ashley Brooks del CDSA del Piedmont la posible reactivación de servicios de apoyo familiar, dado que Chuy ya fue dado de alta de intervención temprana pero podría beneficiarse de recursos adicionales en el hogar.

PLAN DE TRATAMIENTO

Se iniciará terapia en las oficinas de Carolina Pediatric Therapy, PLLC a partir del 17 de marzo de 2026, con sesiones los martes a las 3:30 p.m. y los jueves a las 4:00 p.m. Los objetivos iniciales incluirán: (a) producción correcta de consonantes finales /s/, /n/ en palabras monosilábicas en español con 80% de precisión en tres sesiones consecutivas; (b) reducción de la simplificación de grupos consonánticos iniciales en inglés; y (c) uso correcto del artículo definido y del pronombre clítico en enunciados espontáneos, reduciendo la frecuencia de omisiones tipo [EW] observadas en la muestra SALT.

Se solicitará autorización de Medicaid bajo el número 987654321A para doce sesiones iniciales de terapia bajo el código CPT 92507, con reevaluación de autorización programada para 9/15/2026.

Esta evaluadora está disponible para discutir estos hallazgos con el equipo escolar, el pediatra Dr. Michael Chen, o con la coordinadora de servicios Ashley Brooks en cualquier momento. Se agradece a la familia Domínguez Salinas-Flores Castillo por su colaboración durante todo el proceso de evaluación.

Atentamente,

Patricia Gómez-Hidalgo, MS, CCC-SLP
Patóloga del Habla-Lenguaje Bilingüe
Carolina Pediatric Therapy, PLLC

text:
CONFIDENTIAL — SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
4820 Monroe Road, Suite 210, Charlotte, NC 28205
Phone: (704) 555-0148  |  Fax: (704) 555-0149

Child's Name: Maria Jose Hernandez Lopez (called "Majo" at home)
Date of Birth: June 14, 2022
Chronological Age at Evaluation: 3;4
Record ID: LD-48217
Medicaid ID: 902847561B
Evaluation Dates: October 2, 2025 and October 9, 2025
Report Date: October 15, 2025
Parents/Guardians: Lucia Lopez Ramirez (mother), Jose Hernandez Castillo (father)
Home Address: 118 Sycamore Hollow Lane, Charlotte, NC 28216
Home Phone: 704-555-9271
Mother's Cell: (704) 555-3087
Father's Cell: 704.555.6642
Primary Home Language: Spanish, with English also used
Referral Source: Mecklenburg County CDSA, Service Coordinator Monica Reyes (704-555-1120)
Evaluator: Rachel Kim, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual Spanish-English clinician

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Majo was referred for a bilingual speech-language evaluation by Mecklenburg County CDSA following a routine developmental screening at Little Learners Bilingual Academy, where her teacher, Miss Ana, raised concerns that Majo's speech was difficult for unfamiliar listeners to understand in both Spanish and English, and that she used shorter sentences than her classmates. Her mother, Lucia Lopez Ramirez, echoed similar concerns, noting that extended family members, including Majo's grandmother, doña Lupe, who speaks with her by phone and video call, often ask Lucia to repeat what Majo has said. Majo currently attends Little Learners Bilingual Academy four days a week, where Spanish literacy instruction is provided twice weekly by la maestra Carmen. No prior speech-language services have been provided, and this is Majo's first formal evaluation of any kind.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

According to Lucia Lopez Ramirez, Majo was born at 35 weeks gestation at Piedmont Regional Medical Center in Charlotte on June 14, 2022, following a pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia. Birth weight was 4 lb 11 oz. Majo was admitted to the Level III NICU at Piedmont Regional Medical Center for 18 days for respiratory support and feeding difficulties. Her attending neonatologist during that admission was Dr. Samantha Osei, and her ongoing care was later transferred to her pediatrician, Dr. Hector Flores, for well-child visits. Lucia reported that Majo had several episodes of otitis media between ages 1 and 2, treated with antibiotics, and underwent placement of bilateral pressure-equalization tubes on March 3, 2024, performed by otolaryngologist Dr. Priya Nair. Hearing was last screened on September 20, 2025 by audiology, with results within normal limits bilaterally. No history of seizures, head injury, or significant illness was reported. Majo currently has no diagnosed medical conditions outside of her resolved history of ear infections and takes no daily medications. Her most recent well-child visit with Dr. Flores was on August 11, 2025, at which growth and vision were documented as age-appropriate.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Majo lives with her parents, Lucia Lopez Ramirez and Jose Hernandez Castillo, and her older brother, Diego Hernandez Lopez (age 7), in Charlotte. The family also shares their home with a dog named Luna, of whom Majo is reportedly very fond and frequently talks about. Jose works in construction for Blue Ridge Construction, and Lucia works part time as a certified nursing assistant for Atrium Senior Living. Both parents report that Spanish is the primary language spoken in the home, though English is increasingly used by Diego, who is in the second grade at Sunview Elementary School and is becoming more English-dominant. Lucia estimates that Majo hears approximately 70% Spanish and 30% English in a typical week, with English exposure coming mainly from Diego, television, and daycare.

Majo's maternal grandmother, doña Lupe, lives in Guadalajara and speaks with Majo by video call several times a week; the family can be reached at her number, +52 33 4455 6789, for coordination when she visits. A paternal aunt, Patricia Hernandez Castillo, lives nearby in Concord and frequently babysits Majo and Diego on weekends, speaking to them primarily in Spanish. Lucia reported that Majo's early language milestones were somewhat delayed relative to Diego's: she said her first words around 18 months and began combining two words close to her second birthday, later than Diego, who combined words by 16 months. Lucia denied any family history of hearing loss but noted that Majo's father, Jose, was "a late talker" as a child, per his own mother's report.

At Little Learners Bilingual Academy, Majo is in a mixed-age classroom with her teacher, Miss Ana, and assistant teacher Miss Brenda. Miss Ana reports that Majo enjoys playing with her classmate, Sofia, during free play but becomes frustrated and sometimes cries when peers do not understand her requests. The daycare's bus driver, Mr. Tom, also commented to Lucia at pickup that Majo "talks like a baby" compared to other three-year-olds he transports, which prompted Lucia to raise the concern with Miss Ana and ultimately pursue this evaluation.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

Majo presented as a friendly, socially engaged child who separated from her mother without difficulty for both sessions, held on October 2, 2025 and October 9, 2025 at the clinic offices on Monroe Road. She demonstrated adequate attention for structured tasks of 15 to 20 minutes with brief breaks, and she transitioned between Spanish and English testing materials without apparent distress, though her speech was judged to be moderately to severely unintelligible to this examiner on first listen, improving somewhat with context and repetition. Oral-motor structures were judged grossly within normal limits for structure and function, with adequate range of motion for the lips, tongue, and jaw observed during imitative and spontaneous speech tasks. Hearing could not be formally retested given the recent normal screening result on file.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND RESULTS

The following standardized and informal measures were administered in both Spanish and English as appropriate to assess Majo's receptive language, expressive language, and speech sound production.

STANDARDIZED TEST RESULTS

Measure                                                        Score         Percentile
Preschool Language Scale-5, Spanish (PLS-5 Spanish)
   Auditory Comprehension                                      SS 76         5th
   Expressive Communication                                    SS 71         3rd
   Total Language Score                                        SS 72         3rd
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), English
   Sounds-in-Words                                             SS 68         2nd
Bilingual English Spanish Assessment (BESA)
   Morphosyntax, Spanish                                       within normal limits for age
   Morphosyntax, English                                       below average range

Informal measures (100-utterance spontaneous language sample, Spanish):
   Percentage of Consonants Correct (PCC): 58%
   Mean Length of Utterance in morphemes (MLU-m): 3.1, below the expected range of 4.0 to 4.5 for her age
   Intelligibility in context, unfamiliar listeners: approximately 40%
   Intelligibility in context, familiar listeners: approximately 70%

Error pattern analysis of the Spanish and English samples revealed frequent final consonant deletion (for example, "pan" produced as "pa"), stopping of fricatives (for example, "casa" produced as "cata"), and cluster reduction (for example, "plato" produced as "pato"). In English, Majo substituted /w/ for /r/ in words such as "wabbit" for "rabbit" and showed liquid gliding consistent with typical developmental patterns, though it is persisting beyond the age at which it is usually expected to resolve. One sample utterance, "quiero jugo" [EW], was coded during the Spanish sample to reflect an early-word reduction. Stimulability testing showed that Majo could produce /s/ in isolation and in "casa" with mod cues, correcting to "casa" on 6/10 trials with modeling, suggesting a favorable prognosis for this sound with direct intervention.

CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on today's assessment, Majo presents with a speech sound disorder and an expressive-receptive language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with a primary language and speech impairment rather than a pattern attributable to typical bilingual development alone. Her scores fall well below expectations in both languages assessed, and her phonological error patterns in Spanish mirror those observed in English, which argues against normal cross-linguistic transfer as the sole explanation for her presentation. Her reported history of chronic otitis media with effusion during a developmentally sensitive period for speech and language acquisition, along with her NICU course following preterm birth, are considered possible contributing factors, although her most recent hearing screening is within normal limits. Given her current language exposure of roughly 70% Spanish, intervention should be delivered primarily in Spanish, with ongoing attention to cross-linguistic skills as her English exposure continues to increase through her brother, Diego Hernandez Lopez, and her daycare environment. Majo's strong stimulability for several error sounds and her engaged, social presentation during testing are favorable prognostic indicators.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Individual speech-language therapy, twice weekly, in 30- to 45-minute sessions, delivered primarily in Spanish with English support as needed, at Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC.
2. Referral to audiology for a repeat comprehensive hearing evaluation given the history of chronic otitis media, through Dr. Priya Nair's office, 704-555-7734.
3. Continued coordination with Mecklenburg County CDSA Service Coordinator Monica Reyes regarding preschool special education eligibility prior to Majo's next birthday.
4. A structured home language program, with parents Lucia Lopez Ramirez and Jose Hernandez Castillo encouraged to continue rich Spanish language exposure, including narrating daily routines and expanding Majo's utterances rather than correcting them directly.
5. Coordination with daycare staff, Miss Ana and la maestra Carmen, to reinforce target sounds and vocabulary during the school day, and to reduce peer frustration through modeling and repetition with classmates such as Sofia.
6. Re-evaluation recommended in 6 months, or sooner if progress plateaus, to reassess standard scores and update the plan of care.

A follow-up re-evaluation has been tentatively scheduled for April 15, 2026 at 10:00 AM. The family may contact this office with questions at (704) 555-0148 or by email at rkim@carolinabilingualslp.com.

Thank you for the opportunity to evaluate Majo. Please do not hesitate to contact this office with any questions regarding these findings.

Respectfully submitted,

Rachel Kim, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC

PROGRAMA INFANTIL-PREESCOLAR DE CAROLINA DEL NORTE (NC ITP)
PLAN DE SERVICIO FAMILIAR INDIVIDUALIZADO (IFSP) — REVISIÓN DE 6 MESES

INFORMACIÓN DE LA FAMILIA

CG principal: Lucía Esperanza Rodríguez Paz, madre de Teo. Lucía Rodríguez trabaja de noche en el almacén de distribución de Harris Teeter en Hope Mills, turno de 11:00 PM a 7:00 AM, de domingo a jueves. Domicilio actual de la familia: 1420 Rosewood Court, Fayetteville, Condado de Cumberland, NC, 28314. Tel. de contacto: (910) 555-2184 (celular de mamá). La familia reporta que este es el 2do domicilio desde la mudanza de Hope Mills hace aprox 8 meses.

Los primos de Teo, Diego y Valentina (hijos de la hermana de Lucía), visitan casi cada fin de semana desde Hope Mills y juegan c/ Teo en el patio trasero.

Hermana mayor: Camila Fernández Rodríguez, edad 5;11, en kinder en Montclair Elementary. Camila habla inglés y español y a veces interpreta frases cortas de Teo para la familia. El vecino J. Ortiz a veces recoge a Camila de la parada del autobús cuando mamá está dormida después del turno de noche.

Mascota de la familia: perro llamado Rocky, un labrador mezclado; Teo señala a Rocky y produce aprox. de la palabra "perro" como [peo].

COORDINADOR(A) DE SERVICIOS / OFICINA CDSA

Coordinadora de Servicios: Michelle Owens, de la oficina CDSA del Sureste de Carolina del Norte, ubicada en Fayetteville. Tel: (910) 555-7740, ext. 212. Email: m.owens@cdsa-se.nc.gov. Michelle Owens coordinó la última revisión semestral y continúa como punto de contacto principal de la familia para asuntos de elegibilidad y servicios.

Terapeuta del habla y lenguaje (SLP) que redacta esta nota: Patricia Gómez, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingüe, contratada a través de Terapias Pediátricas Bilingües de Carolina, PLLC. Email de contacto: pgomez@tpbcarolina.com. Visitas quincenales en el hogar, sesiones de 45 min.

Otros proveedores en el equipo: pediatra Dr. Alan Kim en Cape Fear Valley Pediatrics; terapeuta ocupacional Brenda Sosa, quien ve a Teo mensualmente para integración sensorial.

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA (en palabras de la familia)

Lucía Rodríguez reporta: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Teo no me dice lo que quiere, solo llora o me jala la ropa. En la guardería dicen que se frustra mucho con los otros niños porque no puede pedir las cosas." También comenta: "A veces repite lo que uno dice, como un eco, pero no sale de él mismo. Quiero que aprenda a usar sus propias palabras en español y en inglés, los dos, porque en la casa hablamos español pero en la guardería todo es inglés."

José Fernández agrega, a través de interpretación de Lucía durante la llamada telefónica: "Yo casi no estoy en la casa por el trabajo, pero cuando estoy, noto que Teo se enoja rápido cuando no lo entendemos. Queremos que hable más claro."

Prioridades identificadas por la familia para esta revisión:
1. Que Teo use palabras funcionales (no solo gestos/llanto) p/ pedir comida, agua y juguetes, en ambos idiomas.
2. Reducir las rabietas relacionadas a la frustración comunicativa, especialmente en Sunshine Kids Daycare.
3. Seguir recibiendo visitas en el hogar en lugar de clínica, por el horario de trabajo de Lucía Rodríguez.
4. Apoyo para que Camila no tenga que cargar tanta responsabilidad de "traducir" a su hermano.

RUTINAS DIARIAS

Mañana: Lucía Rodríguez llega de su turno aprox 7:15 AM, despierta a Teo y a Camila p/ llevarlos a la guardería y a la escuela. Teo asiste a Sunshine Kids Daycare de 8:00 AM a 3:30 PM, de lunes a viernes. Su maestra principal es Karen Díaz, quien reporta que Teo se frustra durante el círculo y la hora de juego libre c/ sus compañeros Liam y Sofía, a veces empujando cuando quiere un juguete que otro niño tiene.

Tarde/noche: Rosa Elena Martínez, la niñera, llega aprox 5:30 PM y se queda hasta que Lucía Rodríguez sale p/ su turno a las 10:30 PM. Durante esta ventana, Rosa prepara la cena, baña a los niños, y sigue el "plan de lenguaje" que Patricia Gómez le dejó por escrito: nombrar objetos, esperar 5 segundos antes de dar el ítem, y modelar frases de 2 palabras ("quiero agua", "más galleta"). Rosa reporta mejoría leve: Teo ahora dice "ma" p/ pedir más, de forma consistente.

Fines de semana: la familia pasa tiempo c/ los primos Diego y Valentina, y José Fernández suele estar en casa si no viaja por trabajo. Teo disfruta jugar afuera c/ Rocky y los primos; produce aprox. "wawa" p/ agua y señala mucho.

OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS

- Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Cumberland (DSS): la familia recibe asistencia de SNAP; trabajadora de caso D. Alvarado revisó elegibilidad en 15 de agosto de 2026.
- WIC de Cumberland County: seguimiento nutricional mensual; Lucía Rodríguez reporta que a Teo le cuesta transicionar de comidas coladas a sólidas, lo cual se correlaciona c/ las metas motoras orales de este plan.
- Smart Start del Condado de Cumberland: ofreció un cupo de guardería subvencionado que permitió el cambio de Teo a Sunshine Kids Daycare en julio de 2026.
- Oficina CDSA (CDSA del Sureste de Carolina del Norte): revisión de elegibilidad continua, coordinada por Michelle Owens.

EVALUACIÓN DE SEGUIMIENTO (resumen)

Se administró el Preschool Language Scale-5 Spanish (PLS-5 Spanish) en 2 de octubre de 2026. Puntuación estándar en Lenguaje Auditivo: 70 (percentil 2); Lenguaje Expresivo: 65 (percentil 1); Puntuación Total de Lenguaje: 67. Edad equivalente aprox 1;6, c/ edad cronológica de 2;9 — retraso significativo consistente c/ el patrón observado en la visita inicial.

Muestra de lenguaje espontáneo (15 min, hogar): Teo produjo 8 palabras diferentes; TTR bajo p/ la edad. Ejemplos de producción: dice "aba" p/ "agua" [awa], "nene" p/ "nene/bebé", y "no" de forma clara y funcional. Imita "mamá" y "papá" c/ mod cues pero no los usa espontáneamente fuera de la imitación inmediata. Ecolalia inmediata observada en 4/10 intentos de modelado (repite la última palabra del adulto sin intención comunicativa clara).

Inventario fonético limitado a /m, p, n, a, o/ aprox.; ausencia de /t, k, s/ en ambos idiomas. Praxis oral: dentro de límites normales según Brenda Sosa (OT) en su última nota.

RESULTADOS (OUTCOMES) CON ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: Teo usará mín. 10 palabras funcionales nuevas (combinando español e inglés) p/ pedir, protestar o comentar, de forma espontánea en el hogar y en Sunshine Kids Daycare, en 6 meses.
Estrategias: entrenamiento de CG (mamá y niñera Rosa Elena Martínez) en espera estructurada ("time delay") y modelado de frases cortas; uso de tablero de comunicación c/ imágenes bilingües en la mochila y en casa; colaboración c/ Karen Díaz p/ reforzar las mismas palabras-meta durante el día en la guardería.

Resultado 2: Reducir la frecuencia de conductas de frustración (empujar, llorar prolongado) de un promedio reportado de 6-8x/día a menos de 3x/día, medido por registro de CG.
Estrategias: enseñar 2-3 señas simples (más, terminado, ayuda) como puente mientras se desarrolla el lenguaje verbal; reforzar intentos comunicativos de inmediato c/ respuesta natural; Karen Díaz usará el mismo sistema de señas en el aula.

Resultado 3: Aumentar el inventario fonético funcional incluyendo aprox. de /t/ y /k/ en posición inicial, en al menos 3 palabras c/ mod cues.
Estrategias: práctica de imitación motora oral; juegos de sonidos c/ los primos Diego y Valentina durante visitas de fin de semana, ya que la familia reporta que Teo está más motivado socialmente en ese contexto.

Resultado 4: Apoyar a Camila para que no funcione como "interprete principal", redirigiendo a Teo hacia CG adultos p/ comunicación, y dándole a Camila un rol de "modelo de juego" en lugar de traductora.
Estrategias: Patricia Gómez modelará actividades de juego paralelo entre Camila y Teo donde Camila expande (no traduce) los intentos de su hermano.

FRECUENCIA Y LUGAR DE SERVICIOS

Terapia de habla-lenguaje: 2x/semana, 45 min c/ sesión, en el hogar (1420 Rosewood Court, Fayetteville), proveída por Patricia Gómez a través de Terapias Pediátricas Bilingües de Carolina, PLLC.
Terapia ocupacional: 1x/mes, 30 min, en el hogar, proveída por Brenda Sosa.
Coordinación de servicios: revisión semestral y contacto telefónico según necesidad, por Michelle Owens, CDSA del Sureste de Carolina del Norte.

FECHAS DE SERVICIO Y PRÓXIMOS PASOS

- Próxima revisión semestral del IFSP: 9 de abril de 2027.
- Próxima evaluación formal (PLS-5 Spanish, repetición): aprox marzo de 2027.
- Fecha límite de transición (evaluación de elegibilidad para preescolar, b/c Teo cumple 3 años): aprox enero de 2027, c/ reunión de transición programada p/ 15 de noviembre de 2026 c/ el equipo de preescolar del distrito.
- Envío de nota de progreso firmada a CDSA del Sureste de Carolina del Norte: a más tardar 17 de octubre de 2026.

FIRMAS

Madre: Lucía Esperanza Rodríguez Paz — fecha de firma: 10 de octubre de 2026.
Coordinadora de Servicios: Michelle Owens — fecha de firma: 10 de octubre de 2026.
SLP: Patricia Gómez, M.S., CCC-SLP — fecha de firma: 10 de octubre de 2026.

Nota final de la terapeuta: Esta revisión se completó c/ la madre, Lucía Rodríguez, presente de manera presencial, y el padre, José Fernández, participando por teléfono desde su sitio de trabajo. La familia expresó alivio al saber que Teo ("Teo") sigue calificando p/ servicios continuos bajo Part C, y pidió que se consideren horarios de tarde p/ las próximas sesiones, ya que Rosa Elena Martínez a veces tiene conflictos de horario c/ su otro trabajo de medio tiempo. Se discutió también la posibilidad de trasladar algunas sesiones a Sunshine Kids Daycare p/ generalizar las estrategias c/ Karen Díaz y los compañeros Liam y Sofía presentes, pendiente de aprobación por parte de la directora del centro y de CDSA del Sureste de Carolina del Norte.

Nota de sesión diaria – 10 de octubre de 2026

Paciente: Mateíto (también conocido como Mateo Álvarez), edad 4;2. Proveedor: Patricia Núñez, patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe, Carolina Bilingual Speech Services. Sesión realizada en el hogar de la familia en 214 Willow Bend Court, Cary, Carolina del Norte 27518, de 3:30 p.m. a 4:15 p.m..

Al llegar, yo saludé a Mateíto y a su mamá, Rosa Álvarez, quien estaba terminando una llamada con la coordinadora de servicios de CDSA de la Región del Piedmont, Diana Flores. La hermana mayor de Mateíto, Sol Álvarez, de ocho años, estaba en la sala haciendo la tarea después de llegar de Highcroft Elementary; su presencia ayudó porque Mateíto a veces imita el habla de Sol cuando se siente inseguro.

La sesión comenzó a las 3:30 con juego estructurado usando bloques y figuras de animales para trabajar los fonemas /k/ y /g/ en posición inicial. Mateíto produjo "gato" como "dato" en 6 de 10 ensayos con señal mod cues, mejorando a 8/10 hacia el final del bloque. También trabajamos el fonema /s/ en grupos consonánticos; produjo la palabra meta "estrella" correctamente en 7/10 intentos. Se usó el código SALT [EW] para marcar una expansión espontánea cuando dijo "yo quiero más" sin ayuda.

A las 3:50 hicimos una pausa breve para merendar. Rosa mencionó que el perro de la familia, Capitán, ha estado ladrando mucho durante las sesiones de video con la maestra de intervención temprana, Brenda Castillo, de Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, y que eso distrae a Mateíto. Se sugirió mantener a Capitán en otra habitación durante las llamadas.

Continuamos con un segundo bloque de 3:55 a 4:10, enfocado en seguimiento de instrucciones de dos pasos y vocabulario de acciones. Mateíto siguió instrucciones correctamente en 4/5 ensayos sin apoyo visual. También practicamos saludos sociales con un compañero imaginario llamado "Max" usando un muñeco, ya que Rosa reportó que Mateíto ha tenido dificultad iniciando interacciones con su compañero de clase Liam Jennings en el programa de intervención temprana.

Antes de terminar, hablamos sobre la próxima evaluación de IFSP, programada para el 14 de noviembre de 2026, y confirmamos que el padre de Mateíto, Esteban Álvarez, intentará asistir vía videollamada desde su trabajo en Piedmont Furniture Manufacturing. Rosa pidió que le enviáramos el enlace de la reunión al correo rosa.alvarez82@gmail.com y preguntó de nuevo por los recursos bilingües en el sitio web de la agencia, www.piedmontcdsa.org/recursos-bilingues.

La sesión terminó a las 4:15 p.m.. Plan: continuar con metas fonológicas para /k/, /g/ y grupos consonánticos con /s/, incorporar juego social con pares, y coordinar con Brenda Castillo sobre estrategias en el aula. Número de caso Medicaid de Mateíto: 784512093B. Próxima cita programada para el 17 de octubre de 2026 a las 3:30 p.m.. Contacto de la clínica para dudas: (919) 555-0148.

La madre, Marisol, expresó: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Santi todavía no me dice lo que quiere. Señala las cosas o llora, pero no tiene palabras. Su hermana a su edad ya hablaba mucho más." También compartió: "Quiero que pueda jugar con los otros niños en el parque sin frustrarse tanto."

El padre, Emilio, añadió: "A mí me preocupa que cuando empiece la guardería no lo van a entender. Queremos que aprenda inglés también, pero primero necesita tener las palabras en español."

- Que disminuyan las rabietas relacionadas con la frustración comunicativa.
- Que la familia reciba estrategias para apoyar el lenguaje en ambos idiomas en el hogar.

Santi se despierta aproximadamente a las 7:00 a.m. y desayuna con su familia. La abuela Rosa lo cuida de 8:00 a.m. a 1:00 p.m. mientras la madre trabaja en Henderson County Health Clinic. Durante la mañana, juega con bloques y ve programas infantiles en español. La siesta ocurre de 1:30 p.m. a 3:00 p.m.. Por las tardes, la familia completa suele reunirse para cenar alrededor de las 6:30 p.m., seguido de tiempo de juego con su hermana Camila y el perro de la familia, Canela. La rutina de baño y cuento comienza a las 7:45 p.m., y Santi se duerme cerca de las 8:30 p.m..

7. OTRAS AGENCIAS Y SERVICIOS INVOLUCRADOS

La familia también recibe apoyo de las siguientes agencias:
- WIC del Condado de Henderson para nutrición infantil.
- Smart Start de las Montañas del Oeste, que proporciona recursos de desarrollo infantil temprano.
- La familia está en lista de espera para el programa Head Start a través de Henderson County Partnership for Children.

8. EVALUACIÓN Y NIVELES ACTUALES DE DESARROLLO

La evaluación más reciente, administrada por Laura Fernández el May 28, 2025, utilizó el Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5), versión en español. Santi obtuvo una puntuación estándar de 68 en Lenguaje Expresivo (percentil 2) y 79 en Lenguaje Receptivo (percentil 8). En el muestreo de lenguaje espontáneo, produjo combinaciones de dos palabras en 3/10 oportunidades, con producciones como "más agua" y "no quiero". Se observó el uso del fonema /t/ en posición inicial de manera consistente, pero omisión de /s/ final en palabras como "más" → [ma]. Requirió nivel de ayuda de claves moderadas (mod cues) para imitar vocabulario objetivo.

9. RESULTADOS (OUTCOMES) Y ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: Santi usará de 2 a 3 palabras combinadas para expresar necesidades durante las rutinas diarias en el hogar.
Estrategias: Modelado de lenguaje expandido durante las comidas y el juego; uso de encuadre de rutina con la abuela Rosa y la madre Marisol; práctica de vocabulario funcional ("quiero", "más", "ayuda") con apoyo visual.

Resultado 2: La familia identificará y usará al menos tres estrategias de comunicación aumentada (gestos naturales, espera estructurada, opciones limitadas) durante las rutinas de juego y alimentación.
Estrategias: Entrenamiento de los padres en sesiones quincenales; práctica conjunta durante la sesión de terapia de los jueves a las 9:30 a.m..

Resultado 3: Santi disminuirá los episodios de frustración comunicativa (actualmente 5 a 6 por día) a 2 o menos por día mediante el uso de comunicación funcional.

text:
Mateo Alejandro Flores, known to his family as "Teo," was born on January 14, 2024 and is currently enrolled in the NC Infant-Toddler Program through Piedmont CDSA. This report documents the Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) review conducted on September 29, 2026 at the family's home located at 1427 Maplewood Drive, Greensboro, 27401, in Guilford County. The review was facilitated by Dana Whitfield, Service Coordinator with Piedmont CDSA, and co-led by Priya Desai, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual pediatric speech-language pathologist with Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Partners. Mateo's Medicaid ID is MC4471829K, and his CDSA case file number is IT-2025-00417. Questions about this plan may be directed to Ms. Whitfield at (336) 555-0184 or to the clinic at (336) 555-0922. The family may also be reached by email at lucia.flores82@gmail.com, and general program information is available at www.piedmontcdsa.org.

Mateo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez, his father, Héctor Flores, and his older sister, Camila Flores, who is six years old and attends first grade. The family moved to Greensboro three years ago from the small village of El Rosario, where su mamá Lucía Rodríguez was raised and where several members of the extended family still live. Lucía Rodríguez works part-time in billing at Cone Health, and Héctor Flores works full shifts on the assembly line at Ashley Furniture Industries. Because of their work schedules, Mateo spends several afternoons each week with his babysitter, Rosa Hernández, a neighbor who has cared for him since he was an infant and who speaks only Spanish with him at home. Mateo's cousins, Sofía Martínez and Diego Martínez, visit most weekends and are described by the family as "his favorite playmates." The household also includes a small dog named Canela, whom Mateo reportedly follows around the house and attempts to call by pointing and vocalizing.

During the review meeting, Lucía Rodríguez shared the family's concerns and priorities in her own words, with interpretation support provided informally by Priya Desai when needed, though the family is comfortable communicating in both English and Spanish. Lucía Rodríguez stated, "Lo que más nos preocupa es que Mateo no habla como su hermana hablaba a esta edad. Entendemos todo lo que le decimos, pero él casi no usa palabras todavía. Dice 'mamá' y 'agua' y a veces 'pelota,' pero nada más." She went on to say, in English, "We want him to be able to tell us what he wants instead of getting so frustrated. He pulls our hands and cries when we don't understand him, and that's hard for all of us, especially for his sister." Héctor Flores added that he worries about how Mateo will do once he starts preschool, saying, "I don't want him to fall behind just because he's quiet. He's smart — he understands everything, he just doesn't say it." The family's stated priorities for this review period are: (1) increasing Mateo's expressive vocabulary in both English and Spanish, (2) reducing frustration-related behaviors during daily routines, and (3) preparing Mateo for a successful transition into a classroom setting.

Mateo currently attends Greensboro Early Head Start three mornings a week, where his lead teacher is Brenda Alvarez. Ms. Alvarez reports that Mateo is affectionate with peers and enjoys parallel play, particularly with classmates Jayden Coleman and Maya Patel, though he rarely initiates verbal interaction and instead relies on gestures, pulling, and pointing to communicate his needs. Ms. Alvarez noted that during circle time, Mateo will imitate the sign for "more" but does not yet combine words or signs spontaneously. The family also receives nutrition support through the Guilford County WIC Program and has been connected with parenting and early literacy resources through Guilford County Smart Start. Guilford County DSS has an open case related to a prior housing assistance application, and the family's current DSS caseworker has coordinated with Ms. Whitfield to ensure continuity of services; this coordination was noted at the review but does not currently affect Mateo's eligibility or services under the IFSP.

Mateo's daily routine was reviewed in detail to inform strategy selection. He wakes around 7:00 AM and eats breakfast with his sister before Lucía Rodríguez drives him to Greensboro Early Head Start by 8:30 AM. On the three mornings he does not attend the program, Rosa Hernández arrives at the home by 8:00 AM and takes him on a walk with Canela, which the family says is one of his most regulated and happy times of day. Lunch is typically a shared family meal, and Mateo naps from roughly 1:00 PM to 2:30 PM. Evenings include bath time, during which Héctor Flores reports Mateo is most vocal, babbling and occasionally approximating words like "agua" for water. Bedtime routines involve a shared book with Camila Flores, who the parents say has started "talking for him" to classmates and cousins when he struggles to be understood, a behavior the team discussed as well-intentioned but something to monitor so that Mateo continues to have opportunities to communicate independently.

The most recent evaluation was completed on September 15, 2026 by Priya Desai using the Preschool Language Scale, Fifth Edition (PLS-5). At a chronological age of 2;8, Mateo obtained an Auditory Comprehension standard score of 92 (30th percentile), within normal limits, and an Expressive Communication standard score of 70 (2nd percentile), indicating a significant delay in expressive language relative to his comprehension skills and same-age peers. Spontaneous language sampling conducted in both English and Spanish yielded a mean length of utterance of 1.1 morphemes, with an expressive vocabulary estimated at fewer than fifteen consistent words across both languages combined. Articulation screening using selected items from the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Third Edition (GFTA-3), suggested percent consonants correct (PCC) of approximately 58%, with inconsistent production of /k/, /s/, and /r/ in word-initial position; for example, Mateo produced "pelota" as "e-ota" and "agua" as "awa." These error patterns are considered consistent with his overall expressive delay rather than a distinct articulation disorder at this time, though they will continue to be monitored as expressive language increases. No concerns were noted regarding hearing, as a recent audiological screening coordinated through Dr. Angela Kim, Mateo's pediatrician, returned normal results bilaterally.

Based on these findings, the team, including Lucía Rodríguez, Héctor Flores, Dana Whitfield, and Priya Desai, developed and reviewed three outcomes for the coming IFSP period. The first outcome states that Mateo will increase his use of single words and early word combinations to request, label, and comment during daily routines, as reported by his parents and observed by the service coordinator. Strategies to support this outcome include modeling target vocabulary during meal times and bath time using simple, repeated phrases in the language the caregiver is most comfortable with; expanding Mateo's one-word utterances into two-word combinations (for example, responding to "agua" with "más agua" or "more water"); and using a core vocabulary board at home and at Greensboro Early Head Start so that Mateo has a consistent visual support across settings. Ms. Alvarez agreed to incorporate the same core board during classroom routines and to log any new spontaneous words weekly, coded in session notes as [EW] for early word emergence consistent with the family's SALT transcription system used by the therapy team.

The second outcome addresses reduction of frustration behaviors, specifically pulling, crying, and hitting, that occur when Mateo's communication attempts are not understood. The team agreed that caregivers, including Lucía Rodríguez, Héctor Flores, and Rosa Hernández, will consistently pair a gesture or sign with a spoken word before fulfilling a request, giving Mateo a brief wait time (approximately five seconds) to attempt an approximation before the caregiver repeats and provides the item. During the September evaluation, this strategy, implemented with moderate verbal cues and visual prompting, resulted in successful word approximations on 6 of 10 trials when caregivers paused appropriately, compared to 2 of 10 trials when the caregiver anticipated the request without waiting. The family will track frustration episodes in a simple daily log to be reviewed at the next contact, and Priya Desai will continue direct intervention sessions twice monthly to model the pause-and-expand strategy in vivo.

The third outcome focuses on transition readiness, given that Mateo will likely move from Part C to Part B services within the next IFSP cycle. The team discussed that Mateo's current classroom routine at Greensboro Early Head Start already approximates many preschool expectations, including circle time, structured snack, and peer play with classmates such as Jayden Coleman and Maya Patel, and that continued exposure to these routines, alongside continued speech-language intervention, will support a smoother transition. Dana Whitfield will initiate the transition planning conference at least ninety days prior to Mateo's third birthday and will coordinate with the local education agency to schedule a Part B eligibility evaluation. The family indicated they would like transition materials made available in both English and Spanish, and Priya Desai agreed to provide bilingual handouts summarizing Mateo's current strategies for use by any future preschool teacher.

The family also discussed ongoing support from extended family and community resources. Lucía Rodríguez noted that during visits to see relatives near El Rosario, Mateo is exposed primarily to Spanish, and the team agreed this supports rather than hinders his overall language development, consistent with current evidence on bilingual language acquisition in young children with expressive delays. The parents expressed appreciation for the flexibility of the Piedmont CDSA team in scheduling visits around Héctor Flores's shift changes at Ashley Furniture Industries and around Lucía Rodríguez's part-time hours at Cone Health. The team also confirmed that the family continues to receive nutrition benefits through Guilford County WIC Program without interruption and that the Smart Start-funded playgroup coordinated by Guilford County Smart Start remains a good fit for continued peer exposure on non-program days.

Service delivery for the current period is as follows. Speech-language intervention through Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Partners will continue twice monthly for 45-minute sessions, provided primarily in the home, with Priya Desai as the primary provider. Developmental service coordination will continue monthly through Piedmont CDSA, provided by Dana Whitfield. A family training component, billed under CPT code 92507 for individual speech-language treatment and CPT code 92605 when augmentative strategies are introduced, will be documented at each visit. The initial IFSP for this eligibility period was signed on April 22, 2025, and the plan was last formally reviewed prior to this meeting on March 18, 2026. This review, conducted on September 29, 2026, updates outcomes and strategies as described above, and the next scheduled six-month review will occur on or before March 29, 2027, unless the family or service coordinator requests an earlier review due to a significant change in Mateo's status.

The parents signed consent for continued services at the close of the meeting. Lucía Rodríguez stated that she felt the plan reflected the family's concerns accurately and appreciated that the strategies could be used both in English and Spanish at home. Héctor Flores asked whether Camila Flores could be included in a future session to learn some of the same prompting strategies, since she spends a significant amount of time with Mateo after school; the team agreed this would be incorporated into the next home visit. Priya Desai will also provide Rosa Hernández with a brief written summary of the core vocabulary strategy, translated into Spanish, so that the babysitter can reinforce the same approach during her time with Mateo. Dana Whitfield confirmed that all contact information on file, including the family's address at 1427 Maplewood Drive and email lucia.flores82@gmail.com, remains current, and reminded the family that additional program information, intake forms, and a calendar of Smart Start playgroup dates are posted at www.piedmontcdsa.org.

This review was completed collaboratively, and all team members, including Lucía Rodríguez, Héctor Flores, Dana Whitfield, and Priya Desai, agreed that Mateo continues to make steady progress toward his outcomes, particularly in auditory comprehension and social engagement with peers, while expressive language remains the area of greatest focus. The team will reconvene as scheduled, or sooner if requested, to continue monitoring Mateo's progress toward independent, functional communication across home, community, and future preschool settings.

Lo recogí porque la maestra Carmen me avisó que Mateo había tenido una mañana difícil. Su mamá, Lucía Rodríguez, me escribió anoche: "Mateo solo quiere hablar inglés con su hermana Camila, pero conmigo usa puro español, y a veces se frustra cuando no lo entendemos." Hablé también con doña Lupe, la abuela que lo cuida los lunes y miércoles mientras su papá, Jorge Hernández, trabaja en Triangle Build Supply en Durham.

Durante la sesión trabajamos los sonidos /k/ y /g/ en posición inicial usando tarjetas bilingües. Mateo produjo "gato" con mod cues y logró "casa" de forma espontánea, alcanzando 8/10 en el set de palabras dirigidas. En inglés, imitó "cup" y "go" con apoyo visual; marcamos [EW] en dos intentos donde hubo expansión espontánea del enunciado. Su maestra reportó que durante el círculo matutino, cuando su amigo Ethan le ofreció un juguete, Mateo dijo "gracias" claramente, sin sustitución de /g/, un avance desde la evaluación con el Goldman-Fristoe de enero, donde obtuvo un puntaje estándar de 78 (percentil 7).

Platicamos sobre el IFSP: la revisión está programada para el martes 4 de junio de 2025, y la fecha límite para firmar los documentos es el 20/05/2025. Le recordé a Lucía que la coordinadora de servicios de Smart Start de Wake County necesita el formulario actualizado antes de esa fecha; también está pendiente la carta de autorización de Medicaid, número 604837291B, que vence pronto. INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN (IFSP) — ANNUAL REVIEW / REVISIÓN ANUAL

---

INFORMACIÓN FAMILIAR / FAMILY INFORMATION

Mother: Elena Mendoza, age 29. Mom works nights at Biscuitville on Huffman Mill Road in Burlington and is home with Lupita during the day before her shift.
Father: Javier Torres, age 31, works days installing cabinets and is usually home by dinner.
Siblings: older brother Diego Torres Mendoza, age 6, and baby brother Juan Torres Mendoza ("Juanito"), age 8 months.
Other caregiver: maternal grandmother Rosa Mendoza ("Abuela Rosa"), who cares for Lupita two afternoons a week while Mom sleeps before her shift.

Home address: 412 Willowbrook Lane, Burlington, NC 27217
Home phone: (336) 555-0192   Cell (Mom): (336) 555-0233

Primary language in home: Spanish and English (hogar bilingüe)
Interpreter needed at meetings: [X] Yes  [ ] No — interpretation provided by Sofia Ramirez

---

NIVELES ACTUALES / PRESENT LEVELS

Lupita was assessed on September 10, 2026 using a bilingual battery. On the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale, she performed at the 20-22 month level receptively and the 16-18 month level expressively, below her chronological age of 2;11. On the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3, she produced word-initial consonants consistently but omitted most final consonants, for example saying "pa" for "pan" and "ga" for "gato." Stimulability for final /n/ was present with mod cues. On the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development-4, cognitive scores fell within the average range (standard score 95, 37th percentile). On the Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5, receptive vocabulary standard score was 82 (12th percentile), and expressive vocabulary checklist estimates were below the 10th percentile in both languages.

Oral-motor exam was within normal limits. Hearing screening passed bilaterally on August 20, 2026.

---

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA / FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES
(in the family's own words)

Mamá Elena shared, "Lo que más me preocupa es que Lupita no habla tanto como su hermano Diego a esta edad. Ella dice pocas palabras y a veces solo señala." She also said, "Quiero que aprenda a pedir las cosas, both in español and in English, porque va a empezar daycare pronto."

Papá Javier added, "I just want her to be able to tell us when she's hurt or hungry. Right now she gets frustrated and llora mucho, and we don't always know what she wants."

Abuela Rosa said, "Cuando yo le hablo español, ella me entiende todo, pero no me responde con palabras. Solo señala o me jala la mano."

Family priorities identified:
1. Lupita will use more words to request favorite foods and toys at home and at Little Sprouts Early Learning Center.
2. Family will receive strategies in Spanish and English to support language at mealtimes and bath time.
3. Family wants help understanding what to expect when Lupita starts the 2s classroom with Miss Patterson in January 2027.

---

Primary caregiving setting: [X] Home  [ ] Daycare  [ ] Relative's home
Current childcare: Lupita attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center [X] 3 days/week  [ ] 5 days/week, in Miss Patterson's toddler room. Her best friend there is a classmate named Emma, who she follows around during free play; staff report she also plays alongside a classmate called Noah during outdoor time.

Mealtimes: [X] High chair  [ ] Booster seat  [ ] Table
Lupita eats con la familia en la mesa. She will say "más" for more pero no pide comidas específicas todavía; family reports she eats a limited variety and prefers soft foods.

Nap/Sleep: [X] One nap  [ ] Two naps  [ ] No nap. Lupita naps from 1:00 PM to 2:30 PM at daycare and from about the same time on weekends at home.

Bedtime routine: [X] Bath  [X] Book  [ ] Bottle
Bath time is a favorite; family says "le encanta el agua" and she babbles happily but does not yet request items like "jabón" or "toalla" by name.

Pets in home: [X] Yes  [ ] No — family dog named Canela, whom Lupita calls "Ne-ne."

---

OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS / OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

[X] WIC  [X] DSS (food assistance)  [X] Smart Start  [ ] Head Start
Family receives nutrition support through WIC at the Alamance County office and has an open case with Alamance County DSS for food assistance. Elena also attends a parenting class through Smart Start of Alamance County on Tuesday evenings when Rosa watches the children.

Pediatrician: Dr. Raj Patel, Cone Health Pediatrics at Alamance Regional, last well visit August 3, 2026.
Physical Therapy evaluation: Mark Sullivan, PT, assessed gross motor skills on September 15, 2026; next visit scheduled October 15, 2026.

---

RESULTADOS Y ESTRATEGIAS / OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Lupita will use 2-3 word combinations to request desired items across settings (home, Little Sprouts Early Learning Center), increasing from a baseline of single words, within 6 months.
Strategies: Model simple phrases in both languages ("más agua," "more water"); mark targets using SALT code [EW]; follow her lead during play; offer forced choices at snack time; coach Miss Patterson on cueing during free play.

Outcome 2: Lupita will produce final consonants in familiar words with mod cues in structured play, measured by percentage correct across 3 consecutive sessions, target 8/10 trials.
Strategies: Emphasize target final sounds during book reading; use exaggerated word-final production; practice with gato/pan minimal pairs; reinforce approximations immediately.

Outcome 3: Family will report increased confidence using bilingual strategies at home, measured by a caregiver survey, by the next review.
Strategies: Provide handouts in Spanish and English; coach Elena and Javier during home visits; include Rosa as an additional communication partner given her regular caregiving role.

---

PRESTACIÓN DE SERVICIOS / SERVICE DELIVERY

Speech-Language Therapy: 2x/week, 45 minutes, provided by Yolanda Ortiz through Piedmont Pediatric Therapy Services, PLLC, in the home. Start date January 20, 2025; continuing through next review on March 22, 2027.

Physical Therapy: 1x/week, 30 minutes, provided by Mark Sullivan, beginning October 15, 2026.

Service Coordination: Ongoing, provided by Carla Jiménez of Catawba Valley CDSA, with quarterly reviews.

Transition planning: Family was informed that Lupita will transition from the Infant-Toddler Program near her third birthday. Transition conference to be scheduled for August 2026 re-confirmed for September 2026 with the local preschool team, pending referral to the school system by April 14, 2027.
