text:
CONFIDENTIAL SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

Child's Name: Mateo Alejandro Flores Rodríguez ("Mateo")
Date of Birth: November 14, 2023
CA: 2;10
Eval Dates: September 8, 2026 and September 15, 2026
Referral Source: Monica Reyes, Service Coordinator, Central Piedmont CDSA
Parents: Lucía Rodríguez (mother), Héctor Flores (father)
Home Address: 482 Willow Branch Ln, Monroe, NC 28110 (Union County)
Phone (CG cell): (704) 555-0168
Medicaid ID: 7719204456T
CDSA Case #: CPC-30421
Examiner: Jennifer Adams, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual (Spanish/English), Bright Path Therapy Services, PLLC
Interpreter present for parent report: Rosa Martínez, certified medical interpreter

BACKGROUND

Mateo is a 2;10 male referred for a comprehensive speech-language ax 2/2 CG and teacher concern re: limited expressive vocab in both Spanish and English, min use of 2-word combos, and frustration behaviors (hitting, throwing) when not understood. Referral came from Monica Reyes, SC at Central Piedmont CDSA, following an initial eligibility screening request submitted by Lucía Rodríguez after discussion w/ staff at Little Sprouts Early Head Start, where Mateo was enrolled from approx 6 mo to 24 mo of age. Family was connected to EHS through a joint referral from Mecklenburg County DSS and Mecklenburg County WIC when Mateo was an infant, during a period of housing instability. Lucía Rodríguez reports CG also received parenting support and a crib voucher through Smart Start of Union County around the same time.

CG report obtained via interview w/ Lucía Rodríguez (primary informant) and brief phone contact w/ Héctor Flores, w/ interpreter Rosa Martínez assisting for portions conducted in Spanish. Case hx and prior records reviewed, incl. EHS progress notes, DSS intake summary, and pediatric well-child notes from Dr. Sarah Kim at Union Family Pediatrics.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Pregnancy reportedly unremarkable per CG report; no reported substance use, no gestational diabetes. Mateo born November 14, 2023 at CarolinaCare Medical Center at 38 wks via vaginal delivery, birth wt 6 lbs 11 oz. Apgars WNL per CG recall (records not directly reviewed by examiner). Brief NICU observation period of approx 24 hrs 2/2 transient respiratory distress; no vent support required, d/c'd home w/ mother.

Med hx incl recurrent bilateral OM, approx 5 documented episodes btwn 8 mo and 22 mo, tx'd w/ oral abx each time. ENT referral made by Dr. Sarah Kim in February 2026; eval by Dr. James Patel at Union Family Pediatrics's affiliated ENT clinic resulted in bilateral myringotomy w/ tube placement, s/p March 11, 2026. CG reports no recurrence of OM since tube placement, and most recent audiology screening (June 2026) WNL bilaterally. No hx of seizure, no hospitalization beyond birth and tube placement, no current meds. Vision screening WFL per well-child visit. Gross/fine motor milestones reported WNL (walked indep approx 13 mo).

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Mateo is the youngest of three. Older sister Valentina (age 7) is reportedly a strong student, bilingual, attends elementary school in Monroe and often translates/interprets for Mateo at home per CG report, which examiner noted as a possible factor limiting Mateo's own communicative attempts. Middle sibling Joaquín (age 5) attends a different pre-K program; CG reports Joaquín's language development was unremarkable and typical.

Home language environment is primarily Spanish, est 70% Spanish / 30% English, per parent-completed Bilingual Input-Output ratio estimate. Lucía Rodríguez speaks mostly Spanish to Mateo; Héctor Flores code-switches more freely and uses more English at home, especially re: work-related talk. Héctor Flores is employed full-time at Catawba Valley Poultry Processing and works variable shifts, limiting his direct caregiving time on weekdays. Lucía Rodríguez is the primary daytime CG and does not currently work outside the home.

Extended family involved in daily care incl maternal grandmother, doña Lupe, who stays w/ the family approx 3 days/wk and speaks exclusively Spanish to Mateo. A part-time babysitter, Miss Ana, cares for Mateo on Héctor Flores's long shift days and reportedly uses a mix of English and simplified Spanish. Two cousins, Sofía (age 4) and Diego (age 6), live nearby and visit frequently; CG reports Mateo "parallel plays" more than interacts verbally w/ them. Family also reports a household dog, Canela, w/ whom Mateo reportedly initiates more vocalizations than w/ unfamiliar adults, per CG anecdote.

Mateo currently attends El Buen Camino Child Development Center M–F, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM, in la maestra Carmen's toddler room. Lead teacher la maestra Carmen and assistant teacher Mr. Tom both report via a classroom communication form that Mateo is social w/ peers during free play but has notably fewer words than classmates, incl Emma and Jayden, who are close in age. Prior to May 2026, Mateo attended Little Sprouts Early Head Start in Ms. Lopez's room, where he reportedly transitioned out of that program at age 24 mo per standard EHS age-out policy; records from that placement were requested and partially reviewed (brief developmental screening notes only).

Family's current IFSP, last reviewed July 22, 2026 and due for the 6-mo review on January 22, 2027, lists SLP, DT (developmental therapy), and SC services. This current ax was requested to inform tx planning and to update present levels prior to that review.

TEST RESULTS

Standardized and informal measures were admin'd in both languages w/ CG report supplementing direct observation, per best practice for a bilingual toddler assessment. Sessions occurred in the home, w/ Lucía Rodríguez and doña Lupe present for session 1, and at examiner's office for session 2, w/ Lucía Rodríguez present throughout.

Behavioral observations: Mateo separated easily from CG, engaged w/ toys and examiner w/in approx 3 min. Attention to task fair, required frequent redirection and mod cues to return to table activities. Play skills observed informally as appropriate for age — functional and early symbolic play noted (fed a doll, pushed a car and said "vroom"). Social engagement w/ examiner improved across session 2, incl increased eye contact and joint attention.

Oral mech exam: structures and function WNL. No signs of dysarthria or dysphagia; CG denies feeding concerns beyond mild picky eating.

Hearing: per most recent audiology screening (June 2026), hearing WNL bilaterally; no current concerns reported by family or ENT.

| Measure | Domain | Standard Score | Percentile | Age Equiv. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PLS-5 Spanish-English Bilingual Edition | Auditory Comprehension | 72 | 3rd %ile | approx 1;9 |
| PLS-5 Spanish-English Bilingual Edition | Expressive Communication | 68 | 2nd %ile | approx 1;7 |
| PLS-5 Spanish-English Bilingual Edition | Total Language Score | 68 | 2nd %ile | approx 1;8 |
| REEL-4 (parent report, Spanish version) | Receptive Language | 70 | 2nd %ile | approx 1;10 |
| REEL-4 (parent report, Spanish version) | Expressive Language | 65 | 1st %ile | approx 1;6 |
| MacArthur-Bates CDI: Inventario (CG report) | Vocab Checklist (Words Produced) | N/A | <10th %ile | approx 50 words total across both langs |

Informal speech sound inventory (combined conversational sample and single-word imitation, both langs): Mateo produced consonants /m, p, b, n, t, d, w/ consistently across word positions. Variable/inconsistent production of /k, g, f, s/; frequent fronting of velars (e.g., "dog" → "doh," /k/ → [t] in word-initial position). Final consonant deletion noted in approx 60% of opportunities (e.g., "más" → "ma"). No concerns re: oral-motor based artic disorder; pattern most consistent w/ phono delay 2/2 limited overall language exposure/opportunity rather than a primary speech sound disorder.

Expressive language sample: approx 15 min spontaneous + elicited sample yielded 22 different word approximations across both langs (e.g., "agua," "more," "ma" for mamá, "pa" for papá, "no," "up," "ba" for Canela [the family dog]). No true 2-word combinations observed; Mateo used single words and some gesture+word combos (pointing + "ma" to request). MLU could not be reliably calculated given predominance of single-word utterances; estimated MLU approx 1.1 morphemes/utterance.

Receptive language: Mateo followed simple 1-step directions w/ mod cues (gesture, modeling) approx 6/10 trials in Spanish, 3/10 in English w/o cues, improving to 7/10 w/ mod cues in English. Identified 8/10 common objects by pointing when named in Spanish; 5/10 in English. Responded to own name consistently (8/10).

Social communication / pragmatics: joint attention present but inconsistent; initiated communication primarily via gesture, pointing, and vocal approximations rather than conventional words. Frustration-related behaviors (throwing toy, brief crying) observed 2x across both sessions when communicative attempts were not understood by examiner, resolving quickly w/ redirection and modeling of the target word.

IMPRESSIONS

Based on standardized scores, CG/teacher report, and direct observation, Mateo presents w/ a Language Disorder affecting both receptive and expressive language, in both Spanish and English, consistent w/ a true bilingual language impairment rather than typical second-language acquisition variability — scores fall significantly below expected limits in BOTH languages, which supports a primary language disorder rather than a language difference pattern. Co-occurring mild-moderate phonological delay noted, likely compounded by hx of recurrent OM and associated fluctuating hearing during a critical early language-learning period, though current hearing is WNL. Frustration-related behaviors appear functionally related to communication breakdown rather than a primary behavioral/sensory concern, though this should continue to be monitored.

Mateo continues to meet eligibility criteria for EI services under NC's Infant-Toddler Program through Central Piedmont CDSA. Given scores in both languages and CG preference, recommend continued SLP services be delivered bilingually when possible, w/ consistent coaching for all CGs (incl doña Lupe and Miss Ana) to increase language-rich routines and reduce reliance on sibling Valentina's interpreting role, which may be limiting Mateo's independent communicative attempts.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Mateo is eligible for and recommended to continue direct SLP services at a frequency of 2x/wk, 30 min sessions, delivered in home and/or at El Buen Camino Child Development Center, per IFSP team decision at next review (January 22, 2027).
2. Bilingual service delivery recommended when feasible given mixed-language home environment; if a bilingual SLP is unavailable through Central Piedmont CDSA's contracted providers, recommend interpreter support (e.g., Rosa Martínez or another certified interpreter) for all direct sessions and CG coaching.
3. Parent/CG coaching across all primary caregivers (mother Lucía Rodríguez, father Héctor Flores, grandmother doña Lupe, and babysitter Miss Ana) on strategies incl expectant waiting, modeling 2-word combos, and reducing CG-to-CG linguistic inconsistency.
4. Recommend coordination w/ la maestra Carmen and Mr. Tom at El Buen Camino Child Development Center to incorporate target vocab and simple requesting strategies into classroom routines; consult form to be sent to classroom staff w/ parent consent.
5. Continue routine audiology monitoring given hx of recurrent OM; f/u w/ Dr. James Patel (ENT) per his recommended schedule.
6. Re-screen artic/phono skills in approx 6 mo or at next IFSP review, given expected gains w/ EI and resolution of OM-related hearing fluctuation.
7. Encourage reduced reliance on sibling Valentina as primary interpreter for Mateo's needs; instead use her as a peer-modeling support under adult guidance (e.g., modeling target phrases alongside Mateo rather than translating for him).
8. SC Monica Reyes to update present levels of development in the IFSP to reflect current findings and to coordinate continued eligibility documentation w/ Central Piedmont CDSA.
9. Family may also benefit from continued connection to community supports incl Smart Start of Union County playgroups and Mecklenburg County WIC nutrition counseling, both of which CG has found helpful historically.
10. R/O need for AAC supports at this time given functional gesture use and emerging word approximations; re-eval if minimal progress noted at 3-mo check-in.

This report reflects findings as of the eval dates above and should be considered alongside ongoing EI team input, CG report, and classroom observation data. Please contact examiner at jadams@brightpaththerapy.com or (704) 555-0199 w/ questions.

Jennifer Adams, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Bright Path Therapy Services, PLLC
Report Date: September 22, 2026

RESUMEN DE LA FAMILIA Y PRIORIDADES

Santiago vive con su mamá, Daniela Ruiz Soto, su papá, Alexander Peña Vargas, y su hermana mayor, Valentina Peña Ruiz, de 5 años, en Mebane. Su abuela, Rosario Soto, lo cuida tres tardes a la semana mientras los padres trabajan. El padre trabaja en Durham Steel Fabricators y la madre trabaja medio tiempo en Mebane Family Dental.

Durante la entrevista inicial el 15 de septiembre de 2026, la madre compartió, en sus propias palabras: "Siento que Santiago entiende todo lo que le decimos, pero casi no habla. Dice 'mamá', 'papá' y 'agua', pero nada más. Mi otra hija, Valentina, hablaba mucho más a esta edad. Me preocupa que se quede atrás cuando empiece la escuela." El padre añadió: "Yo trabajo mucho y no estoy tanto en casa, pero cuando estoy, veo que se frustra y empieza a gritar porque no lo entendemos."

Las prioridades de la familia son: (1) que Santiago use más palabras para pedir lo que necesita, (2) reducir las rabietas por frustración de comunicación, y (3) prepararlo para la transición a servicios escolares antes de cumplir 3 años.

RUTINAS DIARIAS

Santiago se despierta a las 6:45 a.m. y desayuna con la familia hasta las 7:30 a.m. Su abuela Rosario llega a las 8:00 a.m. y se queda hasta las 5:00 p.m. los lunes, miércoles y viernes. Asiste al programa de Early Head Start en el centro de Mebane los martes y jueves de 9:00 a.m. a 1:00 p.m., donde su maestra, Brenda Tyson, reporta que juega cerca de otros niños pero rara vez se comunica con ellos, incluyendo su compañero favorito, Mason. La siesta es de 1:30 p.m. a 3:00 p.m. La cena familiar es a las 6:00 p.m. y la rutina de baño y cuento comienza a las 7:15 p.m., terminando con la hora de dormir a las 8:00 p.m.

OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS

La familia recibe apoyo nutricional de WIC en la oficina de Hillsborough y está inscrita en el programa Smart Start del Condado de Orange para actividades de desarrollo temprano. DSS del Condado de Orange mantiene un caso abierto de seguimiento preventivo (no relacionado con custodia), con la trabajadora social Teresa Obando como contacto. El pediatra de Santiago, Dr. Andrés Villalobos, en UNC Children's Clinic de Hillsborough, refirió al niño al programa ITP tras notar el retraso de lenguaje durante su visita de los 24 meses.

EVALUACIÓN

La evaluación se realizó el 20 de septiembre de 2026 de 10:00 a.m. a 12:15 p.m. en el hogar familiar, con la intérprete Rosa Elena Méndez presente para apoyar a la familia en español.

Se administró la Escala Rossetti de Lenguaje Infantil, obteniendo un desempeño por debajo del nivel esperado para su edad en las áreas de pragmática (6;2 meses equivalente) y vocabulario expresivo (9 meses equivalente). En la prueba de articulación Goldman-Fristoe 3, Santiago produjo únicamente /m/, /p/ y /a/ de manera consistente, con un inventario fonético muy limitado para su edad cronológica. Las Escalas Bayley de Desarrollo Infantil (Bayley-4) mostraron una puntuación compuesta de comunicación de 70 (percentil 2), mientras que el dominio cognitivo estuvo dentro de límites normales (puntuación compuesta de 95). En el Test de Vocabulario en Imágenes Peabody (adaptado para evaluación informal dado su edad), Santiago identificó 4/10 ítems correctamente cuando se le pidió señalar.

Durante la sesión, Santiago produjo las palabras "aba" para "agua" y "mamá" de forma clara, pero no combinó palabras. Mostró comprensión de instrucciones simples de un paso con apoyo gestual 8/10 veces.

RESULTADOS DESEADOS (OUTCOMES) Y ESTRATEGIAS

Resultado 1: Santiago usará al menos 20 palabras funcionales de manera espontánea para pedir objetos y actividades preferidas en el hogar y en Early Head Start.
Estrategia: Modelado de lenguaje aumentado durante rutinas de comida y juego; uso de apoyos visuales; sesiones de terapia del habla dos veces por semana, 3:30 p.m. a 4:15 p.m., los martes, y 4:00 p.m. a 4:45 p.m., los jueves, con Marisol Fuentes, MS, CCC-SLP.

Resultado 2: La familia usará estrategias de comunicación funcional (señalar, gestos, palabras aproximadas) para reducir las rabietas relacionadas con la frustración comunicativa.
Estrategia: Entrenamiento a los padres mediante el modelo "Hanen - Más Que Palabras" adaptado, con visitas de coaching el primer miércoles de cada mes de 5:30 p.m. a 6:15 p.m.

Resultado 3: Santiago completará la transición a servicios de preescolar especial antes de los 3 años, con evaluación de elegibilidad coordinada por Orange County Schools, Programa de Intervención Temprana.
Estrategia: Reunión de transición programada para January 15, 2027; la coordinadora de servicios Yanira Collazo facilitará el intercambio de documentación con el equipo escolar.

FECHAS DE SERVICIO Y FIRMAS

Servicios de terapia del habla y lenguaje iniciaron el 28 de septiembre de 2026 y continuarán hasta la revisión semestral programada para el April 2, 2027. El plan fue firmado por Daniela Ruiz Soto y Alexander Peña Vargas el October 2, 2026, y por la coordinadora de servicios Yanira Collazo en la misma fecha.

Para preguntas sobre este plan, contactar a Marisol Fuentes, MS, CCC-SLP en m.fuentes@carolinapedstherapy.com o visitar www.carolinapedstherapy.com para recursos adicionales en español sobre el desarrollo del lenguaje infantil.

Nota de seguimiento: la próxima visita domiciliaria está programada para el November 4, 2026 a las 2:00 p.m., con reprogramación posible si la abuela Rosario Soto no puede estar presente para traducir instrucciones adicionales a los otros miembros de la familia.

Record Type: IFSP Annual Review
Program: NC Infant-Toddler Program (ITP)
CDSA Office: Foothills Children's Developmental Services Agency
Child Name: María José Fuentes Reyes
Preferred Name: Majo
Date of Birth: 4 de junio de 2022
Child ID: ITP-884217
Medicaid ID: NC9204471385J
Primary Home Language: Spanish/English
Parent/Guardian 1: Lucía Fuentes Hernández
Parent/Guardian 2: Carlos Reyes Torres
Home Address: 142 Hollyhock Lane, Hickory, NC 28601
County: Catawba County
Home Phone: (828) 555-0142
Parent Email: lucia.fuentes.h@mailbox.com
Service Coordinator: Jennifer Álvarez
SC Phone: (828) 555-0199
IFSP Meeting Date: 3 de marzo de 2025
IFSP Review Date: 09/15/2025
Annual IFSP Due Date: 03/03/2026
Report Author: Patricia Gómez-Wilson, M.S., CCC-SLP
Author Employer: Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC
Primary Diagnosis (ICD-10): F80.2 — Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder
CPT Codes (Current Services): 92507, 92523

RAZÓN DE LA REUNIÓN / REASON FOR MEETING

This six-month IFSP review was held on el martes 9 de septiembre de 2025 at the Foothills Children's Developmental Services Agency office in Morganton, NC, with a follow-up phone check-in on 09/15/2025. The purpose of the meeting was to review progress on Majo's current outcomes, update la información de la familia, and confirm services and frequency going into the next IFSP period. Present at the meeting were Lucía Fuentes Hernández (madre), Carlos Reyes Torres (padre, by phone from his job site), Jennifer Álvarez (Service Coordinator), and this writer, Patricia Gómez-Wilson, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist with Carolina Bilingual Therapy Partners, PLLC. Dr. Michael Ortiz, pediatrician, sent a written update in lieu of attending in person.

ANTECEDENTES / BACKGROUND

María José, a quien la familia llama Majo en casa, nació el 4 de junio de 2022 at Catawba Valley Medical Center. Según mamá, el embarazo y el parto fueron sin complicaciones, "nació a término, sin problemas, todo normal." Majo was referred to the Foothills CDSA on January 10, 2024 by her pediatrician, Dr. Michael Ortiz, después de que mamá reportó que Majo no decía ninguna palabra a los 18 meses. The initial eligibility evaluation, completed 02/02/2024, confirmed eligibility under the category of established developmental delay in the area of communication, consistent with ICD-10 code F80.2.

Majo vive en casa con su mamá, Lucía; su papá, Carlos, quien trabaja largas horas en Blue Ridge Freight Lines como conductor; su hermano mayor Diego Fuentes Reyes, de 5 años; y su abuela materna, Rosa Hernández, who moved in with the family last year and cares for Majo several afternoons a week while mamá works at Hickory Furniture Mart. The family also has a small dog, Max, who Majo loves to chase around the backyard. Diego attends kindergarten and, per mamá, "le ayuda mucho a su hermanita, le repite las palabras y juega con ella."

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA / FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

During the meeting, Lucía shared her ongoing concerns en sus propias palabras: "Todavía me preocupa que no hable tanto como los otros niños de su edad. Ella entiende todo, pero no me dice las cosas." She added, "en la guardería dicen que se frustra cuando quiere algo y no puede decirlo, y empieza a llorar o a jalar a la maestra." Carlos, joining by phone, agreed: "Yo quiero que ella pueda decir lo que necesita sin tanto drama, that's my main priority para que no se frustre tanto."

Both parents identified three priorities for the coming IFSP period:
1. Que Majo use more two- and three-word combinations in Spanish and English at home and at daycare.
2. Que pueda pedir lo que quiere ("quiero agua," "más galleta") instead of crying or pulling an adult's hand.
3. Continued support for bilingual language development so that Majo "no pierda el español" while also building English skills for preschool.

Rosa added during the visit, "yo le hablo solo en español, y a veces no sé si eso la confunde o la ayuda," which this writer addressed directly, reassuring the family that dual language exposure does not cause or worsen language delay.

RUTINAS DIARIAS DE LA FAMILIA / DAILY ROUTINES

Majo's typical day begins around 7:00 a.m. when she wakes up and has breakfast with Diego before mamá drops both children off — Diego at school and Majo at Little Steps Early Learning Center on Startown Road in Hickory — around 7:45 a.m.. Her classroom teacher, Ms. Hannah Price, reports that Majo enjoys circle time and music but becomes frustrated during free play when she wants a toy that a classmate, Emma, is using. Ms. Price noted, "she'll point and grunt, or just grab, instead of using any words, even 'mine' or 'help.'"

In the afternoons, Rosa or mamá pick up Majo around 4:30 p.m.. Snack time and bath time are described as favorite routines; mamá reports that Majo is most verbal during bath time, "cuando está en la tina feliz, dice más sonidos, como 'agua' o trata de decir 'pato' por el juguete." Dinner is typically around 6:00 p.m., and bedtime routine includes a favorite book read in Spanish by Rosa and in English by mamá on alternating nights, "para que escuche los dos idiomas."

Weekends often include a visit to tía Marisol, mamá's sister, who lives nearby and has two older children Majo enjoys watching but does not yet initiate play with directly.

OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS / OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

The family currently receives support from WIC for nutrition services, and mamá reported a recent appointment on 08/22/2025 where staff noted Majo's growth is on track. The family was also connected to Smart Start of Catawba County earlier this year for a home-visiting parent coaching program; the home visitor, Monica Reyes (no relation to the family), visits monthly and reinforces language strategies introduced in speech therapy. The family is not currently open with Catawba County DSS, though Jennifer Álvarez noted this as a resource should additional support be needed.

RESULTADOS DE EVALUACIÓN / SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION RESULTS

This writer administered portions of the Preschool Language Scale-5 (Spanish and English editions) and conducted dynamic bilingual assessment during the review period, with results summarized below in the context of ongoing treatment (CPT 92523, bilingual evaluation of speech sound production with evaluation of language comprehension and expression; CPT 92507, individual treatment of speech/language disorder).

Receptive language in both Spanish and English remains a relative strength: Majo followed two-step directions in Spanish ("dame la pelota y ponla en la caja") with 8/10 trials correct (80% accuracy) and followed comparable English directions with 7/10 accuracy (70%). Expressive language continues to show significant delay relative to same-age peers. Spontaneous utterances remain largely single-word or gestural; during a 20-minute structured play sample, Majo produced 14 intelligible single words (mix of Spanish and English, e.g., "agua," "más," "ball," "no") and only 2 two-word combinations ("más agua," "no quiero"). Age-equivalent expressive language skills are estimated at approximately 1;6, against a chronological age of 3;3.

Phonological skills were assessed informally; Majo substitutes /t/ for /k/ in word-initial position (e.g., "taza" produced as "tasa" is accurate, but "casa" is produced as "tasa"), and frequently deletes final consonants, consistent with expected patterns at this developmental stage rather than a primary articulation disorder. No oral-motor structural concerns were noted on examination.

Pragmatic/functional communication remains an area of concern consistent with family report: Majo uses pulling, grabbing, and crying as her primary strategies for requesting and protesting in approximately 60% of observed opportunities, with verbal or gestural communication (pointing plus a word attempt) used in the remaining 40%. With moderate verbal cueing and modeling, Majo was able to imitate two-word phrases with 8/10 accuracy (80%) during structured drill, suggesting good stimulability for continued direct intervention.

RESULTADOS Y ESTRATEGIAS / OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: Majo will use two-word combinations (noun + verb, or noun + noun) to request preferred items and activities in both Spanish and English, across home, daycare, and therapy settings, with 80% accuracy across three consecutive sessions.

Strategies: Continue weekly individual speech-language therapy (CPT 92507) focused on expansion of single words into two-word combinations using a bilingual carrier-phrase approach ("quiero ___," "más ___," "I want ___"). This writer will model target phrases in both languages during structured play and coach Lucía, Carlos, and Rosa on using the same expansion strategy during daily routines (snack, bath, play). Ms. Price at Little Steps Early Learning Center will be given a simple visual cue card to prompt Majo to use words instead of grabbing during free play, and will track frequency of word use versus grabbing/crying weekly.

Outcome 2: Majo will reduce use of grabbing, pulling, and crying as a primary communication strategy, replacing these behaviors with a word, approximation, or clear gesture paired with eye contact in at least 70% of observed communication opportunities at home and at daycare.

Strategies: Direct coaching for Rosa and both parents on consistent "wait time" and modeling (count to five silently, then model the target word) before meeting Majo's request, so she has the opportunity to attempt communication first. Monica Reyes from Smart Start will reinforce this same strategy during monthly home visits so that the approach is consistent across providers. Data will be collected informally by family and daycare staff using a simple frequency tally shared with this writer monthly.

Outcome 3: The family will continue to receive services and information in both Spanish and English to support bilingual language development, so that Majo continues to build skills in both languages without being pressured to use only one.

Strategies: All therapy materials, home programs, and written reports will be provided in Spanish and English. This writer, who is bilingual, will continue to deliver direct services bilingually, following Majo's lead on which language she initiates in during a given activity rather than requiring a single language. The team reaffirmed to the family, in response to Rosa's question above, that continued Spanish exposure at home will not delay or confuse Majo's English development, and in fact supports stronger overall language outcomes long term.

FRECUENCIA Y DURACIÓN DE SERVICIOS / SERVICE FREQUENCY AND DURATION

Speech-language therapy (CPT 92507) will continue at a frequency of one 45-minute individual session per week, delivered in the home setting, through the end of the current IFSP period and into the next annual IFSP, with re-evaluation (CPT 92523) scheduled prior to the annual review. Developmental therapy consultation at Little Steps Early Learning Center will continue monthly to support classroom carryover. Service coordination through Foothills CDSA will continue at the standard IFSP review interval, with the next formal six-month review scheduled for March 9, 2026 and the annual IFSP due no later than 03/03/2026.

The family was given this writer's direct contact information for questions between visits: Patricia Gómez-Wilson may be reached at (828) 555-0177 or p.gomezwilson@carolinabilingualtherapy.com. Additional program information is also available through Foothills CDSA's family resource line.

SEGUIMIENTO / NEXT STEPS

Jennifer Álvarez will send the family an updated written copy of the IFSP in both Spanish and English within ten business days of this meeting. Ms. Price will begin the weekly tracking log at Little Steps Early Learning Center starting el lunes 15 de septiembre de 2025. Monica Reyes will be contacted by this writer to coordinate shared strategies prior to her next scheduled home visit. The family's next individual therapy session is scheduled for 09/22/2025 at 10:30 a.m. at the family home.

Mamá expressed appreciation for the bilingual approach: "me gusta que todo esto está en los dos idiomas, así yo entiendo bien y puedo ayudar a Majo en casa." Both parents verbally agreed to the outcomes and strategies outlined above and consented to continued services as described.

FIRMAS / SIGNATURES

Parent/Guardian: Carlos Reyes Torres — Date: 09/09/2025 (verbal consent via phone, confirmed by Service Coordinator)
Service Coordinator: Jennifer Álvarez — Date: 09/09/2025

CAROLINA BILINGUAL SPEECH & LANGUAGE SERVICES, PLLC
919 Cary Parkway, Suite 220, Cary, NC 27511 • (919) 555-0148 • intake@carolinabilingualslp.com

EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y LENGUAJE / SPEECH-LANGUAGE EVALUATION REPORT

IDENTIFYING INFORMATION
- CHILD'S NAME / NOMBRE DEL NIÑO: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Fernández ("Mateo")
- DATE OF BIRTH: March 14, 2021
- CHRONOLOGICAL AGE AT EVALUATION: 4;7
- EVALUATION DATES: September 15, 2026 and September 22, 2026
- REPORT DATE: September 29, 2026
- MEDICAID ID: 908773412B
- CDSA CASE NUMBER: WC-2026-04471
- HOME ADDRESS: 142 Hollyridge Lane, Garner, NC 27529 (Wake County)
- HOME PHONE: (919) 555-0231
- PARENT/GUARDIAN: su mamá Lucía Rodríguez Cruz and su papá Héctor Fernández Ramos
- SIBLINGS: hermana mayor Sol Fernández Cruz (age 7, 2nd grade) and hermanito Emiliano Fernández Cruz (age 1)
- EVALUATOR: Daniela Soto-Hernández, M.S., CCC-SLP (bilingual, evaluation conducted en español e inglés)
- SERVICE COORDINATOR: Brenda Alvarez, Wake County CDSA
- REFERRAL SOURCE: Keisha Lopez, lead teacher, Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center

REASON FOR REFERRAL
- Mateo was referred by his teacher, Ms. Lopez, and by his service coordinator, Ms. Alvarez, due to ongoing concerns about speech sound intelligibility and limited sentence length in both Spanish and English.
- Mamá Lucía reports, "No lo entienden ni sus primos," noting that even extended family struggle to understand him during visits.
- Classroom staff, including aide T.G., report that Mateo often points or gestures instead of using words when frustrated, especially during transitions and group circle time.
- This evaluation was requested to determine eligibility for continued services through Wake County CDSA and to update the Individualized Family Service Plan (IFSP) ahead of the annual review scheduled for November 3, 2026.

BACKGROUND INFORMATION / HISTORIA DEL DESARROLLO
- Mateo is a 4-year-old bilingual (Spanish-English) male who lives with both parents and two siblings in Garner, NC.
- He has attended Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center since January 2023, currently in the Pre-K 2 classroom under Ms. Lopez.
- Family enrolled with Wake County CDSA in April 2023 following a referral from the pediatrician's office; Mateo has received CDSA-funded speech-language therapy since June 2023, one 30-minute session weekly.
- Family also receives support from WIC and has previously used services coordinated through Smart Start of Wake County for a developmental playgroup.
- A home visit record from DSS in 2022 is noted in the file related to a prior housing-stability referral; no open concerns are documented at this time.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY / HISTORIA MÉDICA
- Mateo was born at WakeMed Faison Women's Hospital at 34 weeks gestation via emergency cesarean section due to placental abruption.
- Birth weight was 4 lbs 2 oz; Apgar scores were 5 and 7.
- He spent 19 days in the NICU at WakeMed Faison Women's Hospital, where he was treated for respiratory distress syndrome and mild jaundice.
- Attending neonatologist during the NICU stay was Dr. Patricia Nguyen; his current pediatrician is Dr. Samuel Osei at WakeMed Garner Healthplex.
- Mamá Lucía reports a normal pregnancy prior to the abruption, with routine prenatal care through a midwife practice in Raleigh, NC.
- Developmental milestones per parent report: sat independently at 7 months, walked at 15 months, first words around 20 months in Spanish ("agua," "mamá," "más").
- No history of chronic ear infections; a single episode of otitis media was treated at age 2 with no tympanostomy tubes placed.
- Hearing screening passed bilaterally on August 10, 2026 at WakeMed Garner Healthplex; no vision concerns reported.
- No history of seizures, head injury, or hospitalization beyond the neonatal period.
- Family history is significant for a maternal uncle with a reported history of "problemas para hablar de niño" (childhood speech delay), resolved by school age without formal diagnosis.

FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY / HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE
- The home language is primarily Spanish, spoken by both parents, Sol, and extended family who visit frequently, including abuela María Elena Ramos and tía Rosa Fernández, who provides childcare two afternoons per week.
- Papá Héctor works full time at Perdue Farms processing plant in Clayton, NC; mamá Lucía works part time at the Food Lion distribution center in Garner, NC.
- English exposure occurs primarily at daycare and through Sol, who is more English-dominant and often interprets for Mateo with peers and extended family.
- Parents report that Mateo understands more than he produces in both languages ("entiende todo, pero no lo dice").
- Mamá Lucía states, "En la casa hablamos español casi siempre, pero cuando Sol habla con él en inglés, él se queda calladito."
- The family dog, Max, is frequently mentioned by Mateo and was used informally as a motivator during testing breaks.
- No prior speech-language services were received before enrollment with Wake County CDSA.
- Parents deny any family history of autism spectrum disorder; previous developmental screenings (ASQ-3) completed through Smart Start of Wake County did not flag concerns outside of communication.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES
- Review of records, including CDSA file, pediatric records, and daycare progress notes
- Parent interview (conducted bilingually with mamá Lucía and papá Héctor)
- Classroom observation at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center on September 15, 2026
- Formal and informal speech sound assessment in both languages
- Language sampling in structured and naturalistic contexts
- Oral-motor examination
- Standardized testing, including:
  - Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), English version
  - Spanish Articulation Measures (SAM), informal criterion-referenced probes
  - Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), Spanish-English bilingual edition
  - Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), select English subtests
  - Oral and speech motor screening checklist

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS
- Mateo separated easily from mamá Lucía in the waiting area and transitioned into the testing room with mild hesitation, warming quickly to toys and praise.
- He engaged well with bilingual instructions, frequently code-switching mid-sentence ("quiero el carro, the red one").
- Attention was adequate for structured tasks of 15-20 minutes with brief breaks; he required occasional redirection during less preferred activities.
- Articulation was notably more intelligible in single words than in connected speech; intelligibility in connected speech was estimated at 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 70% to familiar listeners (parent and clinician).
- Mateo used gestures, pointing, and single words more than multiword utterances when frustrated, consistent with teacher report.
- Rapport was supported by the use of the family dog Max and his sister Sol as conversational anchors; he readily discussed "jugar con Max" and "mi hermana Sol me ayuda."

ORAL-MOTOR EXAMINATION
- Facial symmetry within normal limits at rest and during movement
- Lip rounding, retraction, and alternating movements accomplished with mild imprecision
- Tongue lateralization, elevation, and protrusion within functional limits; mild reduced range noted for tongue tip elevation
- Dentition within normal limits for age; no structural abnormalities of hard or soft palate observed
- Diadochokinetic rates informally judged as mildly reduced for /pataka/ sequences
- No signs of dysarthria or significant oral-motor weakness identified; findings are consistent with a phonological-based speech sound disorder rather than a motor speech disorder

SPEECH SOUND PRODUCTION / PRODUCCIÓN DE SONIDOS DEL HABLA

ENGLISH (GFTA-3)
- Raw score: 38
- Standard score: 68 (2nd percentile), indicating speech sound production significantly below age expectations
- Phonological processes noted: final consonant deletion (e.g., "ca" for "cat"), cluster reduction (e.g., "poon" for "spoon"), stopping of fricatives (e.g., "tun" for "sun")
- Stimulable sounds with moderate cues (mod cues): /s/, /z/, /r/
- Sounds not stimulable even with maximal cues: /θ/, /ð/

SPANISH (SAM informal probes)
- Estimated percentage of consonants correct (PCC) in single words: 58%
- Target word 'sol' elicited during the Spanish picture-naming probe (meaning "sun"); Mateo produced [tol], substituting a stop for the initial fricative, consistent with the stopping pattern also observed in English
- Interestingly, when shown a photo of his sister during a separate warm-up activity, Mateo spontaneously said, "esa es mi hermana Sol," producing her name with the same [tol] substitution, confirming the error is phonologically based rather than lexically specific
- Other Spanish error patterns: liquid simplification (/r/ and /l/ frequently produced as glides), cluster reduction in words like "fruta" → [futa], final consonant deletion in words ending in /s/ and /n/
- Spanish trilled /r/ was not yet stimulable even with maximal cueing; tap /r/ was stimulable with mod cues in word-initial position

Score Summary Table

| Measure | Language | Raw/Score | Standard Score | Percentile | Classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GFTA-3 | English | 38 | 68 | 2nd | Significantly Below Average |
| SAM (informal) | Spanish | PCC 58% | N/A | N/A | Below Age Expectations |
| PLS-5 Auditory Comprehension | English | 32 | 72 | 3rd | Below Average |
| PLS-5 Expressive Communication | English | 29 | 65 | 1st | Significantly Below Average |
| PLS-5 Total Language Score | Bilingual | 30 | 67 | 1st | Significantly Below Average |
| CELF Preschool-3 Sentence Structure | English | 5 | 70 | 2nd | Below Average |
| CELF Preschool-3 Word Structure | English | 6 | 73 | 4th | Below Average |

LANGUAGE SAMPLE ANALYSIS
- A 50-utterance spontaneous language sample was collected during structured play in both languages and analyzed for mean length of utterance (MLU) and grammatical structures.
- MLU in morphemes: Spanish sample = 2.4; English sample = 2.1, both below expected range for chronological age (typically 3.5-4.5 morphemes at 4;7)
- Vocabulary diversity (number of different words, NDW) was within the low-average range relative to CDSA bilingual norms for children of similar language exposure history
- Grammatical forms frequently omitted in Spanish: plural markers (-s), definite articles ("el," "la") in obligatory contexts
- Grammatical forms frequently omitted in English: copula "is," third-person singular -s, past tense -ed
- Example utterance (Spanish): "yo quiero el [tol]" (target: "yo quiero el sol"), produced during a picture description task
- Example utterance (English): "Mateo want car red" (target: "Mateo wants the red car")
- Pragmatic skills, including turn-taking, joint attention, and requesting, were judged appropriate for age in both languages
- No concerns noted regarding social reciprocity, eye contact, or restricted/repetitive behaviors during this evaluation

CLASSROOM OBSERVATION SUMMARY
- Observation conducted at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center during morning circle time and center-based play on September 15, 2026
- Mateo participated in group songs but used primarily single words or gestures during verbal turns
- Peer interaction was observed with classmate Josiah, who frequently repeated Mateo's requests aloud to the aide to help communicate his needs
- Teacher Ms. Lopez reported that Mateo "entiende las instrucciones perfectamente pero casi no habla en grupo"
- Classroom aide T.G. noted that Mateo is more verbal during one-on-one interactions than in whole-group settings

IMPRESSIONS / IMPRESIONES DIAGNÓSTICAS
- Results of this evaluation indicate that Mateo presents with a moderate-to-severe speech sound disorder (phonological) affecting both Spanish and English, characterized by consistent, cross-linguistic error patterns including stopping of fricatives, cluster reduction, liquid simplification, and final consonant deletion.
- Concurrently, Mateo presents with a language disorder affecting both receptive and expressive language in Spanish and English, consistent with a bilingual child exhibiting difficulties beyond what would be expected from typical second-language acquisition or dialectal variation alone, as error patterns are present and proportionally similar across both languages.
- Diagnostic impression: Speech Sound Disorder (ICD-10: F80.0) and Language Disorder (ICD-10: F80.2), affecting a bilingual Spanish-English speaker, with patterns not attributable to dialectal difference or typical bilingual language acquisition.
- Severity is considered moderate-to-severe based on standard scores falling at or below the 4th percentile across multiple measures and estimated connected-speech intelligibility of 40% to unfamiliar listeners.
- These findings are consistent with, and represent an increase in severity compared to, concerns noted at the time of initial CDSA enrollment in April 2023.
- Mateo continues to meet eligibility criteria for ongoing early intervention services under Wake County CDSA guidelines based on documented delay exceeding 25% in two or more developmental domains (communication and, to a lesser extent, social-emotional functioning related to communication frustration).

RECOMMENDATIONS / RECOMENDACIONES
- Continue individual speech-language therapy through Wake County CDSA, increasing frequency from once weekly to twice weekly 30-minute sessions to address the combined speech sound and language disorder.
- Therapy should be conducted bilingually, targeting shared phonological processes (stopping, cluster reduction, liquid simplification, final consonant deletion) across both Spanish and English to maximize cross-linguistic transfer.
- Incorporate family-centered coaching strategies so that mamá Lucía, papá Héctor, and caregiver tía Rosa can reinforce targets during daily routines in the home language.
- Collaborate with classroom staff, including Ms. Lopez and aide T.G., to support carryover of expressive language targets during group activities at Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center.
- Update the IFSP at the scheduled annual review on November 3, 2026 to reflect current goals and increased service frequency; service coordinator Brenda Alvarez to facilitate scheduling with the family.
- Recommend a follow-up hearing screening in 6 months given the history of fluctuating language development, despite the recent passed screening on August 10, 2026.
- Encourage continued enrollment in WIC and consider referral to Smart Start of Wake County playgroup services to increase structured peer language exposure.
- Reassess in approximately 6 months, or sooner if significant changes in communication skills are observed, to monitor progress toward IFSP goals and determine continued eligibility.
- Provide the family with bilingual home-practice materials, including a target word list containing minimal pairs such as 'sol/tol' and 'casa/tasa', to support generalization of fricative production outside of therapy sessions.
- Consider referral for an audiology consult if speech intelligibility does not improve within 3 months of increased therapy frequency, to rule out subtle auditory processing contributions.

SUMMARY
- Mateo Alejandro Cruz Fernández, age 4;7, presents with a moderate-to-severe phonological speech sound disorder and a language disorder affecting both Spanish and English, consistent with difficulties beyond typical bilingual development.
- He remains eligible for and would benefit from increased early intervention services coordinated through Wake County CDSA.
- Family involvement, including mamá Lucía Rodríguez Cruz, papá Héctor Fernández Ramos, and extended family support from tía Rosa Fernández and abuela María Elena Ramos, is strong and should continue to be leveraged in treatment planning.
- This report should be shared with Little Sprouts Early Head Start Center staff, the family's pediatrician Dr. Samuel Osei, and the CDSA IFSP team to support coordinated care.

Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist

Nota de sesión diaria – terapia de lenguaje y habla

3 de marzo de 2025, sesión número catorce con Mateo Fernández (edad 4;2) en el domicilio familiar, ubicado en 214 Calle Roble, Durham, NC, 27703. La sesión comenzó a las 3:30 p.m. y terminó a las 4:15 p.m., conforme a la autorización número AUTH-887234-NC y al plan de servicios bajo Medicaid ID 998213456A. El número de ITP de Mateo en el sistema NC es ITP-0455921, y el número de miembro de la aseguradora secundaria es MB-7745201.

Al llegar, Mateo estaba jugando en la sala con su hermana Sol, quien tiene seis años y participó brevemente al inicio de la sesión imitando sonidos junto a su hermano, lo cual ayudó a disminuir la ansiedad inicial de Mateo. Su mamá, Lucía Fernández, estuvo presente durante toda la sesión y reportó que, el martes 4 de marzo, Mateo usó la palabra "más" espontáneamente en casa, lo cual es un avance notable respecto a semanas anteriores. También mencionó que la niñera, Carmen Osorio, ha estado reforzando los mismos objetivos durante las tardes en que ella trabaja en Duke Regional Logistics.

Trabajamos con tarjetas de vocabulario funcional y se practicó la producción del fonema /k/ en posición inicial. Mateo logró producir "casa" como ["kasa"] con apoyo de modelado directo (mod cues) en 7/10 intentos, lo cual representa una mejora comparado con la sesión anterior (24 de febrero de 2025), cuando el desempeño fue de 4/10. También se trabajó el fonema /s/ en sílabas finales; produjo "más" como ["mas"] de forma espontánea sin apoyo en dos ocasiones, registrado en SALT como [EW].

Se administró una revisión corta de seguimiento utilizando ítems del PLS-5, obteniendo una puntuación estándar de 78 en el área de lenguaje expresivo, percentil 7. Esto es consistente con la evaluación formal realizada por la Dra. Alejandra Reyes en enero de 2025, en el Hospital UNC Children's Developmental Center.

Antes de la sesión, hablé brevemente por teléfono con la maestra de preescolar, Srta. Johnson, del salón de Mateo en Little Sprouts Early Learning Center, quien indicó que él ha comenzado a usar gestos combinados con palabras sueltas para pedir ayuda a su compañero Diego durante el juego libre. Esto coincide con lo observado en casa.

La coordinadora de servicios, Mónica Alvarado, de la agencia CDSA del Piedmont Central, confirmó por correo que la próxima reunión de revisión del IFSP será el 14 de abril de 2025. El número de caso asignado por la agencia es CASE-45218-PC.

Hacia el final de la sesión, se recomendó a la familia continuar con la práctica de vocabulario funcional usando objetos reales en casa, incorporando a Sol como modelo de lenguaje cuando sea posible, ya que su participación parece motivar a Mateo significativamente. La familia también comentó que el padre, Javier Fernández, estará disponible para las próximas sesiones los jueves por la tarde, ya que cambió su horario en Triangle Builders Supply.

Próxima cita programada para el 10/03/2025 a las 3:30 p.m.. Se dejó copia de la nota en el expediente físico y se envió resumen electrónico a través del portal seguro de Carolina Pediatric Speech Partners. Contacto de la clínica para dudas administrativas: 919-555-0147 o recepcion@carolinapsp.com. Esta nota fue documentada por Laura Méndez, M.S., CCC-SLP, terapeuta bilingüe tratante, el mismo día de la sesión.

NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN (IFSP) — ANNUAL REVIEW / REVISIÓN ANUAL

Child's Name: María José Hernández Rodríguez    Date of Birth: April 2, 2023    Record ID: IT-48291
Medicaid #: 920483517D    Primary Language: Spanish    Secondary Language: English
IFSP Review Date: September 18, 2026    Next Review Due: March 18, 2027    Service Coordinator: Jennifer Alvarez
CDSA Office: Foothills Children's Developmental Services Agency, Hickory, NC    CDSA Phone: (828) 555-0137
Family Address: 412 Willowbrook Lane, Conover, NC 28613    Family Phone: (828) 555-9042
Mother: Lucía Rodríguez Mejía    Father: Carlos Hernández Vega    Interpreter Needed: Yes — Spanish

PARTICIPANTS / PARTICIPANTES EN LA REUNIÓN

Present at today's meeting were Lucía Rodríguez Mejía (madre), Carlos Hernández Vega (padre, by phone from work), service coordinator Jennifer Alvarez, bilingual speech-language pathologist Ana López, M.S., CCC-SLP of Bilingual Beginnings Speech & Language Services, PLLC, occupational therapist Grace Thompson, OTR/L, and interpreter Marisol Peña. María José's maternal grandmother, Rosa Mejía, who provides daily child care, also attended. This report was written by Ana López, contact ana.lopez@bilingualbeginningsslp.com, office website www.bilingualbeginningsslp.com.

RESUMEN FAMILIAR / FAMILY BACKGROUND

María José is a bilingual child who lives at home with her parents, Lucía Rodríguez Mejía and Carlos Hernández Vega, and her older brother, Mateo, age 6. Her grandmother, Rosa Mejía, cares for María José three days a week while her parents work. Lucía Rodríguez Mejía works part-time at Conover Family Dental, and Carlos Hernández Vega is employed at Catawba Valley Furniture Manufacturing. The family attends appointments with pediatrician Dr. Michael Osei at Catawba Valley Pediatrics. María José also attends Pequeños Pasos Bilingual Childcare two mornings a week, 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m..

PREOCUPACIONES Y PRIORIDADES DE LA FAMILIA / FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

Lucía Rodríguez Mejía shared, in her own words: "Mi hija entiende todo, pero casi no habla. Le digo 'dame el vaso' y ella me lo da, pero no me dice nada. Solo señala y hace sonidos como 'eh, eh.' Me preocupa que cuando empiece preescolar no la van a entender ni en español ni en inglés." She added, "Quiero que ella pueda decirme 'mamá, tengo hambre' o 'me duele,' porque ahora yo tengo que adivinar todo."

Carlos Hernández Vega, speaking by phone, said: "I just want her to be able to tell her brother Mateo what she wants without crying. Right now if he doesn't understand her she gets really frustrated and throws herself on the floor." He also noted that at Catawba Valley Furniture Manufacturing he has limited flexibility to attend daytime appointments, so he asked that future sessions be scheduled after 4:30 p.m. when possible.

Rosa Mejía added, "Cuando estamos en la cocina ella me señala la nevera y dice 'aba' para agua, pero no dice más palabras. A veces se frustra mucho y grita." The family's top priorities, in order, are: (1) functional words and short phrases in both Spanish and English so María José can make basic needs known, (2) reduction of frustration-related tantrums tied to communication breakdown, and (3) preparation for the transition to Part B preschool services, as María José turns 3 in April 2027.

RUTINAS DIARIAS / DAILY ROUTINES

María José's typical day begins at approximately 7:00 a.m. with breakfast, usually eggs and tortilla, prepared by Rosa Mejía or Lucía Rodríguez Mejía. On daycare days she arrives at Pequeños Pasos Bilingual Childcare by 8:00 a.m. and is picked up at 12:00 p.m.. On non-daycare days she stays with Rosa Mejía, engaging in play with blocks, a push toy, and watching short videos in Spanish. Lunch is around 12:30 p.m., followed by a nap from about 1:00 p.m. to 2:30 p.m.. In the evening, the family eats dinner together around 6:00 p.m., and María José enjoys bath time around 7:30 p.m. before bed at 8:00 p.m.. Her brother Mateo often tries to play with her after school, but the family reports frequent frustration episodes during this time because María José cannot verbally direct play or protest effectively.

OTRAS AGENCIAS INVOLUCRADAS / OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

The family currently receives nutrition support through Catawba County WIC and has an open case with Catawba County Department of Social Services for housing assistance referral, initiated July 14, 2026. The family was also connected with Smart Start of Catawba County for a childcare subsidy application, submitted on August 3, 2026. Jennifer Alvarez confirmed that no additional agency releases are needed at this time, but the family consented to continued information sharing between Foothills Children's Developmental Services Agency and Catawba County Department of Social Services.

EVALUACIONES RECIENTES / RECENT EVALUATIONS

Speech-language evaluation was completed by Ana López, M.S., CCC-SLP on September 2, 2026 using the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (administered bilingually with parent and grandmother report), the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (screening items only, given limited expressive sample), and the Preschool Language Scale, as well as informal play-based observation con la mamá y la abuela presentes.

On the Rossetti, María José (chronological age 2;5 at testing) performed within the 9-12 month range for expressive language and the 15-18 month range for receptive language, reflecting a significant gap between comprehension and production in both languages. Parent report indicated a combined expressive vocabulary of approximately 12 words across Spanish and English ("mamá," "papá," "aba" for agua, "no," "más," "ta-ta" for gracias, "up," "bye," "eh-eh" used as a general request, among others). She demonstrated use of consistent vowel approximations and some early consonants but no two-word combinations.

Occupational therapy evaluation by Grace Thompson, OTR/L, also on September 2, 2026, used the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Fourth Edition, and the Peabody Developmental Motor Scales, Second Edition. María José scored within the average range for gross motor skills (standard score 97) and low average for fine motor skills (standard score 83), with mild difficulty in bilateral hand use noted during block play and self-feeding with a spoon. Cognitive subtests on the Bayley were within the average range, standard score 94, 35th percentile, consistent with age expectations and supporting that her primary area of concern is expressive communication rather than global delay.

A receptive vocabulary screening using select items from the Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5, presented bilingually, suggested receptive skills closer to age level than expressive skills, though full standardized administration was not possible given María José's limited sitting tolerance and attention during the session, which lasted from 9:15 a.m. to 10:40 a.m..

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT / NIVELES ACTUALES DE DESARROLLO

Communication: María José communicates primarily through pointing, pulling adults toward desired objects, and a small set of vocalizations. She imitates some single-syllable approximations ("ba" for "bottle," "pa" for "papá") with moderate verbal and visual cues but does not yet combine words. She understands simple one-step directions in Spanish more consistently than in English, per both standardized testing and parent/grandmother report, and responds to her name and to familiar routine phrases such as "vamos a comer."

Social-Emotional: María José seeks comfort from Lucía Rodríguez Mejía and Rosa Mejía and enjoys parallel play with her brother Mateo, though interactions frequently break down into frustration when she cannot make her wants known. Tantrums, described by the family as "se tira al piso y grita," occur approximately 3-4 times per day, most often around mealtimes and transitions.

Motor/Adaptive: Fine motor skills are emerging appropriately for most tasks but show mild delay in bilateral coordination and utensil use, consistent with OT findings above.

RESULTADOS / OUTCOMES

Outcome 1 (Family priority: functional communication). María José will use at least 10 new single words or approximations across Spanish and English, functionally and spontaneously, to request preferred items, within 6 months.
Strategy: Ana López will model target words at the slow rate using simultaneous bilingual input (Spanish primary, English secondary) during play-based sessions, using cueing levels ranging from minimal verbal cue to moderate cues (mod cues) with hand-over-hand pointing as needed. The family and Rosa Mejía will be coached to pause expectantly after offering choices, rather than anticipating María José's wants, to create communication opportunities during daily routines such as snack time and bath time.

Outcome 2 (Family priority: reducing frustration). María José will use a gesture or vocalization paired with eye contact to protest or request, in place of a full tantrum, in at least 4 of 5 observed opportunities within 4 months.
Strategy: Introduction of a small core set of manual signs (más, no, ayuda) paired with spoken words in both languages, modeled by Ana López and reinforced by Lucía Rodríguez Mejía, Carlos Hernández Vega, and Rosa Mejía during identified high-frustration routines (mealtime, transition out of bath). Mateo will be included in one session to learn how to wait for his sister's attempt before responding to her cues.

Outcome 3 (Family priority: school readiness). María José will participate in short structured listening and turn-taking activities for up to 5 minutes with an adult or peer, in preparation for group settings such as Pequeños Pasos Bilingual Childcare and future Part B preschool.
Strategy: Ana López will coordinate with daycare staff, with written parental consent, to share strategies used in session; Jennifer Alvarez will begin transition planning discussions no later than January 2027 given María José's third birthday in April 2027.

SERVICIOS / SERVICES

Frequency/Duration: 2x weekly, 45 minutes    Start Date: October 1, 2026    End Date: March 31, 2027    Location: Home, 412 Willowbrook Lane, Conover, NC
Service: Occupational Therapy, individual, home-based    Provider: Grace Thompson, OTR/L    Agency: Foothills Children's Developmental Services Agency
Frequency/Duration: 1x weekly, 30 minutes    Start Date: October 3, 2026    End Date: March 31, 2027    Location: Home
Service: Service Coordination    Provider: Jennifer Alvarez    Agency: Foothills Children's Developmental Services Agency
Frequency: Monthly contact, minimum    Start Date: October 1, 2026    End Date: March 31, 2027

Sessions for speech-language therapy are scheduled Tuesdays and Thursdays, 4:45 p.m. to 5:30 p.m., per Carlos Hernández Vega's request so he can attend after work. Occupational therapy sessions are scheduled Wednesdays, 10:00 a.m. to 10:30 a.m., during a time Rosa Mejía confirmed she is available to participate and support carryover.

NOTAS DE LA REUNIÓN / MEETING NOTES

Marisol Peña interpreted the full meeting for Lucía Rodríguez Mejía and Rosa Mejía, confirming understanding of all outcomes and services in Spanish before signatures were obtained. Carlos Hernández Vega confirmed understanding by phone in English and gave verbal consent for the plan, to be followed by a signed copy mailed to the family. Jennifer Alvarez will mail the signature page to 412 Willowbrook Lane, Conover, NC 28613 and follow up by phone at (828) 555-9042 by September 25, 2026 to confirm receipt and return.

The family asked whether additional bilingual resources were available; Ana López shared a handout of home strategies in Spanish and English and noted that the practice's resource page, www.bilingualbeginningsslp.com/recursos, includes short videos demonstrating sign and word modeling techniques. The family can also reach Ana López directly at ana.lopez@bilingualbeginningsslp.com with questions between sessions.

Lucía Rodríguez Mejía stated at the close of the meeting, "Gracias por explicarlo todo en español. Ahora entiendo mejor por qué hay que hacer las señas también en inglés, no solo en español, para que ella esté lista para la escuela." The team agreed this review adequately reflects the family's current concerns and priorities, and the next IFSP review will occur on or before March 18, 2027, with an interim contact scheduled by Jennifer Alvarez around December 15, 2026 to check progress on Outcomes 1 and 2.

Service Coordinator: Jennifer Alvarez, Piedmont CDSA
Evaluator: Katherine Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP, Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Interpreter: Not needed; evaluator is a bilingual English/Spanish provider

ICD-10 Codes: F80.1, F80.2

ANTECEDENTES / BACKGROUND

Mateo Hernández Cruz is a 4;7-year-old bilingual (Spanish/English) boy referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by Dr. Sarah Kim due to parent and teacher concerns regarding limited intelligibility and expressive language delay in both languages. This evaluation was requested as part of an ongoing IFSP through Piedmont CDSA, coordinated by Jennifer Alvarez. Mateo resides with his parents, Lucía Rodríguez Hernández and Francisco Hernández Ortiz, and his older sister, Paz, age 7, at the family home on Sycamore Lane in Charlotte. Lucía Rodríguez Hernández reported during intake, "Él entiende todo, pero cuando habla, a veces no le entendemos." She added, "En casa hablamos los dos idiomas, pero más español conmigo y más inglés con su papá."

HISTORIA DEL NACIMIENTO Y DESARROLLO / BIRTH AND DEVELOPMENTAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 38 weeks gestation via scheduled Cesarean section at Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center on March 14, 2021. Lucía Rodríguez Hernández reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with regular prenatal care. Birth weight was reported as 7 lbs, 2 oz; no NICU admission was required. Mother reported mild jaundice treated with phototherapy for two days, resolved prior to discharge.

Developmental milestones were reported as generally within normal limits for gross and fine motor domains: Mateo sat independently at approximately 6 months, walked at approximately 13 months, and began self-feeding with utensils around 18 months. Mother reported first words emerged "tarde, como a los dos años," noting he said "mamá" and "agua" around 24 months, considerably later than his sister Paz, who the family reports spoke in short sentences by 18 months.

Mateo has a history of recurrent acute otitis media, with four documented episodes between 12 and 30 months of age. Bilateral myringotomy tubes were placed on 3 de marzo de 2023 by Dr. Michael Chen, ENT, at Novant Health Presbyterian Medical Center. A follow-up audiological evaluation on 06/14/2023 documented hearing within normal limits bilaterally post-tube placement, and a repeat screening on 9/18/2025 again confirmed normal hearing sensitivity. No tubes remain in place; the right tube extruded spontaneously and the left was removed during a routine ENT visit. Family denies history of seizures, significant head trauma, or hospitalization beyond the above.

HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DE LENGUAJE / FAMILY AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

The home environment is bilingual. Lucía Rodríguez Hernández was born and raised in Guatemala and emigrated to the United States as a teenager; Spanish is her dominant and preferred language, though she is functionally bilingual. Francisco Hernández Ortiz was born in Charlotte, NC, and is a native English speaker who also speaks Spanish, learned primarily from his own mother. Per parent report, approximately 70% of input to Mateo at home is in Spanish and 30% in English, with substantial code-switching by both parents within conversations and even within sentences.

Mateo's paternal grandmother, Rosa Ortiz, currently resides in Honduras and speaks with the family by phone several times weekly; her number is +504 9876-5432. She visited for six weeks during the summer of 2024 and provided significant childcare at that time, speaking exclusively Spanish with Mateo. During the school year, Mateo's primary daytime caregiver on non-daycare days is his paternal aunt, Carolina Ortiz Méndez, who cares for him two days per week while his parents work. Lucía Rodríguez Hernández is employed at Ramirez Cleaning Services, and Francisco Hernández Ortiz works at Charlotte Pipe and Foundry.

Mateo's sister, Paz, is in second grade at Elm Street Elementary and is reportedly meeting all academic and language milestones with no concerns; she is described by her mother as "muy habladora, igual que su papá." Paz frequently acts as an interpreter between Mateo and unfamiliar adults, per parent report, which the clinician noted may mask some of Mateo's communication difficulty in less structured settings.

Mateo has attended Little Sprouts Academy since age 2. His current teacher, Ms. Amanda Lopez, reported via a note relayed through Lucía Rodríguez Hernández that "no sigue bien las instrucciones en el salón" and that he becomes frustrated during circle time when peers do not understand him. Mateo's primary playmate at daycare is a classmate, Ethan Davis; parent reports their interactions are mostly nonverbal, involving blocks and cars rather than conversation. The family dog, Max, is frequently mentioned at home; Mateo reportedly imitates the dog's bark more reliably than he produces many age-expected words.

An IFSP review meeting is scheduled for el martes 4 de noviembre de 2025 to discuss this evaluation and update goals accordingly.

PROCEDIMIENTOS DE EVALUACIÓN / EVALUATION PROCEDURES

This evaluation was conducted in both English and Spanish across two sessions: 9/25/2025 and October 2, 2025, at the family home and at the Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC clinic office. Procedures included parent interview, structured and unstructured play-based language sampling in both languages, standardized assessment administration, oral-motor examination, and informal speech sound sampling. Lucía Rodríguez Hernández was present for both sessions; Francisco Hernández Ortiz joined by phone for portions of the second session.

RESULTADOS DE LAS PRUEBAS / TEST RESULTS

Standardized and criterion-referenced measures administered are summarized below. Given Mateo's bilingual status, language sampling and select subtests were conducted in both languages, consistent with best practice for dual-language learners.

Test Name | Language | Standard Score | Percentile Rank | Classification
Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax Subtest | Spanish | 76 | 5th | Below Average
Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Morphosyntax Subtest | English | 71 | 3rd | Below Average
Preschool Language Scale-5, Spanish Edition (PLS-5 Spanish), Auditory Comprehension | Spanish | 82 | 12th | Below Average
Preschool Language Scale-5, Spanish Edition (PLS-5 Spanish), Expressive Communication | Spanish | 68 | 2nd | Well Below Average
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3) | English | 73 | 4th | Below Average
Leiter International Performance Scale-3 (Nonverbal Cognitive Screener) | Nonverbal | 94 | 34th | Average

Nonverbal cognitive skills, as measured by the Leiter-3, were within the average range, suggesting that Mateo's language and speech sound difficulties are not attributable to global cognitive delay. Receptive language in Spanish was mildly below average, while expressive language was significantly below average in both languages, consistent with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder affecting both of Mateo's languages rather than a difference attributable to typical bilingual acquisition.

Speech Sound Production

Conversational speech sampling in both languages yielded an estimated intelligibility of approximately 40% to unfamiliar listeners and 65% to familiar listeners (parent estimate). On the GFTA-3, Mateo demonstrated the following error patterns, consistent across both languages:

- Final consonant deletion (e.g., "pato" produced as "pa" for the target /pato/; "sol" produced as "so")
- Stopping of fricatives, with /s/ frequently realized as [t], e.g., target "sapo" produced as "tapo"
- Gliding of liquids, with /r/ realized as [w], e.g., target "perro" produced as "pewo," and English "rabbit" produced as "wabbit"
- Cluster reduction, e.g., "flor" produced as "foh"

In Spanish sampling, Mateo produced "nana" for target "manzana" and "pego" for target "perro," each with mod cues (moderate cueing) required to approximate the target. In English sampling, he produced "tat" for "cat" and "doo" for "shoe." SALT-coded transcription of the Spanish sample noted frequent [EW] (error, word-level) and occasional [FP] (filled pause) codes, consistent with word-finding and production difficulty rather than purely motoric limitations. Target phoneme /k/ was inconsistently achieved, often substituted with [t]; /g/ was similarly fronted. Overall accuracy for word-final consonants was 3/10 correct across both languages, and overall percentage of consonants correct was estimated at 58%, below the expected range for his age.

Oral-Motor and Hearing Status

Oral-motor examination revealed structures and function within normal limits for speech; no evidence of frenulum restriction, asymmetry, or dysarthric features was observed. Diadochokinetic rates were age-appropriate. As noted above, Mateo's most recent hearing screening on 9/18/2025 was within normal limits bilaterally, and there is no current concern for a hearing-based contribution to his speech and language profile, though continued audiological monitoring is recommended given his otitis media history.

Language Sampling and Pragmatics

During play-based sampling, Mateo used primarily single words and occasional two-word combinations (e.g., "más agua," "no quiero") in both languages, with mean length of utterance estimated at 1.8 morphemes in Spanish and 1.6 morphemes in English, both significantly below age expectations (typically 4;7 would be expected to be above 4.0). He demonstrated appropriate eye contact, joint attention, and turn-taking during structured play, and responded to his name and simple one-step directions in both languages. He showed frustration behaviors (gesturing, pulling the examiner's hand) when unable to make himself understood verbally, which is consistent with the pattern described by Ms. Amanda Lopez at Little Sprouts Academy.

IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS / CLINICAL IMPRESSIONS

Based on parent and teacher report, standardized testing in both of Mateo's languages, and direct observation, Mateo presents with a mixed receptive-expressive language disorder (ICD-10 F80.2) and a speech sound disorder (ICD-10 F80.1) affecting both Spanish and English. Because deficits are present and proportionally similar across both languages, this profile is consistent with a true communication disorder rather than a language difference attributable to typical bilingual or second-language acquisition. Nonverbal cognition is a relative strength and should be leveraged in intervention planning. Mateo's history of recurrent otitis media during a critical period of early speech and language development (12–30 months) is a plausible contributing factor, though his current hearing status is within normal limits and does not fully account for the persistence of his difficulties at this point.

Mateo's family provides a rich, supportive bilingual environment, and his sister Paz's frequent interpreting on his behalf, while well-intentioned, may be reducing his opportunities for independent communication attempts in less familiar settings. This should be addressed through family coaching.

RECOMENDACIONES / RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Individual speech-language therapy is recommended twice weekly for 30-minute sessions, delivered in both Spanish and English, focusing on expressive vocabulary growth, early morphosyntax (plurals, verb tense markers), and speech sound targets including final consonants, /s/, /r/, and consonant clusters, in both languages.
2. Continued coordination with Piedmont CDSA and service coordinator Jennifer Alvarez to update the IFSP at the upcoming review on el martes 4 de noviembre de 2025.
3. Family coaching sessions with Lucía Rodríguez Hernández and Francisco Hernández Ortiz to model strategies that encourage Mateo to attempt independent communication before Paz or other family members interpret on his behalf.
4. Consultation with Little Sprouts Academy and Ms. Amanda Lopez to implement simple classroom supports, including visual schedules and structured peer interaction opportunities with classmates such as Ethan Davis.
5. Continued audiological monitoring given Mateo's history of recurrent otitis media; referral back to Dr. Michael Chen if further ear infections occur.
6. Follow-up with pediatrician Dr. Sarah Kim to discuss this report and coordinate ongoing care.
7. Re-evaluation of speech sound and language skills in approximately 6 months, or sooner if significant change is noted, to monitor progress and adjust goals.

This report and its recommendations were discussed with Lucía Rodríguez Hernández and Francisco Hernández Ortiz on October 2, 2025. Both parents verbalized understanding and agreement with the proposed plan. Questions may be directed to the clinic at (704) 555-1190 or kreyes@carolinabilingualslp.com; additional resources are available at www.carolinabilingualslp.com.

Respectfully submitted,

Katherine Reyes, M.S., CCC-SLP
