NORTH CAROLINA INFANT-TODDLER PROGRAM
INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN (IFSP) — ANNUAL REVIEW

Child's Legal Name:  María José Fernández Ortiz      Preferred Name:  Majo      Date of Birth:  March 14, 2024      Sex:  Female
Record ID:  NCITP-884215      Medicaid ID:  729041583A      Primary Language(s):  Spanish, English

Home Address:  1148 Candlewood Lane, Garner, NC  27529      County:  Wake County
Home Phone:  (919) 555-0417      Mother's Cell:  (919) 555-2298      Family Email:  ortizfamilync@gmail.com

Mother/Legal Guardian:  Carmen Ortiz Reyes      Date of Birth:  09/02/1994      Preferred Language:  Spanish
Father/Legal Guardian:  Miguel Fernández Soto      Date of Birth:  1991-11-19      Preferred Language:  Spanish/English
Father's Employer:  Perdue Farms      Work Shift:  3:30 PM–11:30 PM

Household Members:  Sol (sister, age 6), María José (index child), Rosa Reyes (maternal grandmother, lives with family)
Family Pet:  Luna (dog)

Service Coordinator:  Patricia Lin      Agency:  Wake County CDSA      SC Phone:  (919) 555-7740      SC Email:  p.lin@wakecdsa.org
CDSA Office:  Wake County Children's Developmental Services Agency, 2809 Jones Franklin Road, Raleigh, NC  27606

Speech-Language Pathologist:  Elena Castillo Marín, M.S., CCC-SLP      Employer:  Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC
Interpreter present at meeting:  Teresa Vidal (CDSA staff interpreter)

Date of Initial Eligibility Evaluation:  July 22, 2024      Date of Initial IFSP:  August 5, 2024
Date of First Periodic Review:  3 de febrero de 2025      Date of This Annual Review Meeting:  el martes 4 de junio de 2025
Meeting Location:  Wake County CDSA conference room B      Meeting Time:  9:30 AM–11:00 AM
Next Annual Review Due:  2026-06-04

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

María José was born on 14 de marzo de 2024 at WakeMed Faison Women's Hospital at 33 weeks gestation via emergency cesarean section due to placental abruption. Birth weight was 3 lbs 9 oz. She was intubated at delivery and transferred immediately to the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at WakeMed Faison Women's Hospital, where she remained for nineteen days. Her attending neonatologist, Dr. Patricia Nguyen, managed respiratory distress syndrome with surfactant therapy and CPAP support for the first eight days. A grade I intraventricular hemorrhage was identified on cranial ultrasound and resolved without intervention. María José was discharged home on 04/02/2024 on no supplemental oxygen, weighing 4 lbs 11 oz.

Following discharge, her pediatrician, Dr. James Okafor of Garner Pediatric Associates, referred the family to the CDSA on 05/06/2024 due to feeding difficulties and delayed motor milestones noted at the two-month well visit. Carmen Ortiz Reyes reports that María José continued to see a pediatric gastroenterologist, Dr. Lorena Spahn, at UNC Children's Hospital for reflux management through November 2024. No further hospitalizations have occurred since discharge from the NICU.

FAMILY CONCERNS AND PRIORITIES

Carmen and Miguel shared the following during the review meeting, with interpretation provided by Teresa Vidal. Carmen stated, "Nuestra prioridad es que Majo pueda decir lo que necesita sin frustrarse tanto." She elaborated that María José currently uses pointing, pulling on an adult's hand, and a small set of approximated words, but becomes distressed when she cannot make herself understood, particularly with her older sister Sol. Miguel added in English, "At daycare they say she understands everything, but at home with us it feels different sometimes, especially when we switch between Spanish and English."

The family's priorities, in their own words, included:
1. "Que aprenda más palabras en español y en inglés, las dos cosas." (That she learns more words in Spanish and English, both.)
2. "Que coma mejor — todavía se ahoga con texturas gruesas." (That she eats better — she still chokes on thicker textures.)
3. "Queremos entender qué podemos hacer en casa, no solo en terapia." (We want to understand what we can do at home, not only in therapy.)
4. Miguel noted a wish for more written home strategies he could review after his evening shift at Perdue Farms, since he is often not present for daytime sessions.

Rosa Reyes, who cares for María José several mornings a week while Carmen attends ESL classes, also voiced a concern through the interpreter: she worries that María José "se enoja mucho cuando no la entendemos" (gets very angry when we don't understand her), and asked for guidance on simple signs or gestures the whole household could use consistently.

DAILY ROUTINES

María José wakes most mornings around 6:45 AM and is cared for by Rosa or Carmen until 8:30 AM, when she attends Little Sprouts Early Learning Center on weekdays. Her lead teacher there, Ms. Danielle Rivera, reports that María José participates well in circle time and enjoys imitating songs, though her peer group — including a close friend, Noah, and another classmate, Isabella — often speaks for her when she struggles to respond quickly.

Mealtimes remain a focus area. Breakfast is typically oatmeal or scrambled eggs, which María José tolerates well; lunch at daycare and dinner at home both include rice, beans, and softened vegetables, but the family reports gagging with firmer textures such as whole grapes or raw carrot. Carmen mentioned that bath time, around 7:00 PM, is a favorite routine where María José is most verbal, often attempting to name body parts and bath toys. Bedtime routine includes a shared book in Spanish, usually read by Rosa or Carmen, followed by lights out near 8:15 PM.

Weekends are spent largely at home or visiting extended family in Fuquay-Varina. Sol is described as María José's primary playmate and frequently "translates" her sister's attempts at words to adults, which the team discussed as both supportive and potentially limiting independent communication attempts.

OTHER AGENCIES INVOLVED

The family currently receives support from the following agencies in addition to the CDSA:
WIC Program:  Wake County WIC — nutrition counseling related to feeding and texture progression, last visit 05/14/2025
Smart Start:  Smart Start of Wake County — childcare subsidy coordination, renewal application submitted 2025-04-01
Early Intervention OT:  contracted through Wake County CDSA, sessions provided by Hannah Oduya, OTR/L
DSS Involvement:  none at this time; no open case

PRESENT LEVELS OF DEVELOPMENT (Speech-Language)

Assessment conducted by Elena Castillo Marín on May 20, 2025 using the Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (bilingual administration, caregiver report plus direct observation) and the PLS-5 Spanish. Chronological age at testing: 14 months adjusted for prematurity (corrected age); chronological age 15;0.

Expressive language: María José produces approximately 12 consistent word approximations across both languages, including "mamá," "pa" for Miguel, "agua," "más," and "no." She combines gesture with vocalization 8/10 opportunities observed. Receptive language is a relative strength; she follows simple one-step directions in both Spanish and English (e.g., "dame el vaso," "give me the cup") on 9/10 trials.

Oral-motor/feeding: mild hypotonia of the perioral musculature noted; gagging observed with cubed firm textures; no overt signs of aspiration. Reflux well controlled per report. Phonetic inventory includes /m/, /p/, /a/, /o/, with emerging /t/ and [w] in word-initial position; final consonants are largely omitted (e.g., "ba" for "bath").

Social communication: María José initiates joint attention and requests through pointing and vocalization; shared affect is appropriate for age. Frustration tolerance is reduced when communication attempts are not understood, consistent with family report.

OUTCOMES AND STRATEGIES

Outcome 1: María José will increase her expressive vocabulary to 50 functional words across Spanish and English, used spontaneously across at least two settings (home and daycare), by June 2026.
Strategies: Weekly bilingual home-strategy sheets provided to Carmen, Miguel, and Rosa; use of core vocabulary boards during mealtime and bath time; coaching Ms. Rivera on honoring wait-time before peers (including Noah) respond for María José.

Outcome 2: María José will tolerate and self-feed age-appropriate mixed textures (soft-cubed foods) without gagging on 4 out of 5 consecutive meals, by December 2025.
Strategies: Collaboration with Wake County WIC on texture progression; oral-motor exercises modeled for family during home visits; joint session with OT provider Hannah Oduya scheduled for 06/18/2025.

Outcome 3: The family will report increased confidence using at least three consistent gestures or simple signs at home to reduce María José's frustration, as measured by caregiver report at the next review.
Strategies: Direct coaching of Rosa Reyes during Tuesday morning sessions; written sign reference sheet in Spanish provided to household; check-in phone call with Miguel arranged for 07/01/2025 given his evening work schedule at Perdue Farms.

Outcome 4 (carried forward, modified): María José will combine two words to request or comment ("más agua," "no quiero") in 50% of observed communicative opportunities by the next annual review.
Strategies: Continued bilingual intervention emphasizing both languages equally per family preference; expansion modeling of single-word attempts; coordination with Little Sprouts Early Learning Center staff on classroom carryover.

SERVICE DELIVERY

Service:  Speech-Language Therapy      Frequency:  60 min, 1x/week      Location:  Home      Provider:  Elena Castillo Marín      Agency:  Carolina Bilingual Therapy Services, PLLC      Start Date:  August 12, 2024
Service:  Occupational Therapy      Frequency:  45 min, 1x/week      Location:  Little Sprouts Early Learning Center      Provider:  Hannah Oduya      Start Date:  September 3, 2024
Service:  Service Coordination      Frequency:  monthly contact, 90-day face-to-face review      Provider:  Patricia Lin      Agency:  Wake County CDSA
Transportation Assistance:  Not required; family has reliable transportation
Natural Environment Justification:  All services delivered in home and childcare setting consistent with routines-based model; no center-based services recommended at this time.

TRANSITION PLANNING

Given María José's date of birth of 14-03-2024, transition planning conversations will begin no later than September 2026 in preparation for potential transition to Preschool Exceptional Children's services or continuation of community-based supports. Patricia Lin will coordinate with Wake County Public Schools Exceptional Children's Division closer to the transition conference date.

Piedmont CDSA – North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program
IFSP REVIEW / Revisión del IFSP

Child/Niño: Mateo Alejandro Vázquez Ruiz ("Teo") DOB 04/11/2024 (approx 2;6 at this review)
Child ID: IT-048317  Medicaid #: 920471836C
Address: 214 Sweetgum Lane, Hickory, Catawba County, NC 28601
Mamá/Mother: Lucía Rodríguez  Papá/Father: Carlos Vázquez
Phone: (828) 555-0142  Email: lucia.rodriguez84@gmail.com
Service Coordinator: Brenda Hale, Piedmont CDSA, Hickory office
IFSP Review Date: October 8, 2026  Initial IFSP: January 14, 2026
Report by: Daniela Ortiz-Byrne, MS, CCC-SLP (bilingüe), Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners

Antecedentes / Background:
Pt is a 2;6 Spanish/English bilingual tod'r referred by Dr. Nguyen at Catawba Valley Pediatrics for delayed expressive lang. Family home language is primarily español; CG report mixed input in el hogar w/ older sibs modeling English. Pt lives w/ mamá, papá, hermana mayor Sol (age 7), and hermano Diego (age 4). Familia also has a dog, Luna, que el pt adora — CG reports pt points & vocalizes to Luna freq.

Preocupaciones y Prioridades de la Familia (Family Concerns & Priorities, en sus propias palabras):
Mamá Lucía reports, "No entiendo por qué mi hijo no habla todavía — sus primos hablaban mucho más a esta edad." CG also shared, "Me preocupa que cuando empiece pre-k no lo van a entender ni en inglés ni en español." Papá Carlos added via interpreter, "I just want him to be able to tell us what he wants — right now everything es puro llanto y señas."
Prioridades:
1. Pt will use more words (bilingual) to request items at home & daycare.
2. Family wants strategies for both idiomas so pt no se confunda ("no se atrase en ninguno de los dos").
3. CG wants pt understood by Sol and Diego w/o constant "¿qué dijo?"

Rutinas Diarias / Daily Routines:
Mom works nights at Catawba Valley Regional Medical Center as a CNA (approx 11p-7a shifts, 4x/wk); papá works days at a local furniture plant. B/c of mom's schedule, pt's primary daytime CG during the week is his babysitter, Yolanda Castañeda, a neighbor who has watched him since infancy ("es como su abuela," per mamá). Pt attends Little Sprouts Daycare on 9th Ave in Hickory M-F 8a-1p while Yolanda has her own medical appts. Morning routine: wakes approx 6:45 AM, breakfast w/ Sol & Diego before school bus; pt loves pan dulce and will point/vocalize "pa" for "pan." Bath time is a high-engagement routine — CG reports best vocal play occurs then. Bedtime routine w/ papá incl. looking at pics of family & naming (mod cues) "Luna," "Sol" (hermana), "mamá."

Nota clínica sobre blancos de tx: durante sesión del 09/22/2026 se trabajaron palabras CV simples incl. "sol" /sol/ como blanco fonológico (referencia al sol, no a la hermana) junto a "pan," "no," "más." Pt produjo "so" (approx) x2/5 ensayos w/ mod cues; distinguir claramente en notas futuras entre el blanco léxico "sol" y la hermana del pt para evitar confusión en el registro.

Otras Agencias / Other Agencies Involved:
- WIC — family receives nutrition supplement, recert due November 2026.
- Smart Start of Catawba County — referred family to playgroup resources.
- DSS — no open case; family contacted for childcare subsidy app, pending.
- Catawba Valley Pediatrics — Dr. Nguyen, PCP, last well-check 08/03/2026.
- Audiology cleared via Piedmont CDSA contracted audiologist Marisol Pham — passed OAE bilateral 02/01/2026.

Present Levels / Resultados de Evaluación:
Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (readministered 09/15/2026): receptive lang age equiv approx 15 mo (pt CA 2;5 at testing); expressive lang age equiv approx 12 mo. Significant delay both domains, more pronounced expressive.
Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (screener, Spanish phoneme inventory noted informally — not yet normed in español at this CDSA): limited consonant inventory /m, p, n/; mostly vocalic approximations.
Bayley-4 (Cognitive & Motor subtests, admin by Dr. Patel, developmental pediatrician): Cognitive composite in avg range; Fine/Gross Motor WNL. Confirms delay is specific to communication, not global.
Peabody Picture Vocabulary Test-5: not administered — pt below minimum testable age; will attempt at next annual.
MLU (SALT-coded sample, home visit 09/22/2026): 1.1 morphemes; single-word utterances predominant, several w/ jargon [EW] codes noted during sample. Intelligibility to unfamiliar listener approx 10% in Spanish, <5% in English.
Play skills: symbolic play emerging (feeds Luna's stuffed look-alike, pretend phone to ear saying "¿bueno?" — a nice functional phrase approximation).
Social: at daycare pt engages mostly w/ classmate Bryson, who is verbal & often "translates" pt's gestures to teacher Ms. Alvarado. Ms. Alvarado reports pt follows routine 1-step directions w/ visual cues, mod success.

Bystander/Family Context Notes:
Pt has two cousins, Emily (6) and Josué (4), who visit on weekends per mamá — "mis sobrinos hablan muy bien, y eso me hace comparar a Mateo, pero sé que no debo." This comparison noted for CG counseling re: bilingual development trajectories being typical, not delayed, purely due to dual exposure — pt's delay appears to be a true primary lang impairment pattern per combined Rossetti/MLU/parent report data, not bilingual-typical variation.

Outcomes & Strategies / Resultados y Estrategias:

Outcome 1: Mateo will use 2-word combinations (en cualquier idioma, CG's choice) to request & comment during 3/4 observed routines by next review.
Strategies: CG & Yolanda trained in expansion technique — repeat pt's attempt + 1 word, modeled both English & español w/ consistency per speaker (mamá español, papá mixed per report, babysitter español). SLP to model "mas pan," "no quiero," "mira Luna" during tx sessions w/ mod-to-max cues fading to indirect verbal cues over the quarter. Home program sent in español w/ picture supports.

Outcome 2: Family will report increased confidence identifying communication attempts across both idiomas.
Strategies: Bilingual language sample reviewed w/ family qtrly; interpreter not required this visit as SLP conducts bilingually; Brenda Hale (SC) to coordinate shared folder of home-program videos w/ family via secure link.

Outcome 3: Mateo will increase phonemic inventory to incl. /t, k, s/ in CV/VC shapes across 3 sessions, generalized to home per CG report.
Strategies: Minimal pairs & babbling expansion drills; target word "sol" continued as motivating CV+C blend practice (distinct from hermana's name per clinical note above — SLP flagged this homophony risk to CG, who found it "chistoso pero un poco confuso," and family agreed to call hermana "Solcito" during tx sessions specifically to reduce ambiguity for pt and for documentation clarity going forward).

Service Delivery:
SLP direct tx: 2x/wk, 45 min, home-based (per family preference given mom's night shifts; sessions scheduled midday to catch pt at best alertness, coordinated around Little Sprouts Daycare pickup).
DT (Developmental Therapy): 1x/wk, 60 min, provided by Hannah Weir, DT, co-treat w/ SLP monthly.
Service coordination: Brenda Hale to conduct 90-day check-in January 7, 2027.
Next annual IFSP: due by January 14, 2027; next 6-mo review April 8, 2027.

Transition Planning Note:
Family counseled re: eligibility continuum — if pt continues to qualify, transition planning conference will begin approx 6 mo prior to 3rd birthday (April 11, 2027 target window). SC explained local school district referral process (Catawba County Schools Child Find) will be initiated per family consent closer to that date; no action needed at this time.

Additional Notes / Notas Adicionales:
Mamá Lucía expressed gratitude for bilingual services: "Qué bueno que hable español conmigo, porque a veces con otros terapeutas yo no entendía bien qué me estaban pidiendo que hiciera en casa." SLP reinforced that both idiomas support, not hinder, pt's overall lang development; provided handout (Spanish/English) on bilingual milestones from Piedmont CDSA family resource library.

CG also asked re: possible hearing re-check given fluctuating attention during sessions; SLP noted pt passed audiology 02/01/2026 but will flag for SC to monitor and reassess if attention concerns persist by next review, incl. possible ENT referral through Catawba Valley Pediatrics.

REASON FOR REFERRAL

Teo is a 4-year, 7-month-old bilingual (Spanish/English) boy referred for a comprehensive speech-language evaluation by the Piedmont CDSA Office following a concern raised by his daycare teacher, la maestra Carmen, and by his mother, Lucía Rodríguez-Vega, regarding delayed and unclear speech. The family was referred to this clinic through Early Head Start, where Teo was previously enrolled before transitioning to Little Sprouts Early Learning Center. Service coordination is provided by Tom Wachowski, who coordinated scheduling with the family and arranged for a Spanish-English interpreter, Patricia Gómez, to be present for both sessions. The evaluation took place across two visits, el lunes 22 de septiembre de 2026 and 29 de septiembre de 2026, at the request of the family's pediatrician and the CDSA service coordinator, who noted that Teo's intelligibility had not improved despite being enrolled in daycare for over a year.

BIRTH AND MEDICAL HISTORY

Mateo was born at 37 weeks gestation at Cabarrus Valley Medical Center on 03/14/2021 via scheduled cesarean section due to breech presentation. Birth weight was reported as 6 lbs, 4 oz. Mrs. de la Cruz reported an uncomplicated pregnancy with regular prenatal care through the WIC program, which the family also used for nutritional support during Teo's infancy. No NICU stay was required, and Teo was discharged home with his mother on March 16, 2021. Developmental milestones for gross motor skills (sitting, walking) were reported as within normal limits, with independent walking achieved around 13 months. Fine motor skills were also reported as age-appropriate.

Lucía reported a history of frequent ear infections between ages 1 and 3, with at least six documented episodes treated with antibiotics by the family's pediatrician. Tympanostomy tubes were placed on the 4th of June, 2024 (el martes 4 de junio) at an ENT clinic following a referral triggered by a failed hearing screening at a well-child visit. A follow-up hearing evaluation on 07/18/2024 showed normal hearing bilaterally with the tubes in place. No additional surgeries, hospitalizations, or significant illnesses were reported. Teo's vision was last screened at his 4-year well-child visit and was reported as normal. There is no known family history of autism, intellectual disability, or genetic syndromes; however, Mr. de la Cruz reported that his own brother was a "late talker" and did not begin combining words until close to age 4.

FAMILY, SOCIAL, AND LANGUAGE HISTORY

Teo lives with his mother, Lucía Rodríguez-Vega; his father, Tomás de la Cruz; and his older brother, Diego, age 7, at the family's home in Concord, Cabarrus County. The family also has a dog, Rocky, whom Teo frequently mentions during play-based interactions. Teo's maternal grandmother, referred to by the family as doña Lupe, provides after-school and weekend childcare and has lived with the family intermittently since 2023. Doña Lupe speaks primarily Spanish and reports spending several hours daily engaged in verbal play, storytelling, and household routines with Teo.

The home language environment is described as predominantly Spanish, with Lucía estimating that approximately 70% of input at home is in Spanish and 30% in English, largely driven by Diego's school-based English use at home. Tomás works full-time at Carolina Fresh Poultry Processing on the evening shift and reports speaking to Teo primarily in Spanish during the limited time they have together in the mornings. Lucía works part-time as a cashier and is the primary daytime caregiver on days Teo is not in daycare.

Teo began attending Little Sprouts Early Learning Center in January 2025 after transitioning out of the Early Head Start program, which the family accessed through a referral from Cabarrus County DSS when Teo was an infant. At daycare, instruction is delivered primarily in English. Teo's classroom teacher, la maestra Carmen, reports that he is social and eager to interact with peers but is frequently difficult to understand, which has led to frustration during group activities. The assistant teacher, Miss Ana, echoed similar concerns, noting that Teo often resorts to pointing or physical gestures rather than verbal requests when peers do not understand him. One peer in particular, Sofía, has reportedly become Teo's preferred playmate and often "translates" his requests to other classmates and staff.

The family's involvement with Smart Start of Cabarrus County began earlier this year when Lucía attended a parent workshop on early language development, which prompted her to request this evaluation. Lucía reported that she had previously raised concerns about Teo's speech with his pediatrician around his second birthday but was told to "wait and see," which contributed to the delay in seeking a formal evaluation.

BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATIONS

During both evaluation sessions, Teo presented as a friendly, curious child who separated easily from his mother and engaged readily with this examiner and with the interpreter, Patricia Gómez. He demonstrated age-appropriate play skills, including symbolic play with toy animals and a pretend kitchen set, and engaged in reciprocal turn-taking during structured and unstructured tasks. Attention and engagement were adequate for the duration of both sessions, though some redirection was needed during longer verbal tasks.

Speech intelligibility was notably reduced in connected speech, estimated at approximately 40% for unfamiliar listeners and 65% for familiar listeners (parent report), consistent with concerns raised by la maestra Carmen and Lucía. Teo was observed to use a limited consonant inventory, with frequent final consonant deletion (e.g., "ca" for "cat"), cluster reduction ("poon" for "spoon"), and gliding of liquids (e.g., "wed" for "red," producing /w/ for /r/). In Spanish, similar patterns were observed, with simplification of consonant clusters in words like "problema," produced as [poblema], and difficulty with the trilled /r/ sound. Teo was stimulable for several target sounds with moderate cueing, achieving correct productions of /k/ and /g/ in isolation with mod cues during structured drill tasks.

ASSESSMENT PROCEDURES AND RESULTS

The following standardized and informal measures were administered in both English and Spanish, with input from the interpreter, Patricia Gómez, to ensure accurate administration and scoring in both languages.

Standardized Measures:

| Measure | Language | Standard Score | Percentile Rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation–3 (GFTA-3) | English | 72 | 3rd |
| Clinical Evaluation of Language Fundamentals Preschool-3 (CELF Preschool-3), Core Language | English | 79 | 8th |
| Preschool Language Scales-5 (PLS-5), Spanish-Bilingual Edition | Spanish/English | 68 | 2nd |
| Bilingual English-Spanish Assessment (BESA), Phonology Subtest | Spanish | 70 | 2nd |
| Expressive Vocabulary Test-3 (EVT-3) | English | 76 | 5th |

Oral mechanism examination revealed adequate structure and function for speech purposes, with no evidence of structural abnormality, dysarthria, or apraxia-related symptoms. Diadochokinetic rates were judged to be within age expectations.

Spontaneous language samples were collected in both English and Spanish during play-based interaction. In English, Teo produced primarily 2- to 3-word utterances (e.g., "I want that," "dog go outside"), with occasional 4-word combinations. Mean length of utterance in morphemes (MLU-m) was calculated at 2.8, below the expected range for his chronological age. SALT coding of the sample identified frequent omission of grammatical morphemes, coded as [EW] for several utterances involving omitted copula "is" (e.g., "he happy" for "he is happy"). In Spanish, utterances were similarly limited in length and complexity, with omission of articles and inconsistent verb conjugation (e.g., "yo quiero ir" produced as "yo queer ir").

Articulation testing revealed a moderate phonological disorder affecting both languages, with phonological processes including final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, gliding, and stopping of fricatives. Target word probes elicited productions such as "sun" produced as [tʊn] and "shoe" produced as [tu], with the fricative /ʃ/ consistently realized as [t]. In quoted productions, Teo was able to approximate the word "casa" as "tasa" and "perro" as "peo," demonstrating difficulty with the trilled /r/ phoneme. Stimulability testing showed that Teo could approximate several target sounds with moderate cueing, including /s/ and /ʃ/ in isolation, though not yet in connected speech.

Receptive and expressive vocabulary in both languages fell within the low-average to below-average range, with notably stronger vocabulary in Spanish for home and family-related concepts and stronger vocabulary in English for daycare and school-related concepts, consistent with the bilingual language environment described by the family.

IMPRESSIONS

Based on parent and teacher report, direct observation, and standardized and informal assessment results, Teo presents with a moderate speech sound disorder affecting intelligibility in both English and Spanish, alongside a mild-to-moderate expressive and receptive language delay in both languages. Because deficits are present and proportionally similar across both of Teo's languages, this profile is consistent with a true communication disorder rather than a language difference attributable to typical bilingual development or reduced exposure to either language. Teo's strengths include strong social engagement, intact play skills, adequate oral-motor structure and function, and stimulability for several error sounds with cueing support, all of which are positive prognostic indicators for therapy.

The history of chronic otitis media with effusion, treated with tympanostomy tubes placed on June 4, 2024, may have contributed to early speech sound development delays, though current hearing status is reported as normal. Teo's rich home language environment, supported by his mother, father, and grandmother (doña Lupe), provides a strong foundation for bilingual intervention, and his family's engagement with community supports, including WIC, Smart Start, and Cabarrus County DSS, reflects a supportive and resourceful family system.

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Teo qualifies for speech-language therapy services based on standardized testing, clinical observation, and significant parent and teacher concern, meeting criteria for both articulation/phonology and expressive/receptive language impairment in both English and Spanish.

2. Individual speech-language therapy is recommended at a frequency of two sessions per week, 30 minutes each, provided in both English and Spanish to the extent possible, with goals targeting phonological processes (final consonant deletion, cluster reduction, gliding, stopping), expanding utterance length and grammatical morpheme use, and increasing overall intelligibility across both languages.

3. Continued coordination with Piedmont CDSA Office and service coordinator Tom Wachowski is recommended to ensure services are reflected in Teo's IFSP, with the next IFSP review meeting recommended for December 2026 to assess progress and discuss transition planning ahead of his third birthday... [note: chronological age noted above reflects current status; transition planning should instead focus on kindergarten entry given his age].

4. Collaboration with Little Sprouts Early Learning Center staff, including la maestra Carmen and Miss Ana, is recommended to support carryover of therapy targets into the classroom setting, including use of visual supports and peer modeling strategies with classmates such as Sofía.

5. Home practice strategies were discussed with Lucía Rodríguez-Vega and doña Lupe, including modeling target sounds during daily routines and expanding Teo's utterances during shared book reading in both Spanish and English.

6. A hearing re-screening is recommended within the next 6 months given Teo's history of chronic ear infections, to be coordinated through his primary care provider.

7. Re-evaluation of progress is recommended in approximately 6 months, or sooner if requested by the family, daycare staff, or service coordinator.

This evaluation and report were completed with the assistance of a qualified Spanish-English interpreter, Patricia Gómez, to ensure accurate communication with the family throughout both sessions.

Respectfully submitted,

Alejandra Ferris, M.S., CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Bilingual Speech & Language Services, PLLC
Report completed: October 3, 2026

Piedmont Regional CDSA
1215 Westover Terrace, Greensboro, Guilford County, NC 27408
Teléfono de la oficina / Office phone: (336) 555-0142 • Fax: 336-555-0199

10 de octubre de 2025

Estimada familia Cruz Hernández / Dear Cruz Hernández Family,

Les escribo para resumir, in English and en español, lo que hablamos en la reunión de revisión del IFSP de Mateo el martes 4 de junio de 2025, y para dejarles por escrito los próximos pasos. Thank you both, Lucía Fernanda Cruz Hernández and Josué Cruz Ramírez, for making time to meet with me and with your service coordinator, Ms. Brenda Watts, during such a busy week. I know Josué had to shift a delivery route to be there, and I am grateful. Su hijo, a quien ustedes llaman cariñosamente "Teo," cumplió 2;3 años el mes pasado (nació el 3 de marzo de 2023), and this review covers his progress since the last IFSP meeting on 01/14/2025.

Información de la familia / Family Information

Child's full name: Mateo Alejandro Cruz Hernández, Date of birth: March 3, 2023, IFSP record #: IFSP-2025-04417, Medicaid ID: 998271534K.

Mateo vive con su mamá Lucía, su papá Josué, y su hermana mayor, Ximena Cruz Hernández, quien tiene seis años y va a primer grado en Guilford Park Elementary. En casa también los ayuda mucho la abuela materna, Rosa Hernández, quien vive a dos cuadras y cuida a Mateo los días que su mamá trabaja. La familia también cuenta con una niñera de confianza, Carmen Osorio, quien llega los martes y jueves por la tarde. La familia tiene un perrito llamado Max que, según cuenta Lucía, "a Mateo le encanta jugar con Max en el patio."

Address on file: 4420 Shady Grove Lane, Greensboro, NC 27406. Home phone: 336-555-0871; mom's cell: (336) 555-0273; dad's cell: 336.555.0456. La familia también nos dio el número de la abuela paterna, quien vive en Honduras y a veces ayuda por videollamada con el cuidado de Mateo: +504 9988-7766. Un número adicional, de un tío que vive en México y que a veces visita en diciembre, es +52 55 1234 5678.

Inquietudes y prioridades de la familia, en sus propias palabras / Family Concerns and Priorities (in the family's own words)

Durante la reunión, Lucía compartió lo siguiente: "Lo que más me preocupa es que Mateo no me dice lo que quiere, y a veces hace rabietas porque no lo entendemos. Él señala y grita, pero no usa muchas palabras." She also said, in English, "I want him to be able to tell his sister what he wants, not just cry or hit her." Josué added, "Yo trabajo mucho, pero cuando estoy en casa quiero jugar con él y que me entienda cuando le digo cosas simples, como 'ven aquí' o 'dame la pelota.'"

Family priorities identified at this review:

1. Mateo will use more words, in either English or Spanish, to ask for things he wants instead of crying or pointing only.
2. La familia quiere estrategias para apoyar el desarrollo bilingüe de Mateo sin "confundirlo," como dijo Lucía, "porque la doctora en la clínica me dijo que hablarle dos idiomas lo iba a atrasar, y yo no sé si eso es cierto."
3. Ximena necesita herramientas para jugar con su hermano sin frustrarse cuando él no le responde.
4. The family would like Mateo to be better understood by his daycare teachers so that he can participate more in circle time and snack routines.

Rutinas diarias / Daily Routines

Mateo se despierta alrededor de las 7:00 a.m. y desayuna con su familia antes de que Lucía lo lleve a Little Lambs Early Head Start Center a las 8:15 a.m. Su maestra principal, el Sr. Danh Tran, reporta que Mateo juega bien al lado de otros niños, especially his classmate Ava Whitfield, pero rara vez inicia el juego verbalmente. Durante el almuerzo, a eso de las 11:30 a.m., Mateo señala la comida que quiere en lugar de nombrarla. Por las tardes, Josué o la abuela Rosa lo recogen cerca de las 4:30 p.m., y la familia cena junta alrededor de las 6:00 p.m. "Es el momento del día en que más habla," dijo Lucía, "porque está contento de ver a todos."

El baño es a las 7:30 p.m. y la rutina de dormir incluye dos cuentos, uno en inglés y uno en español, que Josué le lee cuando llega a tiempo del trabajo. La familia describe esta rutina como el mejor momento para practicar palabras nuevas, since Mateo is most relaxed and attentive then.

Otras agencias involucradas / Other Agencies Involved

La familia recibe apoyo de varias agencias además de este CDSA:

- Guilford County DSS administra la asistencia de cuidado infantil (childcare subsidy) que ayuda a pagar Little Lambs Early Head Start Center. The family's caseworker there is Ms. Keisha Thornton, reachable at 336-555-0398.
- La familia participa en WIC (Women, Infants, and Children) desde que nació Ximena, y sigue recibiendo cupones de alimentos en la oficina de Greensboro.
- Smart Start of Guilford County ayudó a conectar a la familia con Little Lambs Early Head Start Center y les proporcionó materiales de lectura bilingüe el año pasado.
- El programa federal Early Head Start financia parte del cupo de Mateo en el centro de cuidado.
- El pediatra de Mateo, la Dra. Amara Chen, de Cone Health Pediatrics at Wendover, completó la evaluación médica requerida el 02/10/2025 y no reportó preocupaciones auditivas ni motoras.
- Mateo también ve a una terapeuta ocupacional, Jenna Whitfield, OTR/L, los miércoles para trabajar en integración sensorial; sus notas se comparten con este equipo con el permiso de la familia.

Resultados de la evaluación / Present Levels of Development

Esta servidora, Marisol Delgado Peña, MS, CCC-SLP, bilingual speech-language pathologist with Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services, PLLC, completó la reevaluación de lenguaje el 28 de mayo de 2025 con la interpretación de Ana Beltrán, interpreter certified through Piedmont Regional CDSA.

On the Preschool Language Scales, Fifth Edition (PLS-5), Spanish-English bilingual form, Mateo obtained a standard score of 72 on the Auditory Comprehension subtest (3rd percentile) and a standard score of 68 on the Expressive Communication subtest (2nd percentile), both more than 1.5 standard deviations below the mean for his age. On the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), he produced target consonants correctly in 6/10 opportunities at the word level, with the most consistent errors on /k/ and /g/, which he frequently fronted to [t] and [d] (e.g., target "gato" produced as [ˈtato]). Spontaneous language sample analysis, coded in SALT, showed a mean length of utterance of 1.4 morphemes and frequent code-switching within utterances, marked [CS] in the transcript (e.g., "quiero [CS] water," "mas [CS] please"), which is developmentally appropriate for a bilingual toddler and not itself a disorder marker.

During structured play, Mateo requested preferred items with moderate verbal cues approximately 40% of the time, improving to 70% with simultaneous Spanish and English verbal models. He imitated the target word "agua" as [ˈwawa] and "más" as [ˈmas] with minimal cues. These findings are consistent with a mixed receptive-expressive language delay in both of Mateo's languages, which supports continued eligibility for Part C services and does not reflect simple bilingual exposure, contrary to the concern Lucía mentioned above.

I explained to the family, using the interpreter, that children raised bilingually do not experience language delay "because of" two languages; research consistently shows no such causal link, and that Mateo's profile shows delay across both languages, which is the pattern we would expect to see and treat regardless of how many languages he hears at home. Lucía seemed relieved to hear this and said, "Entonces puedo seguir hablándole español en casa," to which I responded that yes, continuing Spanish at home is strongly recommended and will support, not hinder, his progress in English.

Resultados y estrategias / Outcomes and Strategies

Outcome 1: Mateo will use 2-word combinations in Spanish and/or English to request desired objects or activities during daily routines, in at least 8 of 10 observed opportunities, by the next IFSP review.

Strategies: Family will model short phrases ("quiero más," "want ball") during meals and play rather than single words; Rosa and Josué will use the same bilingual expansion technique so modeling is consistent across caregivers; daycare staff, including Mr. Tran, will offer forced-choice questions ("¿agua o leche? / water or milk?") during snack time to elicit verbal requests rather than accepting pointing.

Outcome 2: Mateo will use at least 10 new single words functionally across both home and daycare settings, documented by parent and teacher report, within the next three months.

Strategies: Continue weekly direct speech therapy sessions targeting /k/ and /g/ production in structured and naturalistic contexts; family to practice target words identified in session using the home program provided in both English and Spanish; Ximena will be coached briefly during sessions on how to wait and model rather than answer for her brother, to give Mateo space to attempt words himself.

Outcome 3: Mateo will participate in one structured turn-taking game with a peer at daycare, such as rolling a ball back and forth with Ava, for at least 5 consecutive turns, by the next review date.

Strategies: Daycare staff will set up small-group play with no more than two peers at a time; Jenna Whitfield will coordinate with speech services so that sensory regulation strategies are in place before language-based play tasks, since Mateo regulates better when he has had movement breaks first.

Servicios y fechas / Services and Dates

Speech-language therapy: individual sessions, 30 minutes, twice weekly, in the home and at Little Lambs Early Head Start Center, billed under CPT code 92523 (evaluation) and 92507 (treatment). Current authorization period: 06/01/2025 through 11/30/2025. Occupational therapy: 45 minutes weekly, continuing as previously authorized. Service coordination: Ms. Watts will continue monthly contact and will coordinate the next annual IFSP meeting, tentatively scheduled for el martes 2 de diciembre de 2025, at the Piedmont Regional CDSA office or by videollamada if the family prefers.

The family also asked about transition planning, since Mateo will turn three on 03/03/2026. We discussed that the transition conference must occur at least 90 days before that date, and I will coordinate with Watts and the local school system to schedule this no later than 01/05/2026. Ms. Watts will send a separate letter regarding transition rights closer to that date.

Nota sobre contacto / Contact Note

If the family has questions before our next visit, please call my direct line at 336-555-0117 or email me at m.delgado@carolinapediatrictherapy.com. You may also reach Ms. Watts at 336-555-0142 ext. 214, or by email at b.watts@piedmontcdsa.org. For general questions about Early Head Start enrollment, the center director can be reached at (336) 555-0920. The Guilford County DSS childcare subsidy line is 336-555-0677, and WIC appointments can be scheduled at 336-555-0455.

Please remember that your next home visit is scheduled for el jueves 19 de junio de 2025 at 4:00 p.m., and your daycare-based session is scheduled for 06/23/2025 at 10:30 a.m. I will bring updated home practice materials in both English and Spanish at that time.

Gracias de nuevo, Lucía y Josué, por su compromiso y cariño hacia Mateo. It has been a pleasure to watch him grow, and I look forward to celebrating his progress with your family, including Ximena and abuela Rosa, at our next visit. Un saludo afectuoso,

Marisol Delgado Peña, MS, CCC-SLP
Bilingual Speech-Language Pathologist
Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services, PLLC
On behalf of the Mateo Alejandro Cruz Hernández IFSP Team

Review meeting date: el martes 4 de junio de 2025

This review was completed following a face-to-face meeting at the family's home on June 4, 2025, attended by Lucía Castillo Ramírez, Javier Fernández Soto, Service Coordinator Ana Gutiérrez, physical therapist Mark Davis, DPT, occupational therapist Sarah Kim, OTR/L, and this bilingual speech-language pathologist, Jennifer Lowe, M.S., CCC-SLP, of Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services. The meeting was conducted in a mix of English and Spanish per the family's preference; this writer served as interpreter when needed, though both parents are comfortable code-switching.

Antecedentes familiares / Family Background: María José vive con sus dos padres y dos hermanos en 1847 Yadkin Road, Fayetteville, en Cumberland County. Her older brother, Diego Fernández Castillo, is six years old and attends first grade; her baby sister, Camila Fernández Castillo, is one year old. La familia también tiene un perrito llamado Max que María José adora y menciona frecuentemente durante las sesiones. Javier works full-time at Southern Fasteners Inc., and Lucía works part-time housekeeping at Holiday Inn Express on weekends while her mother-in-law, Rosa Soto Mendoza, helps with childcare. The home language is primarily Spanish, with English introduced through daycare and television. Both parents report feeling comfortable speaking either language with María José, though they note she responds more consistently in Spanish at home and is beginning to use some English words learned at daycare.

María José attends Little Explorers Child Development Center on Yadkin Road four days per week from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. while her parents work. Her teacher there, Ms. Brianna Holt, reports that María José has made progress interacting with peers but still struggles to be understood, particularly by classmates who do not speak Spanish. One peer in particular, Noah, has become a close friend and often tries to interpret for her during play, according to Ms. Holt.

Preocupaciones y prioridades de la familia, en sus propias palabras: During the review, Lucía shared, "Quiero que mi hija pueda decirme lo que necesita sin frustrarse. A veces llora porque no puede decirme qué le duele o qué quiere comer, y eso me rompe el corazón." (I want my daughter to be able to tell me what she needs without getting frustrated. Sometimes she cries because she can't tell me what hurts or what she wants to eat, and that breaks my heart.) Javier added, "Nos preocupa que no la entiendan en la guardería, que los otros niños se burlen o que ella se quede callada porque siente que nadie la entiende." (We're worried they don't understand her at daycare, that the other kids will tease her or that she'll stay quiet because she feels like no one understands her.) Both parents also expressed a desire for María José to be ready for kindergarten enrollment, noting that Diego had a much easier time with language development and they want to understand whether her difficulties are related to being raised bilingual or something more.

This writer explained, en términos sencillos, that research does not support the idea that bilingual exposure causes speech or language delays, and that María José's difficulties reflect a true speech sound disorder and language delay that would likely be present regardless of language exposure. The family expressed relief hearing this and reaffirmed their wish to continue raising her bilingually.

Rutinas diarias / Daily Routines: On a typical day, María José wakes around 7:00 a.m., eats breakfast with her family (often cereal or huevos con tortilla), and is dropped off at daycare by Javier before he goes to work. At daycare she participates in circle time, outdoor play, and a nap from approximately 1:00 p.m. to 2:30 p.m.. In the evenings, the family eats dinner together, and María José enjoys bath time and bedtime stories read by Lucía, usually in Spanish. Family routines also include weekly visits to la iglesia on Sundays and occasional visits to abuela Rosa Soto Mendoza's apartment nearby.

Otras agencias involucradas / Other Agencies: The family receives nutritional support through the WIC Office of Cumberland County and recently enrolled Camila in Fayetteville Early Head Start for childcare support. Smart Start of Cumberland County has also provided the family with a Spanish-language parenting resource guide. The family has had minimal contact with Cumberland County Department of Social Services, aside from an initial WIC referral made by their pediatrician, Dr. Patricia Owens, at the time of María José's 18-month well-check.

Evaluación y diagnóstico: María José carries diagnoses of a speech sound disorder and mixed receptive-expressive language disorder (ICD-10: F80.2), confirmed at her initial evaluation on April 15, 2024 and supported by standardized assessment and ongoing progress monitoring. Her most recent speech sound inventory showed stimulable but inconsistent production of /k/, /g/, and final consonants, with spontaneous intelligibility estimated at 60% to unfamiliar listeners and closer to 85% for her parents. During structured probes this session, she produced target words containing final consonants with 8/10 accuracy (80%) when given moderate cues, an improvement from her initial baseline of 4/10 (40%).

Resultados y estrategias / Outcomes and Strategies:

Outcome 1 (Communication/Expressive Language): María José will use two- to three-word phrases in Spanish and/or English to request desired items and express needs during daily routines (mealtime, play, dressing) across home and daycare settings, with 80% accuracy as measured by parent report and clinician observation. Strategies include: modeling expansion of single words into short phrases ("quiero jugo" instead of "jugo"); use of a bilingual visual communication board at home and at daycare developed collaboratively with Ms. Holt; parent coaching in both languages during the author's weekly home visits; and encouragement of both parents to continue using their strongest language (Spanish) rather than restricting input. Progress to date: María José now spontaneously combines two words in approximately 70% of opportunities, up from 30% at the initial IFSP.

Outcome 2 (Speech Sound Production): María José will produce word-final consonants and the sounds /k/ and /g/ in single words with 80% accuracy given minimal cues, generalizing from structured drill to spontaneous speech. Strategies include: articulation drill using minimal pairs and visual/tactile cueing (e.g., touch cues for final consonant deletion); home practice sheets translated into Spanish for parent carryover; and coordination with the family to practice target sounds during bath time and mealtime, routines the family identified as natural practice opportunities. Progress to date: as noted above, María José achieved 8/10 (80%) accuracy for word-final consonants with moderate cues this session, meeting the first benchmark toward this outcome; she is not yet consistent without cueing support.

Outcome 3 (Family Support/Access to Services): The family will continue to access bilingual early intervention services and community resources to support María José's communication development and prepare for the transition to preschool services. Strategies include: continued coordination between this writer, Service Coordinator Ana Gutiérrez, and Fayetteville Early Head Start staff; a referral to Smart Start of Cumberland County's bilingual parenting workshop series beginning el 10 de julio de 2025; and preparation of transition paperwork for the local school system's Child Find process, anticipated around María José's third birthday in March 2026. The family also requested information about continuing therapy privately if IFSP services end before kindergarten entry, which this writer will provide at the next visit.

Servicios y fechas / Services and Dates: María José currently receives speech-language therapy twice weekly, 30 minutes per session, under CPT code 92507, and received a comprehensive speech sound and language re-evaluation under CPT code 92523 on May 28, 2025 in preparation for this review. Physical therapy with Mark Davis and occupational therapy with Sarah Kim continue weekly, each addressing fine and gross motor goals documented in separate sections of this IFSP. All services are authorized under record/authorization number CPTS-2025-04471 through December 1, 2025, at which point reauthorization will be requested based on continued need. The family's Medicaid coverage (ID 987654321B) and secondary insurance (member ID W123456789) were both verified as active for the coming service period as of June 2, 2025.

Next steps include a scheduled follow-up visit on el martes 1 de julio de 2025 to review progress on the final consonant goal, and the next full IFSP review is scheduled for December 3, 2025. The family can be reached at (910) 555-0147 via Service Coordinator Ana Gutiérrez, or this writer directly at (910) 555-0192 or jlowe@carolinapediatrictherapy.com with any questions prior to the next scheduled contact.

Comentarios adicionales de la familia: Before closing the meeting, Lucía added, "Gracias por explicarnos todo en los dos idiomas. Antes sentíamos que nadie entendía lo que queríamos decir sobre nuestra hija." (Thank you for explaining everything to us in both languages. Before, we felt like no one understood what we were trying to say about our daughter.) This writer noted the family's strong engagement and consistent follow-through with home strategies as a significant strength supporting María José's continued progress.

Documentación completada por: Jennifer Lowe, M.S., CCC-SLP, Carolina Pediatric Therapy Services, en nombre del equipo del IFSP, June 5, 2025.

text:
Estimada familia Carlos y Lucía:

Les escribo esta carta para compartir con ustedes el resumen de la reunión de revisión del Plan Individualizado de Servicios para la Familia (IFSP) de su hijo Emiliano Rodríguez, a quien todos en el programa llamamos cariñosamente Emi. Fue un gusto verlos a ustedes, a doña Lupe y a la pequeña Sol el 6 de octubre de 2026 en las oficinas del CDSA del Condado de Alamance, en 210 Avenida Roosevelt, Burlington, NC 27215. Gracias por llegar puntuales a las 10:00 a.m. y por traer el reporte más reciente de la guardería.

Como ustedes saben, participaron en esta reunión Miss Ana, la coordinadora de servicios de nuestro equipo del CDSA; Mr. Tom, el fisioterapeuta consultor; la maestra Carmen del Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pequeños Pasos, quien se unió por videollamada desde la guardería; y yo, Patricia Gómez, la patóloga del habla y lenguaje bilingüe de Terapias Pediátricas Carolina que atiende a Emi desde hace ocho meses. También estuvo presente el intérprete Jorge Martínez, quien ayudó a asegurarnos de que toda la conversación fuera clara tanto en inglés como en español.

**Información de la familia**

Emi nació el 14 de febrero de 2024 en el Hospital Regional Alamance, y ahora tiene 2 años 8 meses (edad cronológica 2;8). Vive con ustedes, su mamá Lucía Rodríguez y su papá Carlos Rodríguez, su hermanita Sol, de 6 años, y su abuela doña Lupe, quien lo cuida algunas tardes mientras ustedes trabajan. El perrito de la familia, Max, también vive en casa y, según nos contaron, es uno de los motivadores favoritos de Emi durante las actividades de juego.

La familia está inscrita en WIC a través de la oficina local, y recientemente Sol comenzó el programa de Early Head Start mientras que Emi continúa en el Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pequeños Pasos. Ustedes mencionaron que también han estado en contacto con el Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Alamance (DSS) para solicitar asistencia de cuidado infantil, y con Smart Start de Alamance para obtener información sobre programas de alfabetización familiar. Es un placer para nuestro equipo coordinar con estas agencias para apoyar a toda la familia.

**Las preocupaciones y prioridades de la familia, en sus propias palabras**

Durante la reunión, ustedes compartieron lo siguiente, y quisimos anotarlo con sus propias palabras porque es lo que guía nuestro trabajo:

"Lo que más nos preocupa es que Emi no dice casi ninguna palabra clara todavía. En la casa lo entendemos porque conocemos sus señas, pero cuando estamos en la tienda o con otras personas, él se frustra mucho porque nadie le entiende."

También dijeron: "Queremos que Emi pueda jugar con otros niños en la guardería sin ponerse a llorar de frustración. La maestra Carmen nos dice que él quiere participar, pero no puede decir lo que necesita."

Y doña Lupe agregó, con una sonrisa: "A mí me da gusto cuidarlo, pero también quisiera aprender mejor cómo ayudarlo a hablar, porque paso muchas horas con él."

Estas prioridades —comunicación funcional, reducción de la frustración, y herramientas para que toda la familia, incluyendo a doña Lupe, puedan apoyar a Emi— son el centro de los resultados que escribimos a continuación.

**Rutinas diarias**

Emi pasa de lunes a viernes, de las 8:00 a.m. a las 4:30 p.m., en el Centro de Cuidado Infantil Pequeños Pasos, donde la maestra Carmen reporta que juega bien en paralelo con otros niños del salón, aunque rara vez inicia interacción verbal. En las tardes, cuando Lucía trabaja en el turno vespertino en el Walmart de Burlington, doña Lupe lo recoge y pasan la tarde en casa, generalmente jugando con bloques, viendo videos cortos en español y jugando con Max en el patio. Carlos trabaja en Industrias Textiles Piedmont y llega a casa alrededor de las 6:00 p.m., momento en el que suele hacer la rutina de baño y cuento con Emi y con Sol.

La hora de la comida es un momento clave: Emi come bien, pero cuando quiere más agua o más comida, generalmente señala o jala la ropa de un adulto en lugar de usar palabras. Durante el juego con Sol, ella a menudo habla por él, anticipando lo que quiere, lo cual, aunque bien intencionado, ha reducido las oportunidades de que Emi practique sus propias palabras.

**Resumen de la evaluación**

Como parte de esta revisión, administré la Preschool Language Scale-5 (PLS-5) en su versión en español, además de una muestra de lenguaje espontáneo grabada durante el juego con bloques y animales de granja. Los resultados de la subprueba de Comunicación Expresiva arrojaron una puntuación estándar de 70 (percentil 2), consistente con un retraso significativo del lenguaje expresivo en comparación con su edad cronológica de 2;8. La Comunicación Receptiva estuvo dentro de límites bajos-normales, con una puntuación estándar de 85 (percentil 16).

En la muestra de habla, Emi produjo once palabras diferentes de forma espontánea, incluyendo aproximaciones como "upa" por "arriba", "aba" por "agua", y "tete" por "leche". Notamos procesos fonológicos típicos de su edad, como la reducción de grupos consonánticos y la sustitución de /k/ por [t] en palabras como "casa", producida como [tasa]. En una tarea de imitación estructurada de 10 ítems, Emi logró producir correctamente 8/10 palabras objetivo con claves moderadas (mod cues), es decir, un 80% de precisión, lo cual indica buena capacidad de imitación cuando se le da apoyo. En la transcripción codificamos dos instancias como [EW] (palabra ininteligible) donde no pudimos determinar la intención comunicativa con certeza.

Con base en estos hallazgos, y en consulta con el equipo, el diagnóstico que mejor describe el perfil actual de Emi corresponde al código ICD-10 F80.2 (trastorno mixto del lenguaje receptivo-expresivo). Los servicios de terapia del habla y lenguaje se facturan bajo los códigos CPT 92507 (tratamiento individual del habla, lenguaje, voz y/o audición) y 92523 (evaluación del habla, fonología y lenguaje), según corresponda a cada sesión.

**Resultados del IFSP y estrategias**

Basado en las prioridades que ustedes compartieron, el equipo, junto con ustedes, acordó los siguientes tres resultados:

Resultado 1: Emi usará al menos 25 palabras diferentes de forma espontánea, de forma consistente, en casa y en la guardería, para pedir, comentar y protestar, para la próxima revisión del IFSP.
Estrategias: Durante las comidas y el juego, los adultos (incluyendo a doña Lupe y a la maestra Carmen) harán pausas de espera de 5 segundos antes de anticipar lo que Emi quiere, dándole la oportunidad de intentar comunicarse primero. Pedimos a Sol que, en lugar de hablar por su hermanito, le haga preguntas sencillas como "¿qué quieres?" y espere su respuesta.

Resultado 2: Emi participará en juego interactivo con un compañero en la guardería durante al menos 5 minutos sin llorar de frustración, en 8 de 10 oportunidades observadas.
Estrategias: La maestra Carmen usará tarjetas visuales sencillas durante el juego grupal para que Emi pueda señalar lo que quiere mientras desarrolla su vocabulario verbal. Yo continuaré visitando la guardería mensualmente para modelar estas estrategias directamente con ella y con los demás niños del salón.

Resultado 3: La familia, incluyendo a doña Lupe, se sentirá segura usando al menos tres estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje en casa, reportado mediante una escala de confianza familiar.
Estrategias: Continuaré las sesiones quincenales en el hogar para modelar las técnicas de expansión de lenguaje (por ejemplo, si Emi dice "aba", el adulto responde "sí, quieres agua") y dejaré hojas de práctica en español para doña Lupe y para ustedes.

**Otras agencias involucradas**

Además de los servicios de terapia del habla y lenguaje a través del CDSA, el equipo coordinará con las siguientes agencias para apoyar a la familia de manera integral: WIC, para continuar el apoyo nutricional; el Departamento de Servicios Sociales del Condado de Alamance (DSS), respecto a la solicitud de asistencia de cuidado infantil; Smart Start de Alamance, para el programa de alfabetización familiar en el que ustedes expresaron interés; y Early Head Start, donde Sol está actualmente inscrita y que también ofrece recursos para familias con niños pequeños en servicios de intervención temprana. Miss Ana, como coordinadora de servicios, se mantendrá en contacto con cada una de estas agencias y servirá como su punto de contacto principal si tienen preguntas sobre cualquiera de estos servicios.

**Fechas de servicio**

Los servicios de terapia del habla y lenguaje de Emi continuarán de la siguiente manera a partir de este IFSP:

- Terapia individual del habla y lenguaje (CPT 92507): dos sesiones de 45 minutos por semana, los martes y jueves a las 2:00 p.m., en el hogar de la familia.
- Consulta de fisioterapia con Mr. Tom: una visita mensual de 30 minutos para monitorear el desarrollo motor grueso, sin preocupaciones actuales.
- Visita de coordinación de servicios con Miss Ana: cada 90 días, o según sea necesario.

La próxima revisión del IFSP está programada para el 6 de abril de 2027, aunque podemos adelantarla si ustedes lo solicitan o si observamos cambios significativos en el progreso de Emi.

**Información de contacto y del expediente**

Para cualquier pregunta sobre este resumen o sobre los servicios de Emi, pueden comunicarse con Miss Ana al teléfono (336) 555-0148 o al correo electrónico ana.coordinadora@cdsaalamance.org. El número de expediente de Emi en el sistema del CDSA es CDSA-2024-04471, y su número de Medicaid es 998271563A. Por favor, tengan ambos números a la mano si llaman para hacer alguna pregunta sobre facturación o servicios.

Quiero agradecerles sinceramente su compromiso y dedicación con el progreso de Emi. Es evidente, en cada sesión, cuánto cariño y esfuerzo pone toda la familia —ustedes dos, doña Lupe y hasta Sol— en ayudarlo a comunicarse. Estamos muy contentos con el progreso que ha logrado desde la última revisión, y confiamos en que, con las estrategias acordadas, seguirá avanzando.

Con cariño y respeto,

Patricia Gómez, M.S., CCC-SLP
Patóloga del Habla y Lenguaje Bilingüe
Terapias Pediátricas Carolina
En colaboración con el CDSA del Condado de Alamance

INFORME DE EVALUACIÓN DEL HABLA Y DEL LENGUAJE

Agencia Remitente:  Agencia de Servicios de Desarrollo Infantil del Condado de Chatham (CDSA Piedmont)
Clínica/Proveedor:  Clínica de Terapia del Habla Piedmont Carolina, PLLC
Correo Electrónico de la Clínica:  recepcion@piedmontcarolinaslp.com
Sitio Web de la Clínica:  www.piedmontcarolinaslp.com
Teléfono de la Clínica:  (919) 555-0142
Patóloga del Habla-Lenguaje:  Maria Elena Castillo, M.S., CCC-SLP
Coordinadora de Servicios (CDSA):  Yesenia Portillo
Fecha de la Evaluación:  14 de septiembre de 2026
Fecha del Informe:  21 de septiembre de 2026

Nombre del Niño:  Jesús Alberto Ramírez Flores (conocido en casa como "Chuy")
Fecha de Nacimiento:  3 de mayo de 2022
Edad Cronológica:  4;4
Sexo:  Masculino
Idioma Primario del Hogar:  Español
Número de ITP de Carolina del Norte:  NC-ITP-00481723
Número de Caso de CDSA:  CDSA-CH-2026-0319
Número de Identificación de Medicaid:  987654321A
Aseguradora/Plan:  WellCare Carolina Complete Health
Número de Miembro del Seguro:  WCC-55290134
Número de Autorización:  AUTH-2026-77410
Dirección:  412 Calle Hickory, Siler City, Condado de Chatham, 27344
Teléfono del Hogar:  (336) 555-0198

Nombre de la Madre:  Lucía Fernanda Flores Hernández
Nombre del Padre:  Roberto Ramírez Soto
Hermanos en el Hogar:  Guadalupe Ramírez Flores ("Lupita"), 7 años; Juan Pablo Ramírez Flores ("Juanito"), 2 años
Cuidadora Principal Durante el Día:  Carmen Soto viuda de Ramírez (abuela paterna)
Escuela/Centro de Cuidado:  Centro de Desarrollo Infantil Pequeños Pasos
Maestra:  Brenda Collazo

I. MOTIVO DE REFERENCIA

Chuy fue remitido para una evaluación integral de habla y lenguaje por su pediatra, el Dr. Nelson Abreu, del Hospital Regional Chatham Memorial, debido a preocupación sobre un retraso significativo en la producción de sonidos del habla y en la longitud de sus enunciados. La familia fue referida inicialmente a través de CDSA Piedmont después de que la trabajadora social de WIC del Condado de Chatham notara que el niño usaba muy pocas palabras durante una visita de rutina. La evaluación de hoy se realizó en el hogar de la familia con el consentimiento informado de la madre, Lucía Fernanda Flores Hernández, y en presencia de la abuela paterna, Carmen Soto viuda de Ramírez. Toda la evaluación se condujo en español, el idioma dominante y preferido del hogar.

II. HISTORIA PRENATAL, PERINATAL Y MÉDICA

Según el reporte materno, el embarazo de Jesús fue de término completo, sin complicaciones mayores, aunque la madre informa haber tenido presión arterial elevada durante el tercer trimestre, controlada sin medicación. El parto fue vaginal, en el Hospital Regional Chatham Memorial, el 3 de mayo de 2022, con un peso al nacer de 7 libras 4 onzas. No se reportaron complicaciones neonatales ni estancia prolongada en la unidad de cuidados intensivos neonatales.

La historia médica de Chuy incluye otitis media recurrente, con al menos cinco episodios documentados entre los 8 y los 30 meses de edad, tratados con amoxicilina en múltiples ocasiones. Fue evaluado por el otorrinolaringólogo pediátrico, el Dr. Felipe Ordóñez, en el Centro Médico Pediátrico Triángulo el 12 de enero de 2025, quien recomendó la colocación de tubos de ventilación bilaterales debido a derrame persistente en ambos oídos. El procedimiento se realizó el 28 de febrero de 2025 sin complicaciones. Una audiometría posterior realizada por la audióloga Marisol Treviño el 15 de marzo de 2025 indicó audición dentro de límites normales en ambos oídos.

No se reportan convulsiones, hospitalizaciones adicionales, cirugías, ni diagnósticos genéticos conocidos. La madre niega exposición prenatal a alcohol, tabaco o drogas. Chuy no toma medicamentos actualmente. La visión fue evaluada como normal en su examen físico anual más reciente, realizado por el Dr. Nelson Abreu el 2 de junio de 2026.

III. HISTORIA DEL DESARROLLO

Según la madre, los hitos motores gruesos y finos de Chuy se alcanzaron dentro de los rangos esperados: se sentó sin apoyo a los 6 meses, caminó de forma independiente a los 13 meses, y actualmente sube y baja escaleras alternando los pies. Sin embargo, el desarrollo del lenguaje se describe como notablemente más lento que el de sus hermanos a la misma edad. La madre reporta que sus primeras palabras aproximadas aparecieron alrededor de los 22 meses, mucho más tarde que las de su hermana Lupita, quien hablaba en frases completas antes de los 2 años.

IV. HISTORIA FAMILIAR Y DEL LENGUAJE

La familia reside en una vivienda multigeneracional en Siler City, compartida con la abuela paterna, Carmen Soto viuda de Ramírez. El español es el idioma exclusivo del hogar; Chuy tiene exposición mínima al inglés fuera del centro de cuidado infantil. La madre, Lucía Fernanda Flores Hernández, trabaja de noche en el Hogar de Ancianos Pinares Dorados como asistente certificada de enfermería, un horario que limita su disponibilidad durante las mañanas. Mamá trabaja de noche en el hogar de ancianos, por lo que la abuela Carmen asume la mayoría de las responsabilidades de cuidado diurno, incluyendo llevar y recoger a Chuy del Centro de Desarrollo Infantil Pequeños Pasos.

El padre, Roberto Ramírez Soto, trabaja tiempo completo en la Procesadora de Aves Valle Verde, con turnos rotativos que a veces incluyen fines de semana. La familia reporta estrés financiero moderado relacionado con los gastos médicos recientes de los tubos de oído y el cuidado de los tres niños.

La historia familiar es positiva para retraso del habla: el hermano del padre, Pepe Soto (tío paterno de Chuy), recibió terapia de lenguaje durante la niñez. No se reporta historia familiar de trastornos del espectro autista, pérdida auditiva permanente, ni discapacidad intelectual.

En el hogar también vive la mascota familiar, un perro llamado Canela, con quien Chuy interactúa frecuentemente y hacia quien dirige algunas de sus pocas palabras espontáneas en español.

Chuy asiste al Centro de Desarrollo Infantil Pequeños Pasos cinco días a la semana, donde su maestra, Brenda Collazo, reporta que el niño se comunica principalmente mediante gestos, señalando y sonidos aislados, y que con frecuencia se frustra cuando sus compañeros, incluyendo a Esteban y Marisela, no entienden lo que intenta comunicar. La maestra Collazo también observa que Chuy prefiere el juego paralelo sobre la interacción directa con sus compañeros durante el tiempo libre.

V. OBSERVACIONES CONDUCTUALES DURANTE LA EVALUACIÓN

Chuy se presentó como un niño activo, curioso y generalmente cooperador durante la sesión de evaluación, aunque mostró periodos breves de resistencia cuando las tareas requerían respuestas verbales repetidas. Estableció contacto visual apropiado, respondió a su nombre de manera consistente, y demostró atención conjunta funcional con la examinadora y con su abuela, Carmen. El juego simbólico fue apropiado para la edad; Chuy alimentó a un muñeco y simuló hablar por teléfono durante el juego libre.

Las habilidades de alimentación no mostraron preocupaciones reportadas por la familia; no hay historia de dificultades de succión, masticación o deglución.

VI. EVALUACIÓN DE HABLA Y LENGUAJE

Se administraron las siguientes pruebas estandarizadas en español, además de observación directa del lenguaje espontáneo y una muestra de habla conectada obtenida durante el juego con la abuela.

Preschool Language Scale-5, Edición en Español (PLS-5 Spanish):
Puntuación Estándar de Comunicación Auditiva: 72 (percentil 3)
Puntuación Estándar de Comunicación Expresiva: 65 (percentil 1)
Puntuación Compuesta de Lenguaje Total: 67 (percentil 1)

Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation-3 (GFTA-3), adaptado al español:
Puntuación Estándar: 71 (percentil 3)
Porcentaje de Consonantes Correctas (PCC): 58%

Rossetti Infant-Toddler Language Scale (administrado como medida complementaria dada la discrepancia severa entre comprensión y expresión):
Nivel funcional estimado: equivalente a 24-28 meses en el dominio expresivo

Muestra de Lenguaje Espontáneo (Longitud Media del Enunciado):
LME en morfemas: 1.8 (significativamente por debajo de lo esperado para 4;4)

Tabla de Resultados Resumida:

Prueba                          Puntuación Estándar      Percentil
PLS-5 Auditivo                  72                        3
PLS-5 Expresivo                 65                        1
PLS-5 Total                     67                        1
GFTA-3                          71                        3

Durante la muestra de habla espontánea, Chuy produjo principalmente enunciados de una sola palabra, con ocasionales combinaciones de dos palabras ("mamá agua", "no quiero"). Se observaron los siguientes patrones fonológicos: procesos de reducción de grupos consonánticos consistentes (por ejemplo, "pato" por "plato"), frontalización de velares (produciendo "teto" por "queso"), y omisión final de consonantes. El fonema /r/ estuvo ausente en todas las posiciones intentadas, y el niño sustituyó consistentemente [w] por /l/ en palabras como "lupa", producida como "wupa". Las producciones de Chuy fueron, en general, ininteligibles para oyentes no familiarizados, con una inteligibilidad estimada del 30% en contexto conocido y menor en contexto desconocido.

Durante una tarea de denominación de imágenes, Chuy identificó correctamente 12 de 20 ítems (60%) mediante señalamiento, pero pudo nombrar verbalmente solo 5 de 20 (25%), lo cual refuerza la discrepancia marcada entre el lenguaje receptivo relativamente más fuerte y el lenguaje expresivo severamente limitado.

La comprensión de instrucciones de dos pasos fue inconsistente, logrando 6/10 en tareas estructuradas con apoyo contextual y gestual. El seguimiento de instrucciones de un solo paso sin apoyo contextual fue de 8/10.

VII. RESUMEN DE HALLAZGOS

Los resultados de esta evaluación indican un Trastorno del Lenguaje Expresivo de severidad moderada a severa, con afectación fonológica concomitante, en un niño bilingüe potencial cuyo idioma dominante actual es el español. La discrepancia entre las habilidades receptivas y expresivas es clínicamente significativa y consistente con un perfil de retraso específico del lenguaje más que con una diferencia dialectal o de exposición bilingüe normal, dado que Chuy tiene exposición mínima al inglés y, por lo tanto, no se esperaría que la adquisición del español estuviera limitada por un proceso típico de desarrollo bilingüe. La historia de otitis media recurrente pudo haber contribuido parcialmente al retraso, aunque la resolución auditiva documentada y la persistencia de las dificultades expresivas sugieren un componente de base del lenguaje independiente de la historia otológica.

VIII. IMPRESIONES CLÍNICAS

1. Trastorno del Lenguaje Expresivo, moderado a severo (código CIE-10: F80.1), basado en puntuaciones estándar significativamente por debajo de la media en las subpruebas expresivas del PLS-5 Spanish y en la muestra de lenguaje espontáneo.
2. Trastorno Fonológico concomitante, caracterizado por procesos de reducción de grupos consonánticos, frontalización de velares, y omisión final de consonantes, afectando la inteligibilidad general del habla.
3. Historia de otitis media recurrente con resolución documentada tras colocación de tubos de ventilación; sin evidencia actual de pérdida auditiva.
4. No se identifican banderas rojas conductuales consistentes con trastorno del espectro autista en el contexto de esta evaluación; sin embargo, se recomienda monitoreo continuo del desarrollo social dado el patrón de juego paralelo reportado por la maestra.

IX. RECOMENDACIONES

1. Se recomienda que Chuy reciba terapia de habla y lenguaje individual, en español, con una frecuencia de dos a tres sesiones por semana, enfocada en la expansión del vocabulario expresivo, la combinación de palabras, y la intervención fonológica dirigida a los patrones identificados.
2. Se recomienda continuar el seguimiento a través de CDSA Piedmont para la elaboración o actualización del Plan Individualizado de Servicios Familiares (IFSP, por sus siglas en inglés), con revisión programada para 15 de diciembre de 2026.
3. Se recomienda coordinación de servicios entre esta clínica, el Centro de Desarrollo Infantil Pequeños Pasos, y la familia para asegurar consistencia en las estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje en todos los entornos del niño.
4. Se recomienda educación familiar continua sobre estrategias de estimulación del lenguaje en el hogar, con instrucciones específicas para la abuela, Carmen Soto viuda de Ramírez, dado su rol como cuidadora primaria durante el día, y para la madre, Lucía Fernanda Flores Hernández, durante las horas en que esté disponible.
5. Se recomienda reevaluación audiológica anual dada la historia de otitis media recurrente, con seguimiento a través del Dr. Felipe Ordóñez según sea necesario.
6. Se recomienda que la familia contacte a la coordinadora de servicios, Yesenia Portillo, al teléfono (919) 555-0276 para coordinar los próximos pasos del proceso de elegibilidad y autorización de servicios continuos.
7. Dado el estrés financiero reportado por la familia, se recomienda explorar recursos adicionales de apoyo a través de Smart Start del Condado de Chatham, incluyendo posible asistencia con transporte a las sesiones de terapia.

X. PLAN DE SEGUIMIENTO

Se programará una sesión de planificación de tratamiento con la familia el 28 de septiembre de 2026 para iniciar formalmente los servicios de terapia de habla y lenguaje. La intérprete certificada, Alondra Jiménez, estará disponible según sea necesario para facilitar la comunicación durante las sesiones de planificación con el equipo interdisciplinario, aunque dado que toda la evaluación y la intervención se conducirán en español, se anticipa que el apoyo de interpretación sea mínimo.

Este informe se comparte con el consentimiento de la familia con CDSA Piedmont, el pediatra Dr. Nelson Abreu, y el Centro de Desarrollo Infantil Pequeños Pasos para apoyar la planificación integral de servicios.

PLAN DE SERVICIO FAMILIAR INDIVIDUALIZADO (IFSP) — INDIVIDUALIZED FAMILY SERVICE PLAN
North Carolina Infant-Toddler Program / Programa para Infantes y Niños Pequeños de Carolina del Norte
IFSP REVIEW REPORT

1. IDENTIFYING INFORMATION / INFORMACIÓN DE IDENTIFICACIÓN

Child's Name / Nombre del niño: Mateo Alejandro Flores Ramírez (called Teo at home)

Mother/Madre: Lucía Rodríguez Flores, 29 años, works part-time at Belk Department Store in Asheboro.

CDSA Office: Catawba Valley CDSA, 118 Fairview Street, Asheboro, 27203

Speech-Language Pathologist / Patóloga del Habla-Lenguaje: Jennifer Hayes, M.S., CCC-SLP, bilingual clinician, Carolina Pediatric Therapy Partners, PLLC
